Who Was John Drakeford?
John Drakeford Alikuwa Nani?

John W. Drakeford (1914–1996) was an Australian-born Baptist pastor, psychologist, and seminary professor who devoted his life to training Christian counselors. He served for many years as Professor of Psychology and Counseling at Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary in Fort Worth, Texas, where he also directed the Marriage and Family Counseling Center. Drakeford was not primarily a clinician working with patients behind closed doors; he was a teacher of pastors, training men and women who would carry his methods into local churches and ordinary congregations all over the world.

John W. Drakeford (1914–1996) alikuwa mchungaji wa Kibaptisti mzaliwa wa Australia, mwanasaikolojia, na profesa wa seminari aliyetoa maisha yake kuwafunza washauri Wakristo. Alihudumu kwa miaka mingi kama Profesa wa Saikolojia na Ushauri katika Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary huko Fort Worth, Texas, ambako pia aliongoza Kituo cha Ushauri wa Ndoa na Familia. Drakeford hakuwa hasa mtaalamu wa tiba aliyefanya kazi na wagonjwa nyuma ya milango iliyofungwa; alikuwa mwalimu wa wachungaji, akiwafunza wanaume na wanawake ambao wangezipeleka mbinu zake katika makanisa ya mahali na makusanyiko ya kawaida duniani kote.

Drakeford wrote prolifically, with books that bridged the academic counseling literature and the practical needs of the pastor in his study. Among his best-known works are Counseling for Church Leaders, People to People Therapy, Integrity Therapy, and The Awesome Power of the Listening Ear. He worked closely with O. Hobart Mowrer, whose Integrity Therapy framework — emphasizing honest confession of real moral failure as the path to wholeness — deeply shaped Drakeford's own thinking. Where many mid-twentieth-century counselors treated moral failure as illness, Drakeford insisted that moral failure was moral failure, and that the gospel had a far better answer to it than the therapeutic culture did.

Drakeford aliandika vitabu vingi sana, vitabu vilivyounganisha maandiko ya kitaaluma ya ushauri na mahitaji ya kivitendo ya mchungaji katika chumba chake cha kujifunzia. Miongoni mwa kazi zake zinazojulikana zaidi ni Counseling for Church Leaders (Ushauri kwa Viongozi wa Kanisa), People to People Therapy (Tiba ya Mtu kwa Mtu), Integrity Therapy (Tiba ya Uadilifu), na The Awesome Power of the Listening Ear (Nguvu ya Ajabu ya Sikio Linalosikiliza). Alifanya kazi kwa karibu na O. Hobart Mowrer, ambaye mfumo wake wa Tiba ya Uadilifu — unaosisitiza kuungama kwa uaminifu kushindwa halisi kwa kimaadili kuwa njia ya kuelekea uzima kamili — uliunda kwa kina fikra za Drakeford mwenyewe. Pale ambapo washauri wengi wa katikati ya karne ya ishirini walikuchukulia kushindwa kwa kimaadili kuwa ugonjwa, Drakeford alisisitiza kwamba kushindwa kwa kimaadili ni kushindwa kwa kimaadili, na kwamba injili ina jibu bora zaidi sana kwa jambo hilo kuliko utamaduni wa kitiba.

Drakeford's reputation was built on his capacity to take dense psychological literature and turn it into something a pastor with no clinical training could actually use on a Tuesday afternoon when a couple walked into his office in crisis. He listened seriously to Freud, Rogers, Skinner, Berne, and the biblical counseling pioneers of his own generation. He kept what served the pastor's work; he set aside what conflicted with Scripture; and he built a method ordinary pastors could learn and practice.

Sifa ya Drakeford ilijengwa juu ya uwezo wake wa kuchukua maandiko mazito ya saikolojia na kuyageuza kuwa kitu ambacho mchungaji asiye na mafunzo ya kitabibu angeweza kweli kukitumia Jumanne alasiri wakati wanandoa walio katika dharura wanapoingia ofisini kwake. Aliwasikiliza kwa makini Freud, Rogers, Skinner, Berne, na waanzilishi wa ushauri wa kibiblia wa kizazi chake. Alishika kile kilichosaidia kazi ya mchungaji; aliweka kando kile kilichopingana na Maandiko; na akajenga mbinu ambayo wachungaji wa kawaida wangeweza kujifunza na kuitumia.
The Ten-Step Model
Mbinu ya Hatua Kumi

Drakeford's distinctive contribution to pastoral counseling is the clear, teachable structure presented in this course. Ten steps walk the counselor from the very first moment of an encounter — establishing time and place — through listening, clarification, investigation of previous counseling, the assignment of responsibility, the modeling of right behavior, the review of alternatives, the exploration of likely outcomes, the supplying of needed information, and finally to provided closure. The steps are not a mechanical script; they are a disciplined sequence that orders the counselor's instincts and protects both counselor and counselee from the most common pastoral errors — speaking too soon, confronting before listening, lecturing before understanding, and leaving the counselee without concrete action.

Mchango wa pekee wa Drakeford katika ushauri wa kichungaji ni muundo ulio wazi na unaoweza kufundishwa unaowasilishwa katika kozi hii. Hatua kumi zinamwongoza mshauri tangu dakika ya kwanza kabisa ya kukutana — kuamua muda na mahali — kupitia kusikiliza, kufafanua hali, kuchunguza ushauri uliotangulia, kuweka uwajibikaji, kuonyesha mfano wa mwenendo sahihi, kupitia njia mbadala, kuchunguza matokeo yanayotarajiwa, kutoa taarifa inayohitajika, na hatimaye kuhitimisha. Hatua hizi si maandishi ya kufuata kimashine; ni mfuatano wenye nidhamu unaopanga silika za mshauri na kumlinda mshauri na mshauriwa dhidi ya makosa ya kichungaji yanayotokea mara nyingi zaidi — kusema mapema mno, kukabili kabla ya kusikiliza, kuhubiri kabla ya kuelewa, na kumwacha mshauriwa bila hatua halisi ya kuchukua.

Each step is a unit in this course. Each unit contains a teaching block, scriptural grounding, and an assessment that tests whether you have learned the material. Pastors trained in these ten steps have helped many thousands of people through marital trouble, family crisis, grief, vocational confusion, moral failure, addiction, and the ordinary discouragements of life. The model is durable. It is also bounded — Drakeford himself was clear that some problems require referral to specialists, and this course teaches that boundary too.

Kila hatua ni sehemu moja katika kozi hii. Kila sehemu ina somo la kufundisha, msingi wa kimaandiko, na tathmini inayopima kama umejifunza somo hilo. Wachungaji waliofunzwa hatua hizi kumi wamewasaidia maelfu mengi ya watu kupitia matatizo ya ndoa, migogoro ya familia, huzuni ya msiba, kuchanganyikiwa kuhusu kazi au wito, kushindwa kwa kimaadili, uraibu, na makatisho tamaa ya kawaida ya maisha. Mbinu hii ni ya kudumu. Pia ina mipaka — Drakeford mwenyewe alieleza wazi kwamba matatizo mengine yanahitaji mtu kupelekwa kwa wataalamu, na kozi hii inafundisha mpaka huo pia.
How the Course Is Organized
Jinsi Kozi Ilivyopangwa

The course contains eleven units. The Foundation Unit is a module that sets Drakeford within the wider landscape of twentieth-century counseling so that you will know not only what the ten steps prescribe but why. Steps One through Ten present Drakeford's model in order, with each unit building on the preceding ones. The steps are designed to be learned in sequence; the work of Step Five is impossible without the listening discipline of Step Two, and the closure of Step Ten cannot be supplied unless the work of Steps One through Nine has actually been done.

Kozi ina sehemu kumi na moja. Sehemu ya Msingi ni moduli inayomweka Drakeford ndani ya mandhari pana ya ushauri wa karne ya ishirini ili ujue si tu nini hatua kumi zinaelekeza bali pia kwa nini. Hatua ya Kwanza hadi Hatua ya Kumi zinawasilisha mbinu ya Drakeford kwa mpangilio, kila sehemu ikijengwa juu ya zile zilizotangulia. Hatua hizi zimekusudiwa kujifunzwa kwa mfuatano; kazi ya Hatua ya Tano haiwezekani bila nidhamu ya kusikiliza ya Hatua ya Pili, na kuhitimisha kwa Hatua ya Kumi hakuwezi kufanyika isipokuwa kazi ya Hatua ya Kwanza hadi ya Tisa imefanyika kweli.

Each unit has the same structure. A teaching block presents Drakeford's material with biblical and theological reflection. Scripture is cited from the Authorized (King James) Version in English and from the Reina-Valera Revisada 1960 in Spanish. After the teaching block comes an assessment. Certificate of Ministry students complete twenty multiple-choice questions per unit, with immediate feedback on each answer. Associate of Divinity students complete the same twenty multiple-choice questions; they also answer ten fill-in-the-blank questions per unit and need nine of them right. Certificate students may try the fill-in-the-blank questions for review; they do not count. Master of Theology and Master of Divinity students complete the same twenty multiple-choice questions plus ten short-answer items in which they must demonstrate working command of key concepts in their own words. Both sections require ninety percent to pass. Upon completion of all eleven units (and, on the M.Div. and Th.M. tracks, the textbook test), students receive a Certificate of Completion from Chapala Theological Seminary.

Maandiko yamenukuliwa kutoka Authorized (King James) Version kwa Kiingereza, kutoka Reina-Valera Revisada 1960 kwa Kihispania, na kutoka Biblia Takatifu (SUV) kwa Kiswahili. A word about what this course is not. It is not a replacement for clinical training, and it does not credential anyone to treat psychiatric conditions, addictions in their acute phase, or the consequences of serious abuse without the involvement of qualified specialists. It is a thorough preparation for the pastoral counseling that happens in the ordinary life of the local church — and that work, properly done, is some of the most important work any pastor will ever do.

The Landscape of Counseling — Where Drakeford Stands
Mandhari ya Ushauri — Drakeford Anasimama Wapi
Five streams shaped twentieth-century counseling. The pastor who knows them recognizes what he is hearing, knows what to keep, and knows why Drakeford's path is what it is.
Mikondo mitano iliunda ushauri wa karne ya ishirini. Mchungaji anayeijua anatambua kile anachokisikia, anajua cha kushika, na anajua kwa nini njia ya Drakeford iko jinsi ilivyo.
"Where there is no counsel, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety."Proverbs 11:14 (KJV)
"Pasipo mashauri taifa huanguka; Bali kwa wingi wa washauri huja wokovu."<cite>Mithali 11:14 (SUV)</cite>

Every counseling method has roots. Drakeford did not invent his ten steps in a vacuum. He sat at the intersection of five major streams that have shaped twentieth-century counseling, and he absorbed from each while rejecting elements of each. The pastor who understands this landscape will recognize what he is hearing when a counselee says, "My last therapist said…" or when he picks up a book at a conference. He will know what to keep, what to set down, and why Drakeford's path is what it is.

Kila mbinu ya ushauri ina mizizi. Drakeford hakubuni hatua zake kumi mahali patupu. Alikaa kwenye makutano ya mikondo mitano mikuu iliyounda ushauri wa karne ya ishirini, naye alichota kutoka kwa kila mmoja huku akikataa baadhi ya vipengele vya kila mmoja. Mchungaji anayeielewa mandhari hii atatambua kile anachokisikia mshauriwa anaposema, "Mtaalamu wangu wa tiba wa mwisho alisema…" au anapochukua kitabu kwenye mkutano. Atajua cha kushika, cha kuweka chini, na kwa nini njia ya Drakeford iko jinsi ilivyo.

Five streams matter most: psychoanalysis (Freud), client-centered therapy (Rogers), behaviorism (Skinner), transactional analysis (Berne), and nouthetic counseling (Adams). Each one names something real about the human person. None of them, by itself, is the whole picture.

Mikondo mitano ndiyo muhimu zaidi: uchanganuzi wa nafsi (Freud), tiba inayomlenga mteja (Rogers), nadharia ya tabia (Skinner), uchambuzi wa miamala (Berne), na ushauri wa kinouthetiki (Adams). Kila mmoja unataja jambo halisi kuhusu nafsi ya mwanadamu. Hakuna hata mmoja wao, peke yake, unaotoa picha nzima.
0.1 Psychoanalysis — The Buried Past (Freud)
0.1 Uchanganuzi wa Nafsi — Yaliyopita Yaliyozikwa (Freud)

Sigmund Freud (1856–1939) is the father of modern psychotherapy. From a Vienna consulting room he developed the system that would dominate Western counseling for half a century, and against which most of what followed was a reaction.

Sigmund Freud (1856–1939) ni baba wa tiba ya kisaikolojia ya kisasa. Kutoka chumba cha mashauriano huko Vienna aliunda mfumo ambao ungetawala ushauri wa nchi za Magharibi kwa nusu karne, na ambao sehemu kubwa ya yaliyofuata ilikuwa ni kuupinga.

Freud's key insight is that the past is alive. Childhood experiences — especially those involving the parents, sexuality, and unmet desire — leave residues in the unconscious mind. These residues do not lie quietly. They surface as anxiety, depression, compulsion, dreams, slips of the tongue, and unexplained symptoms. The counselee does not know why he behaves as he does because the cause is hidden from him.

Ufahamu mkuu wa Freud ni kwamba yaliyopita yako hai. Mambo yaliyompata mtu utotoni — hasa yale yanayohusu wazazi, jinsia, na tamaa zisizotimizwa — huacha mabaki katika akili isiyo ya fahamu. Mabaki hayo hayakai kimya. Hujitokeza kama wasiwasi, sonona, msukumo wa kulazimika kutenda, ndoto, kuteleza kwa ulimi, na dalili zisizoelezeka. Mshauriwa hajui kwa nini anatenda jinsi anavyotenda kwa sababu chanzo kimefichwa kwake.

The method follows the diagnosis. The analyst sits behind the patient on the couch and lets the patient free-associate — say whatever comes to mind without filter. Over many years, the buried material surfaces; the analyst interprets it; insight slowly accomplishes the cure. The doctrine is sometimes called insight therapy: if you know why you do what you do, you will stop doing it.

Mbinu inafuata utambuzi. Mchanganuzi huketi nyuma ya mgonjwa aliyelala kitandani na kumwacha mgonjwa ahusishe mawazo kwa uhuru (free association) — aseme lolote linalomjia akilini bila kuchuja. Kwa miaka mingi, mambo yaliyozikwa hujitokeza; mchanganuzi huyatafsiri; ufahamu polepole huleta uponyaji. Fundisho hili wakati mwingine huitwa tiba ya ufahamu (insight therapy): ukijua kwa nini unafanya unachofanya, utaacha kukifanya.

Freud's weakness is grave. He treats moral failure as illness. The man who lies, who is unfaithful, who steals, has not sinned — he is sick, driven by forces he cannot help. Treatment is medical, not moral. The cross of Christ has no role; the language of guilt is itself the symptom to be dissolved. O. Hobart Mowrer (whom we will meet under Integrity Therapy) spent his career arguing that Freud had reversed the diagnosis: the patient was not sick because he felt guilty; he felt guilty because he had done something genuinely wrong, and the cure was not to dissolve the guilt but to deal with what produced it.

Udhaifu wa Freud ni mzito. Anachukulia kushindwa kwa kimaadili kuwa ugonjwa. Mtu anayesema uongo, asiye mwaminifu katika ndoa, anayeiba, hajatenda dhambi — ni mgonjwa, anasukumwa na nguvu ambazo hawezi kuzizuia. Tiba ni ya kitabibu, si ya kimaadili. Msalaba wa Kristo hauna nafasi; lugha ya hatia yenyewe ndiyo dalili ya kuondolewa. O. Hobart Mowrer (ambaye tutakutana naye chini ya Tiba ya Uadilifu) alitumia maisha yake yote ya kazi akisema kwamba Freud alikuwa amegeuza utambuzi kichwa chini: mgonjwa hakuwa mgonjwa kwa sababu alijisikia mwenye hatia; alijisikia mwenye hatia kwa sababu alikuwa ametenda jambo baya kweli, na dawa haikuwa kuiondoa hatia bali kushughulikia kile kilichoisababisha.

What Christians can learn from Freud is real if limited. He took the past seriously. Patterns repeat. The wound of childhood does not vanish because we have grown up. The Bible itself shows generational sin running from David through Solomon through Rehoboam. A counselor who never asks about the counselee's family of origin is missing material.

Kile ambacho Wakristo wanaweza kujifunza kutoka kwa Freud ni halisi ingawa kina mipaka. Aliyachukulia yaliyopita kwa uzito. Mitindo hujirudia. Jeraha la utotoni halitoweki kwa sababu tumekua. Biblia yenyewe inaonyesha dhambi ya kizazi hadi kizazi ikitoka kwa Daudi kupitia Sulemani hadi Rehoboamu. Mshauri asiyewahi kuuliza kuhusu familia aliyotoka mshauriwa anakosa habari muhimu.

What Drakeford takes: a respect for the past as part of the present. What Drakeford leaves: the medicalization of moral failure. Drakeford's counselee is not sick; he is responsible. His task is not endless excavation; it is confession, change, and obedience.

Anachokichukua Drakeford: heshima kwa yaliyopita kama sehemu ya yaliyopo. Anachokiacha Drakeford: kugeuza kushindwa kwa kimaadili kuwa jambo la kitabibu. Mshauriwa wa Drakeford si mgonjwa; anawajibika. Kazi yake si kuchimbua bila mwisho; ni kuungama, kubadilika, na kutii.
0.2 Client-Centered Therapy — The Mirror Held Up (Rogers)
0.2 Tiba Inayomlenga Mteja — Kioo Kinachoshikwa Mbele Yake (Rogers)

Carl Rogers (1902–1987) was a Chicago counseling psychologist who, in mid-century, broke decisively with Freud. Where Freud had the analyst sit behind the patient and interpret, Rogers turned the chairs to face each other and refused to interpret. The counselor's job, Rogers said, is not to know the counselee's mind for him but to reflect his words back so cleanly that he can hear himself.

Carl Rogers (1902–1987) alikuwa mwanasaikolojia wa ushauri huko Chicago ambaye, katikati ya karne, alijitenga kabisa na Freud. Pale ambapo Freud alimweka mchanganuzi nyuma ya mgonjwa ili atafsiri, Rogers aligeuza viti vielekeane na akakataa kutafsiri. Kazi ya mshauri, Rogers alisema, si kumjulia mshauriwa akili yake, bali kumrudishia maneno yake kwa uwazi kiasi kwamba anaweza kujisikia mwenyewe.

Rogers' key insight is that the counselee, given a safe space and an accepting listener, will move toward health on his own. The counselor provides three things: unconditional positive regard (acceptance regardless of what is disclosed), empathic understanding (entering the counselee's frame and seeing the world from inside it), and congruence (being a real human, not a performing professional). When these three are present, healing happens. Therapy is non-directive: the counselor does not advise, judge, or interpret. He listens, reflects, clarifies, and waits.

Ufahamu mkuu wa Rogers ni kwamba mshauriwa, akipewa mahali salama na msikilizaji anayempokea, ataelekea afya yeye mwenyewe. Mshauri hutoa mambo matatu: kumthamini mtu bila masharti (unconditional positive regard — kumpokea bila kujali lolote analolifunua), kuelewa kwa kuhurumia (empathic understanding — kuingia katika mtazamo wa mshauriwa na kuuona ulimwengu kutoka ndani yake), na uhalisi (congruence — kuwa mwanadamu halisi, si mtaalamu anayeigiza). Mambo haya matatu yanapokuwepo, uponyaji hutokea. Tiba ni ya kutoelekeza: mshauri hashauri, hahukumu, wala hatafsiri. Anasikiliza, anarudisha kilichosemwa, anafafanua, na kungoja.

The method produced one of the most useful frameworks in pastoral counseling. Elias Porter, working out of the Rogerian school, identified five attitudes that lie behind every counselor response: evaluative, interpretive, supportive, probing, and understanding. Porter argued that the understanding response — which neither judges nor diagnoses nor reassures, but simply returns the counselee's experience in slightly clearer language — was the gold standard. Step Two of Drakeford's model relies on Porter's framework directly.

Mbinu hii ilizaa mojawapo ya mifumo yenye manufaa zaidi katika ushauri wa kichungaji. Elias Porter, akifanya kazi ndani ya shule ya Rogers, alitambua mielekeo mitano iliyo nyuma ya kila jibu la mshauri: wa kutathmini (evaluative), wa kutafsiri (interpretive), wa kutegemeza (supportive), wa kudadisi (probing), na wa kuelewa (understanding). Porter alisema kwamba jibu la kuelewa — ambalo halihukumu, halitambui ugonjwa, wala halitoi faraja tupu, bali humrudishia mshauriwa uzoefu wake kwa lugha iliyo wazi kidogo zaidi — ndilo kiwango bora kabisa. Hatua ya Pili ya mbinu ya Drakeford inategemea moja kwa moja mfumo wa Porter.

Rogers' weakness is also his foundation. His system rests on the assumption that the human person is fundamentally good, and given the right conditions will grow toward what is true and right. Christian theology cannot accept that. The human heart is "deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked" (Jeremiah 17:9). A counselee left entirely to himself, however warmly received, may grow in self-justification rather than in truth. There comes a point when the counselor must speak — not interpret in the Freudian sense, but say plainly, "What you are describing is not a misunderstanding; it is sin, and the way out is not through clearer self-knowledge but through repentance."

Udhaifu wa Rogers pia ndio msingi wake. Mfumo wake unasimama juu ya dhana kwamba nafsi ya mwanadamu kimsingi ni njema, na ikipewa mazingira sahihi itakua kuelekea kilicho kweli na haki. Theolojia ya Kikristo haiwezi kulikubali hilo. Moyo wa mwanadamu "huwa mdanganyifu kuliko vitu vyote, una ugonjwa wa kufisha" (Yeremia 17:9). Mshauriwa aliyeachwa peke yake kabisa, hata akipokelewa kwa uchangamfu kiasi gani, anaweza kukua katika kujihesabia haki badala ya kukua katika kweli. Huja wakati ambapo mshauri lazima aseme — si kutafsiri kwa maana ya Freud, bali kusema waziwazi, "Unachokieleza si kutoelewana; ni dhambi, na njia ya kutoka si kujijua kwa uwazi zaidi bali ni kutubu."

What Christians can learn from Rogers is enormous. He recovered listening. He gave the field the discipline of sitting with the counselee long enough actually to hear him. Most pastoral counseling failures are failures at this point: speaking too soon, advising before understanding, applying Scripture to a problem we have not yet seen. Rogers' contribution, by way of Porter, is the counselor's classical posture in the first half of any session.

Kile ambacho Wakristo wanaweza kujifunza kutoka kwa Rogers ni kikubwa mno. Aliurejesha usikilizaji. Aliipa fani hii nidhamu ya kukaa na mshauriwa muda wa kutosha ili kumsikia kweli. Kushindwa kwingi kwa ushauri wa kichungaji ni kushindwa katika jambo hili: kusema mapema mno, kushauri kabla ya kuelewa, kutumia Maandiko kwa tatizo ambalo bado hatujaliona. Mchango wa Rogers, kupitia Porter, ndio mkao wa kawaida wa mshauri katika nusu ya kwanza ya kila kikao.

What Drakeford takes: the discipline of listening, the priority of understanding, Porter's five attitudes. What Drakeford leaves: the assumption that listening alone will heal, and the doctrine of innate human goodness underneath it. Drakeford listens like Rogers in Step Two, and then in Step Five he does what Rogers will not — he asks the counselee, "Where have you failed?"

Anachokichukua Drakeford: nidhamu ya kusikiliza, kipaumbele cha kuelewa, mielekeo mitano ya Porter. Anachokiacha Drakeford: dhana kwamba kusikiliza peke yake kutaponya, na fundisho la wema wa asili wa mwanadamu lililo chini yake. Drakeford husikiliza kama Rogers katika Hatua ya Pili, kisha katika Hatua ya Tano hufanya kile ambacho Rogers hatafanya — humwuliza mshauriwa, "Ni wapi ulipokosea?"
0.3 Behaviorism — What You Do Becomes Who You Are (Skinner)
0.3 Nadharia ya Tabia — Unachokifanya Huwa Ndicho Ulicho (Skinner)

B. F. Skinner (1904–1990), working at Harvard from the 1930s onward, gave the counseling field its most radical alternative. Where Freud went deep into the unconscious and Rogers went deep into feeling, Skinner refused to go inside at all. The inner life, he said, is unobservable and therefore unscientific. What can be observed is behavior. What can be measured is behavior. What can be changed is behavior. Everything else is speculation.

B. F. Skinner (1904–1990), akifanya kazi Harvard tangu miaka ya 1930 na kuendelea, aliipa fani ya ushauri njia yake mbadala iliyo kali zaidi. Pale ambapo Freud alizama ndani ya akili isiyo ya fahamu na Rogers akazama ndani ya hisia, Skinner alikataa kuingia ndani kabisa. Maisha ya ndani, alisema, hayawezi kuonekana na kwa hiyo si ya kisayansi. Kinachoweza kuonekana ni tabia. Kinachoweza kupimwa ni tabia. Kinachoweza kubadilishwa ni tabia. Kila kitu kingine ni makisio tu.

Skinner's key insight is the power of reinforcement. Behavior that is rewarded increases; behavior that is unrewarded extinguishes. A child praised for sharing shares more. A child whose tantrum is met with attention tantrums more. Therapy on this model is technical: identify the behavior to change, identify the reinforcers that maintain it, and rearrange the contingencies. Whole branches of behavior modification grew from this — token economies in institutions, systematic desensitization for phobias, applied behavior analysis for autism, the contracting methods used in addiction treatment.

Ufahamu mkuu wa Skinner ni nguvu ya uimarishaji (reinforcement). Tabia inayozawadiwa huongezeka; tabia isiyozawadiwa hufifia na kutoweka. Mtoto anayesifiwa kwa kugawana hugawana zaidi. Mtoto ambaye ghadhabu yake hupewa usikivu huzidisha ghadhabu. Tiba katika mtazamo huu ni ya kiufundi: tambua tabia ya kubadilishwa, tambua vichocheo vinavyoiimarisha, na upange upya mazingira yanayoitegemeza. Matawi mazima ya urekebishaji wa tabia yalikua kutokana na hili — mifumo ya zawadi kwa vishiria (token economies) katika taasisi, kupunguza hofu hatua kwa hatua (systematic desensitization) kwa woga uliopitiliza, uchambuzi wa tabia unaotumika (applied behavior analysis) kwa usonji, na mbinu za mikataba zinazotumika katika matibabu ya uraibu.

The method's power is undeniable. It works. People do change when their environments change. The counselor who can help a counselee notice which behaviors are being reinforced — by his spouse, his coworkers, his own self-talk — has given him a real tool.

Nguvu ya mbinu hii haikanushiki. Inafanya kazi. Watu hubadilika kweli mazingira yao yanapobadilika. Mshauri anayeweza kumsaidia mshauriwa kutambua ni tabia zipi zinazoimarishwa — na mwenzi wake wa ndoa, wafanyakazi wenzake, maneno anayojiambia mwenyewe — amempa chombo halisi.

Behaviorism's weakness is the same as its strength. By refusing to talk about the inner life, it has no account of meaning, conscience, repentance, love, or worship. The Skinnerian counselor cannot say that an action is wrong; he can only say that it produces consequences the counselee may not want. A counselee whose behavior has been reshaped without any change of heart has been trained, not transformed.

Udhaifu wa nadharia ya tabia ni uleule na nguvu yake. Kwa kukataa kuzungumzia maisha ya ndani, haina maelezo yoyote kuhusu maana, dhamiri, toba, upendo, au ibada. Mshauri wa Skinner hawezi kusema kwamba tendo fulani ni baya; anaweza tu kusema kwamba linaleta matokeo ambayo huenda mshauriwa hayataki. Mshauriwa ambaye tabia yake imeundwa upya bila badiliko lolote la moyo amefunzwa, hajageuzwa.

What Christians can learn from Skinner is the principle of pinpointing. Vague intentions accomplish nothing. "I will be a better father" cannot be lived. "Tonight at supper I will ask each of my children one specific question and listen to the answer without checking my phone" can be lived. Drakeford's Step Six borrows pinpointing directly: the desired behavior must be named, specific, observable, and repeatable. "Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might" (Ecclesiastes 9:10) is biblical specificity; behaviorism merely insists on it.

Kile ambacho Wakristo wanaweza kujifunza kutoka kwa Skinner ni kanuni ya kubainisha kwa usahihi (pinpointing). Nia zisizo wazi hazitimizi kitu. "Nitakuwa baba bora zaidi" haiwezi kuishiwa. "Leo jioni wakati wa chakula nitamwuliza kila mmoja wa watoto wangu swali moja mahususi na kusikiliza jibu bila kuangalia simu yangu" inaweza kuishiwa. Hatua ya Sita ya Drakeford inaazima kanuni ya kubainisha kwa usahihi moja kwa moja: tabia inayotakiwa lazima itajwe, iwe mahususi, ionekane, na iweze kurudiwa. "Lo lote mkono wako utakaloona kufanya, ulifanye kwa nguvu zako" (Mhubiri 9:10) ni umahususi wa kibiblia; nadharia ya tabia inasisitiza tu jambo hilo.

What Drakeford takes: pinpointing, the discipline of measurable behavior, the recognition that environment shapes action. What Drakeford leaves: the refusal to talk about the heart. Drakeford pinpoints behavior because the heart that is changing must show itself in observable conduct. Behaviorism stops at the conduct; Drakeford goes through it to the conscience.

Anachokichukua Drakeford: kubainisha kwa usahihi, nidhamu ya tabia inayoweza kupimwa, kutambua kwamba mazingira huunda matendo. Anachokiacha Drakeford: kukataa kuzungumzia moyo. Drakeford hubainisha tabia kwa usahihi kwa sababu moyo unaobadilika lazima ujionyeshe katika mwenendo unaoonekana. Nadharia ya tabia husimama kwenye mwenendo; Drakeford hupita ndani yake hadi kwenye dhamiri.
0.4 Transactional Analysis — The Tapes Inside (Berne, Harris, James)
0.4 Uchambuzi wa Miamala — Kanda Zilizo Ndani (Berne, Harris, James)

Eric Berne (1910–1970), a Canadian-American psychiatrist trained in psychoanalysis, broke with the Freudian school in the 1950s and developed a more accessible system he called Transactional Analysis. His popular books — Games People Play (1964) and Thomas Harris's I'm OK — You're OK (1967), followed by Muriel James's Born to Win (1971) — moved counseling concepts out of the consulting room and into the bookstores of ordinary readers. By 1970 TA was a household conversation. It has faded somewhat in the Western counseling field but remains influential in Asia and Latin America.

Eric Berne (1910–1970), daktari wa magonjwa ya akili Mkanada-Mmarekani aliyefunzwa uchanganuzi wa nafsi, alijitenga na shule ya Freud katika miaka ya 1950 na kuunda mfumo unaoeleweka kwa urahisi zaidi aliouita Uchambuzi wa Miamala (Transactional Analysis, TA). Vitabu vyake vilivyopendwa na wengi — Games People Play (Michezo Ambayo Watu Hucheza, 1964) na kitabu cha Thomas Harris I'm OK — You're OK (Mimi Niko Sawa — Wewe Uko Sawa, 1967), kikifuatwa na Born to Win (Kuzaliwa Ili Kushinda, 1971) cha Muriel James — vilitoa dhana za ushauri nje ya chumba cha mashauriano na kuziingiza katika maduka ya vitabu ya wasomaji wa kawaida. Kufikia mwaka 1970 TA ilikuwa mazungumzo ya kila nyumba. Imefifia kwa kiasi fulani katika fani ya ushauri ya nchi za Magharibi lakini bado ina ushawishi Asia na Amerika ya Kusini.

Berne's key insight is that every person operates from three ego states: Parent, Adult, and Child. The Parent state contains the recorded voices of authority figures — the rules, judgments, warnings, and comforts absorbed before age six. The Child state holds the feelings, impulses, and reactions of the small person we once were. The Adult state is the rational, present-tense self who handles facts and makes decisions. All three are useful in their place. Trouble comes when the wrong state takes over — when the Adult should be deciding but the Child is feeling, or when the Parent is judging where understanding is needed.

Ufahamu mkuu wa Berne ni kwamba kila mtu hutenda kutoka katika hali tatu za nafsi: Mzazi, Mtu Mzima, na Mtoto. Hali ya Mzazi ina sauti zilizorekodiwa za watu wenye mamlaka — kanuni, hukumu, maonyo, na faraja zilizopokelewa kabla ya umri wa miaka sita. Hali ya Mtoto inashika hisia, misukumo, na miitikio ya yule mtu mdogo tuliyekuwa zamani. Hali ya Mtu Mzima ni nafsi yenye busara ya wakati uliopo, inayoshughulikia ukweli na kufanya maamuzi. Zote tatu zina manufaa mahali pake. Taabu huja hali isiyofaa inapotawala — wakati Mtu Mzima anapaswa kuamua lakini Mtoto ndiye anayehisi, au wakati Mzazi anahukumu pale ambapo kuelewa kunahitajika.

These ego states are stored, Berne said, like tapes in a recorder. When a present situation resembles a past one, the old tape begins to play. A husband hears his wife use a phrase his mother used, and the Child in him reacts to her as if she were his mother. He may not know why he is angry; he only knows that he is. The TA counselor helps the counselee identify which tape is playing and choose, as an Adult, whether to play it through or turn it off. The promising line, repeated often in the literature, is that telling oneself something twenty times begins to record over the old message — that the counselee who looks in the mirror and says, "I am a wonderful person, made in God's image, and I do not have to live under that old voice," is doing real work on his own tapes.

Hali hizi za nafsi zimehifadhiwa, Berne alisema, kama kanda ndani ya kinasa sauti. Hali ya sasa inapofanana na ya zamani, kanda ya zamani huanza kucheza. Mume anamsikia mkewe akitumia msemo aliokuwa akiutumia mama yake, na Mtoto aliye ndani yake anamwitikia mkewe kana kwamba ni mama yake. Huenda hajui kwa nini amekasirika; anajua tu kwamba amekasirika. Mshauri wa TA humsaidia mshauriwa kutambua ni kanda ipi inayocheza na kuchagua, kama Mtu Mzima, kama aiache icheze hadi mwisho au aizime. Msemo wenye matumaini, unaorudiwa mara nyingi katika maandiko hayo, ni kwamba kujiambia jambo mara ishirini huanza kurekodi juu ya ujumbe wa zamani — kwamba mshauriwa anayejitazama kiooni na kusema, "Mimi ni mtu wa thamani kubwa, nimeumbwa kwa sura ya Mungu, na sihitaji kuishi chini ya sauti ile ya zamani," anafanya kazi halisi juu ya kanda zake mwenyewe.

TA also taught the field a memorable framework for self-evaluation, the four life positions. "I'm OK — You're OK" is the healthy stance: I am uniquely gifted and so are you. "I'm OK — You're not OK" is arrogance: I am worthwhile, but you are not. "I'm not OK — You're OK" is depression: I am a failure, but you are successful. "I'm not OK — You're not OK" is despair: nothing is worth anything. Most life problems, the TA literature argued, can be traced to a life position adopted in childhood and never re-examined as an adult.

TA pia iliifundisha fani mfumo wa kukumbukwa wa kujitathmini, yaani misimamo minne ya maisha. "Mimi niko sawa — Wewe uko sawa" ni msimamo wenye afya: nina karama za pekee na wewe pia unazo. "Mimi niko sawa — Wewe hauko sawa" ni majivuno: mimi nina thamani, lakini wewe huna. "Mimi siko sawa — Wewe uko sawa" ni sonona: mimi nimeshindwa, lakini wewe umefanikiwa. "Mimi siko sawa — Wewe hauko sawa" ni kukata tamaa kabisa: hakuna kitu chenye thamani yoyote. Matatizo mengi ya maisha, maandiko ya TA yalisema, yanaweza kufuatiliwa hadi msimamo wa maisha uliochukuliwa utotoni na ambao haukuwahi kuchunguzwa upya katika utu uzima.

Then there are the games. Berne's Games People Play catalogued the small recurring scripts in which two people interact on the surface while pursuing a hidden payoff underneath. "Why don't you — yes but," in which one party offers solutions the other systematically rejects, with the payoff of the rejecter's confirmed helplessness. "If it weren't for you," in which one partner blames the other for limitations actually welcomed. "Kick me," in which one person provokes punishment to reinforce his sense of worthlessness. "Mine is better than yours." "Ain't it awful." The Christian psychiatrist Frank Minirth added "I'm more religious than you" for the church context. Naming the game, Berne argued, often ended it. The counselor who can gently say, "I notice we have been doing 'yes but' for fifteen minutes — what would happen if you actually tried one of these?" is offering the counselee an Adult exit from a Child's pattern.

Kisha kuna michezo. Kitabu cha Berne Games People Play kiliorodhesha maigizo madogo yanayojirudia ambamo watu wawili huingiliana kwa juu juu huku wakifuatilia faida iliyofichwa chini yake. "Kwa nini usi— ndiyo lakini" (Why don't you — yes but), ambamo upande mmoja hutoa masuluhisho ambayo upande mwingine huyakataa kwa utaratibu, na faida yake ni kuthibitishwa kwa kutojiweza kwa yule anayekataa. "Kama si wewe" (If it weren't for you), ambamo mwenzi mmoja humlaumu mwingine kwa mipaka ambayo kwa kweli anaifurahia. "Nipige teke" (Kick me), ambamo mtu mmoja huchochea adhabu ili kuimarisha hisia yake ya kutokuwa na thamani. "Changu ni bora kuliko chako." "Si ni jambo baya mno." Daktari Mkristo wa magonjwa ya akili Frank Minirth aliongeza "Mimi ni mcha Mungu kuliko wewe" (I'm more religious than you) kwa mazingira ya kanisa. Kuutaja mchezo kwa jina lake, Berne alisema, mara nyingi kuliumaliza. Mshauri anayeweza kusema kwa upole, "Naona tumekuwa tukicheza 'ndiyo lakini' kwa dakika kumi na tano — ingekuwaje kama ungejaribu kweli mojawapo ya haya?" anampa mshauriwa njia ya kutoka ya Mtu Mzima katika mtindo wa Mtoto.

Underneath the games lies the life script — a story the person has been writing about himself since childhood, with familiar themes (love, hate, revenge, jealousy) and a predictable ending. Script analysis brings the unconscious narrative into the open so the Adult can revise it.

Chini ya michezo hiyo kuna hati ya maisha (life script) — hadithi ambayo mtu amekuwa akiiandika kuhusu nafsi yake tangu utotoni, yenye maudhui yanayojulikana (upendo, chuki, kisasi, wivu) na mwisho unaotabirika. Uchambuzi wa hati huileta hadithi hiyo isiyo ya fahamu wazi ili Mtu Mzima aweze kuirekebisha.

TA's weakness is its theological thinness. The Parent-Adult-Child framework is descriptive, not redemptive. Awareness can rewrite a script, but only in the limited sense that any self-conscious person can choose differently. TA has no doctrine of regeneration, no Holy Spirit, no atoning blood. The "I'm OK" of the healthy life position rests, finally, on self-acceptance — which the gospel says is precisely not the ground on which a fallen human stands. We are not OK; we are forgiven, which is a different and stronger thing.

Udhaifu wa TA ni wembamba wake wa kitheolojia. Mfumo wa Mzazi-Mtu Mzima-Mtoto ni wa kueleza, si wa kukomboa. Ufahamu unaweza kuandika upya hati ya maisha, lakini kwa maana finyu tu ambayo kwayo mtu yeyote anayejitambua anaweza kuchagua tofauti. TA haina fundisho la kuzaliwa upya, haina Roho Mtakatifu, haina damu ya upatanisho. "Niko sawa" wa msimamo wa maisha wenye afya unasimama, hatimaye, juu ya kujikubali — jambo ambalo injili inasema ndilo hasa si msingi ambao mwanadamu aliyeanguka anasimama juu yake. Hatuko sawa; tumesamehewa, na hilo ni jambo tofauti na lenye nguvu zaidi.

What Christians can learn from TA is substantial. The doctrine of original sin includes the recognition that we have been shaped by voices that were not God's voice — that the Parent tapes in our heads are sometimes truthful but often distortions, and that the work of sanctification includes letting Scripture record over the lies. Ephesians 4:22–24 — "put off concerning the former conversation the old man… and be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and… put on the new man" — is, in TA's language, replacing a corrupted script with a new one written by the Spirit.

Kile ambacho Wakristo wanaweza kujifunza kutoka kwa TA ni kikubwa. Fundisho la dhambi ya asili linajumuisha kutambua kwamba tumeundwa na sauti ambazo hazikuwa sauti ya Mungu — kwamba kanda za Mzazi vichwani mwetu wakati mwingine ni za kweli lakini mara nyingi ni upotoshaji, na kwamba kazi ya utakaso inajumuisha kuyaacha Maandiko yarekodi juu ya uongo huo. Waefeso 4:22–24 — "mvue kwa habari ya mwenendo wenu wa kwanza utu wa kale… na kufanywa wapya katika roho ya nia zenu; mkavae utu mpya" — kwa lugha ya TA, ni kubadilisha hati iliyoharibika kwa hati mpya iliyoandikwa na Roho.

The four life positions also map, with care, onto pastoral categories. "I'm OK — You're not OK" is pride. "I'm not OK — You're OK" is the depressed self-loathing that often masks despair of grace. "I'm not OK — You're not OK" is the cynicism of the abused or the long-discouraged. The counselor who recognizes a life position has a starting point for the gospel address that lifts the counselee out of it.

Misimamo minne ya maisha pia inaweza kulinganishwa, kwa uangalifu, na makundi ya kichungaji. "Mimi niko sawa — Wewe hauko sawa" ni kiburi. "Mimi siko sawa — Wewe uko sawa" ni kujichukia kwa sonona ambako mara nyingi huficha kukata tamaa ya neema. "Mimi siko sawa — Wewe hauko sawa" ni ubeuzi wa walionyanyaswa au wa waliokata tamaa kwa muda mrefu. Mshauri anayetambua msimamo wa maisha ana mahali pa kuanzia kwa ujumbe wa injili unaomwinua mshauriwa kutoka humo.

What Drakeford takes: the discipline of recognizing patterns the counselee cannot see in himself, the willingness to name a game gently as a clarifying move, the recognition that life scripts can be revised. What Drakeford leaves: the assumption that awareness alone is enough, and the "I'm OK" foundation that rests on self-acceptance rather than on Christ's acceptance of the sinner.

Anachokichukua Drakeford: nidhamu ya kutambua mitindo ambayo mshauriwa hawezi kuiona ndani yake mwenyewe, utayari wa kuutaja mchezo kwa upole kama hatua ya kufafanua, kutambua kwamba hati za maisha zinaweza kurekebishwa. Anachokiacha Drakeford: dhana kwamba ufahamu peke yake unatosha, na msingi wa "Niko sawa" unaosimama juu ya kujikubali badala ya kusimama juu ya Kristo kumkubali mwenye dhambi.
0.5 Nouthetic Counseling — Confront with Scripture (Adams)
0.5 Ushauri wa Kinouthetiki — Kabili kwa Maandiko (Adams)

Jay Adams (1929–2020), a Reformed pastor and seminary professor, published Competent to Counsel in 1970 and almost single-handedly launched the modern biblical counseling movement. Adams was reacting both to secular psychology (which he found unbiblical at its roots) and to pastoral counseling that he believed had become too Rogerian — too willing to listen, too slow to confront. His system has shaped large segments of American evangelicalism through the Christian Counseling and Educational Foundation (CCEF) and the Association of Certified Biblical Counselors (ACBC).

Jay Adams (1929–2020), mchungaji na profesa wa seminari wa mapokeo ya Kireformed, alichapisha Competent to Counsel (Mwenye Uwezo wa Kushauri) mwaka 1970 na karibu peke yake akaanzisha vuguvugu la kisasa la ushauri wa kibiblia. Adams alikuwa akipinga saikolojia ya kidunia (ambayo aliiona kuwa si ya kibiblia katika mizizi yake) na pia ushauri wa kichungaji ambao aliamini ulikuwa umekuwa wa mtindo wa Rogers kupita kiasi — tayari mno kusikiliza, mzito mno kukabili. Mfumo wake umeunda sehemu kubwa za Ukristo wa Kiinjili wa Marekani kupitia Christian Counseling and Educational Foundation (CCEF) na Association of Certified Biblical Counselors (ACBC).

Adams's key insight comes from the Greek word noutheteō, which Paul uses in passages such as Romans 15:14 ("able also to admonish one another") and Colossians 1:28 ("admonishing every man"). The word means to confront with the goal of changing behavior. Adams argued that what counseling really is, biblically, is one believer confronting another with the Word of God for the purpose of behavior change. There is no neutral psychological space outside Scripture. Anxiety, depression, anger, marital trouble, and addictive behavior are not illnesses to be treated; they are sin-patterns to be repented of and exchanged for biblical patterns under the discipline of Scripture and the Holy Spirit.

Ufahamu mkuu wa Adams unatoka katika neno la Kigiriki noutheteō, ambalo Paulo analitumia katika vifungu kama Warumi 15:14 ("mwaweza kuonyana ninyi kwa ninyi") na Wakolosai 1:28 ("tukimwonya kila mtu"). Neno hilo linamaanisha kukabili kwa lengo la kubadilisha tabia. Adams alisema kwamba ushauri ni nini hasa, kibiblia, ni mwamini mmoja kumkabili mwingine kwa Neno la Mungu kwa kusudi la kubadilisha tabia. Hakuna nafasi ya kisaikolojia isiyoegemea upande wowote iliyo nje ya Maandiko. Wasiwasi, sonona, hasira, matatizo ya ndoa, na tabia za uraibu si magonjwa ya kutibiwa; ni mitindo ya dhambi ya kutubiwa na kubadilishwa kwa mitindo ya kibiblia chini ya nidhamu ya Maandiko na Roho Mtakatifu.

The method is direct. The counselor listens long enough to identify the sin-pattern, then confronts. The counselee is taught what the Bible commands, given homework (read, memorize, do), and held accountable in the following sessions. The pace is brisk. Most nouthetic counseling is short-term by design — eight to twelve sessions rather than years. The counselee leaves with concrete behavioral commitments, not with self-understanding.

Mbinu ni ya moja kwa moja. Mshauri husikiliza muda wa kutosha ili kutambua mtindo wa dhambi, kisha hukabili. Mshauriwa hufundishwa kile ambacho Biblia inaamuru, hupewa kazi ya nyumbani (soma, kariri, tenda), na huwajibishwa katika vikao vinavyofuata. Kasi ni ya haraka. Ushauri mwingi wa kinouthetiki kwa makusudi ni wa muda mfupi — vikao nane hadi kumi na viwili badala ya miaka. Mshauriwa huondoka akiwa na ahadi halisi za kitabia, si akiwa na kujielewa tu.

Nouthetic counseling's strength is its theological seriousness. Adams insisted, correctly, that the Bible has more to say about the human condition than any other book ever written, and that the pastor with an open Bible is not less competent to counsel a depressed believer than the psychologist with a Ph.D. He took repentance seriously. He took the sufficiency of Scripture seriously. He refused to treat the church's calling to soul care as a junior partnership with the clinic.

Nguvu ya ushauri wa kinouthetiki ni uzito wake wa kitheolojia. Adams alisisitiza, kwa usahihi, kwamba Biblia ina mengi zaidi ya kusema kuhusu hali ya mwanadamu kuliko kitabu kingine chochote kilichowahi kuandikwa, na kwamba mchungaji mwenye Biblia iliyo wazi hana uwezo mdogo wa kumshauri mwamini mwenye sonona kuliko mwanasaikolojia mwenye shahada ya uzamivu (Ph.D.). Aliichukulia toba kwa uzito. Aliuchukulia utoshelevu wa Maandiko kwa uzito. Alikataa kuuchukulia wito wa kanisa wa kuzihudumia nafsi kama ushirika wa daraja la chini chini ya kliniki.

The weakness is in the proportion. Adams's early work tended to treat almost every counseling problem as a sin problem requiring confrontation, and to give insufficient attention to suffering that is not the counselee's fault — to abuse, to grief, to clinical depression with biological components, to the slow work of comforting Job rather than instructing him. The later biblical counseling movement (CCEF in particular, under writers like David Powlison) has refined the model considerably, distinguishing more carefully between sin to be confronted and suffering to be borne with. But the early nouthetic instinct toward swift confrontation could miss the long listening that Step Two requires.

Udhaifu uko katika uwiano. Kazi za mwanzo za Adams zilielekea kulichukulia karibu kila tatizo la ushauri kuwa tatizo la dhambi linalohitaji kukabiliwa, na kutoa uangalifu usiotosha kwa mateso ambayo si kosa la mshauriwa — kwa unyanyasaji, kwa huzuni ya msiba, kwa sonona ya kitabibu yenye vipengele vya kibaiolojia, kwa kazi ya polepole ya kumfariji Ayubu badala ya kumfundisha. Vuguvugu la baadaye la ushauri wa kibiblia (hasa CCEF, chini ya waandishi kama David Powlison) limeiboresha mbinu hiyo kwa kiasi kikubwa, likitofautisha kwa uangalifu zaidi kati ya dhambi ya kukabiliwa na mateso ya kuvumiliwa pamoja na mtu. Lakini silika ya mwanzo ya kinouthetiki ya kukabili haraka ingeweza kukosa usikilizaji mrefu ambao Hatua ya Pili inautaka.

What Drakeford and Adams share is more than what divides them. Both insist that the counselee is responsible, that change is possible, that the Bible is the counselor's primary text, and that the goal is not endless therapy but obedience to Christ. Both reject the medicalization of moral failure. Both believe that an ordinary believing pastor, properly trained, can do real soul work.

Yale ambayo Drakeford na Adams wanashirikiana ni mengi kuliko yale yanayowatenganisha. Wote wawili wanasisitiza kwamba mshauriwa anawajibika, kwamba badiliko linawezekana, kwamba Biblia ndiyo maandiko ya msingi ya mshauri, na kwamba lengo si tiba isiyo na mwisho bali ni utii kwa Kristo. Wote wawili wanakataa kugeuza kushindwa kwa kimaadili kuwa jambo la kitabibu. Wote wawili wanaamini kwamba mchungaji wa kawaida mwenye imani, aliyefunzwa ipasavyo, anaweza kufanya kazi halisi ya kuhudumia nafsi.

What Drakeford takes from the same well Adams drinks from: confidence in Scripture, expectation of change, brevity of treatment. What Drakeford does differently: he listens longer before he confronts. Step Two and Step Three precede Step Five for a reason. Drakeford's counselor earns the right to ask "Where have you failed?" by first hearing the whole story. Adams's classical instinct is to ask sooner. Both can be done biblically; the pastor must know what he is doing and why.

Anachokichukua Drakeford kutoka kisima kilekile ambacho Adams anakinywea: kuyaamini Maandiko, kutarajia badiliko, ufupi wa matibabu. Anachokifanya Drakeford kwa namna tofauti: husikiliza muda mrefu zaidi kabla ya kukabili. Hatua ya Pili na Hatua ya Tatu zinatangulia Hatua ya Tano kwa sababu fulani. Mshauri wa Drakeford hupata haki ya kuuliza "Ni wapi ulipokosea?" kwa kusikia kwanza hadithi nzima. Silika ya kawaida ya Adams ni kuuliza mapema zaidi. Njia zote mbili zinaweza kufanywa kibiblia; mchungaji lazima ajue anachokifanya na kwa nini.
0.6 Where Drakeford Stands
0.6 Drakeford Anasimama Wapi

Drakeford stands roughly here. He is closer to Adams than to Rogers in his doctrine of the person — sin is real, responsibility is real, change requires confession and obedience. He is closer to Rogers than to Adams in the discipline of his early sessions — listen long, understand deeply, do not confront until the counselee has been genuinely heard. He absorbs Skinner's pinpointing without becoming a behaviorist; he uses Berne's pattern-naming without buying TA's anthropology; he respects Freud's recognition that the past is alive without medicalizing the present.

Drakeford anasimama takriban hapa. Yuko karibu zaidi na Adams kuliko Rogers katika fundisho lake kuhusu mwanadamu — dhambi ni halisi, uwajibikaji ni halisi, badiliko linahitaji kuungama na kutii. Yuko karibu zaidi na Rogers kuliko Adams katika nidhamu ya vikao vyake vya mwanzo — sikiliza kwa muda mrefu, elewa kwa kina, usikabili mpaka mshauriwa amesikilizwa kweli. Anachukua kanuni ya Skinner ya kubainisha kwa usahihi bila kuwa mfuasi wa nadharia ya tabia; anatumia mtindo wa Berne wa kutaja mitindo kwa majina bila kukubali mtazamo wa TA kuhusu mwanadamu; anaheshimu utambuzi wa Freud kwamba yaliyopita yako hai bila kugeuza yaliyopo kuwa jambo la kitabibu.

The ten steps are not a neutral technique. They are a deliberately Christian integration. Step One frames the encounter. Steps Two through Four hear the counselee out fully. Step Five turns the conversation toward responsibility — the hinge that secular models cannot turn. Steps Six through Ten move toward action and closure. The shape of the model is the shape of Drakeford's settlement of the field: listen like Rogers in the first half, confront like Adams in the middle, build like Skinner in the second half, recognize patterns like Berne throughout, and let the Spirit do through Scripture what no method can manufacture.

Hatua kumi si mbinu isiyoegemea upande wowote. Ni muunganiko wa Kikristo uliokusudiwa kwa makusudi. Hatua ya Kwanza huweka mazingira ya kukutana. Hatua ya Pili hadi ya Nne humsikiliza mshauriwa kikamilifu. Hatua ya Tano hugeuza mazungumzo kuelekea uwajibikaji — bawaba ambayo mifumo ya kidunia haiwezi kuigeuza. Hatua ya Sita hadi ya Kumi huelekea kwenye matendo na kuhitimisha. Umbo la mbinu hii ndilo umbo la jinsi Drakeford alivyoipatanisha fani: sikiliza kama Rogers katika nusu ya kwanza, kabili kama Adams katikati, jenga kama Skinner katika nusu ya pili, tambua mitindo kama Berne kila wakati, na umwache Roho afanye kupitia Maandiko kile ambacho hakuna mbinu inayoweza kukitengeneza.

The pastor who has studied this landscape will not be intimidated when a counselee says, "My therapist told me…" He will know what tradition the therapist was drinking from. He will know what to keep, what to question, and what to leave alone. He will know where Drakeford stands — and, more importantly, why.

Mchungaji aliyejifunza mandhari hii hatatishika mshauriwa anaposema, "Mtaalamu wangu wa tiba aliniambia…" Atajua mtaalamu huyo alikuwa akinywa kutoka mapokeo yapi. Atajua cha kushika, cha kuhoji, na cha kuacha. Atajua Drakeford anasimama wapi — na, muhimu zaidi, kwa nini.

Determine the Time and the Place
Amua Muda na Mahali
"How long do we have? Where can we meet?" — the architecture of every counseling encounter begins here.
"Tuna muda kiasi gani? Tunaweza kukutana wapi?" — ujenzi wa kila mkutano wa ushauri huanzia hapa.
1.1 The Counseling Frame
1.1 Mfumo wa Ushauri

Before a single word of the counselee's story is spoken, two structural decisions shape everything that follows: when this conversation will happen and where it will take place. These are not preliminaries to clear away before the "real" counseling begins. They are counseling. The wisdom of Drakeford's first step is its insistence that the counselor establish the boundaries of the encounter before the encounter generates its own pressures. A counselor who plunges into the problem without first determining the time and the place will find himself either rushed beyond his ability to help, or trapped in a session that drifts because no one knows when it should end.

Kabla hata neno moja la habari ya mshauriwa halijatamkwa, maamuzi mawili ya kimuundo huunda kila kitu kinachofuata: mazungumzo haya yatafanyika lini na yatafanyika wapi. Haya si mambo ya awali ya kuondolewa njiani kabla ushauri "halisi" haujaanza. Haya ndiyo ushauri. Hekima ya hatua ya kwanza ya Drakeford ni msisitizo wake kwamba mshauri aweke mipaka ya mkutano kabla mkutano wenyewe haujazaa shinikizo zake. Mshauri anayejitosa katika tatizo bila kwanza kuamua muda na mahali atajikuta ama ameharakishwa kupita uwezo wake wa kusaidia, ama amenaswa katika kikao kinachoyumbayumba kwa sababu hakuna anayejua kinapaswa kuisha lini.

When a counselee approaches you, he will rarely give an honest estimate of how long he needs. People in distress habitually understate their need: "Could I bother you for just a minute?" or "This will only take a moment." Almost without exception, the matter that pressed them to seek help cannot actually be addressed in a minute. The first kindness you can do them is to refuse the false economy of their words and ask the truthful question yourself.

Mshauriwa anapokujia, mara chache atatoa makadirio ya kweli ya muda anaouhitaji. Watu walio katika dhiki kwa mazoea hupunguza uzito wa hitaji lao: "Naweza kukusumbua kwa dakika moja tu?" au "Hili litachukua muda mfupi tu." Karibu bila kubagua, jambo lililowasukuma kutafuta msaada haliwezi kweli kushughulikiwa kwa dakika moja. Wema wa kwanza unaoweza kuwatendea ni kukataa ubahili huo wa uongo wa maneno yao na kuuliza wewe mwenyewe swali la kweli.
1.2 The Question of Time
1.2 Swali la Muda

"How much time do we have?" This is the first sentence the counselor should speak after the greeting. It accomplishes three things at once. First, it forces both parties to be honest about availability. The counselee may have thirty minutes before he must collect a child from school; you may have forty-five minutes before another commitment. Naming these constraints aloud removes a hidden tension that would otherwise contaminate the entire session. Second, the question signals that this conversation is bounded — it has a beginning and an end. Counselees who feel a session is open-ended often delay coming to the heart of the matter, sensing they have all evening to circle their pain. A clear time frame focuses the conversation. Third, the question gives you a legitimate close. When the time you agreed upon arrives, you can say without apology, "I see our time is about gone. Thank you for sharing with me."

"Tuna muda kiasi gani?" Hii ndiyo sentensi ya kwanza ambayo mshauri anapaswa kusema baada ya salamu. Inatimiza mambo matatu kwa wakati mmoja. Kwanza, inawalazimisha pande zote mbili kuwa wakweli kuhusu nafasi waliyonayo. Mshauriwa anaweza kuwa na dakika thelathini kabla hajaenda kumchukua mtoto shuleni; wewe unaweza kuwa na dakika arobaini na tano kabla ya ahadi nyingine. Kuyataja mipaka hii kwa sauti huondoa mvutano uliofichika ambao vinginevyo ungechafua kikao kizima. Pili, swali hili huashiria kwamba mazungumzo haya yana mipaka — yana mwanzo na mwisho. Washauriwa wanaohisi kwamba kikao hakina kikomo mara nyingi huchelewa kufika kwenye kiini cha jambo, wakihisi kwamba wana jioni nzima ya kuzunguka maumivu yao. Muda ulio wazi huyalenga mazungumzo. Tatu, swali hili hukupa namna halali ya kuhitimisha. Muda mliokubaliana unapofika, unaweza kusema bila kuomba radhi, "Naona muda wetu unakaribia kwisha. Asante kwa kunieleza."

A common error among inexperienced counselors is the belief that more time produces more help. It does not. Drakeford observed in his decades of practice that long sessions are usually the result of poor technique rather than genuine need. A focused thirty-minute session in which the counselor listens well, clarifies the real problem, and points toward an action plan does more for a troubled soul than three hours of meandering conversation. Some pastors have built reputations for counseling all night with the distressed. This is rarely a mark of dedication; more often it indicates that the counselor never learned to bring a session to closure, and that the counselee has learned that wandering keeps the helper engaged. The biblical counselor sets a frame and trusts God to work within it.

Kosa la kawaida miongoni mwa washauri wasio na uzoefu ni kuamini kwamba muda mwingi zaidi huzaa msaada mwingi zaidi. Sivyo. Drakeford aliona katika miongo yake ya huduma kwamba vikao virefu kwa kawaida ni matokeo ya mbinu duni kuliko ya hitaji halisi. Kikao cha dakika thelathini kilicholengwa, ambamo mshauri anasikiliza vizuri, anafafanua tatizo halisi, na anaelekeza kwenye mpango wa utendaji, humfaa zaidi mtu mwenye taabu nafsini kuliko saa tatu za mazungumzo yanayotangatanga. Baadhi ya wachungaji wamejijengea sifa ya kuwashauri wenye dhiki usiku kucha. Mara chache hiyo ni alama ya kujitoa; mara nyingi zaidi inaonyesha kwamba mshauri hakuwahi kujifunza kukifikisha kikao mwisho wake, na kwamba mshauriwa amejifunza kwamba kutangatanga humfanya msaidizi aendelee kushughulika naye. Mshauri wa kibiblia huweka mfumo na humtumaini Mungu kufanya kazi ndani yake.

When the agreed time begins to expire and the work is genuinely incomplete, you may extend with full transparency: "If it is all right with you, we can take a few more minutes." Notice the counselee's permission is sought; you do not unilaterally extend. This preserves the dignity of the agreement and prevents the session from becoming an obligation the counselee cannot escape.

Muda uliokubaliwa unapoanza kwisha na kazi bado kweli haijakamilika, unaweza kuongeza muda kwa uwazi kamili: "Kama ni sawa kwako, tunaweza kuchukua dakika chache zaidi." Angalia kwamba ruhusa ya mshauriwa inaombwa; hauongezi muda kwa uamuzi wako peke yako. Hili hulinda heshima ya makubaliano na huzuia kikao kisigeuke kuwa wajibu ambao mshauriwa hawezi kuukwepa.
1.3 The Question of Place
1.3 Swali la Mahali

"Where can we meet?" Place matters more than beginning counselors typically assume. The setting communicates before you speak. A pastor's study with a closed door communicates one set of expectations; a coffee shop booth communicates another; a hospital bedside communicates yet another. Drakeford's principle is that the ideal setting is a private situation in a semipublic place. Privacy is required because troubled people will not unburden themselves where they fear being overheard. Semipublic visibility is required because counseling alone with a person of the opposite sex behind a closed and opaque door creates conditions for both real and imagined impropriety.

"Tunaweza kukutana wapi?" Mahali ni muhimu kuliko washauri wanaoanza wanavyodhani kwa kawaida. Mazingira huwasiliana kabla wewe hujasema. Ofisi ya mchungaji yenye mlango uliofungwa huwasilisha matarajio ya aina moja; kibanda katika mgahawa wa kahawa huwasilisha mengine; kando ya kitanda hospitalini huwasilisha mengine tena. Kanuni ya Drakeford ni kwamba mazingira bora ni hali ya faragha mahali palipo wazi kwa kiasi. Faragha inahitajika kwa sababu watu wenye taabu hawatajifunua mahali wanapoogopa kusikiwa na wengine. Kuonekana kwa kiasi kunahitajika kwa sababu kumshauri peke yako mtu wa jinsia tofauti nyuma ya mlango uliofungwa usiopenya macho hutengeneza mazingira ya utovu wa adabu, wa kweli na wa kudhaniwa.

Many seasoned pastors install a glass panel in the office door, or leave the door slightly ajar with a secretary working in an adjacent room. These are not paranoid measures; they are acts of pastoral wisdom that protect both counselor and counselee. The gospel that called you into this work also calls you to maintain a reputation above reproach (1 Tim 3:2). When that reputation is preserved by the architecture of your space, you do not have to defend it later by your word.

Wachungaji wengi wenye uzoefu huweka kipande cha kioo katika mlango wa ofisi, au huuacha mlango wazi kidogo huku katibu akifanya kazi katika chumba jirani. Hizi si hatua za woga usio na sababu; ni matendo ya hekima ya kichungaji yanayomlinda mshauri na mshauriwa pia. Injili iliyokuita katika kazi hii pia inakuita kudumisha sifa isiyolaumika (1 Timotheo 3:2). Sifa hiyo inapolindwa na mpangilio wa mahali pako, hutalazimika kuitetea baadaye kwa neno lako.

The arrangement of furniture inside the room carries its own message. Do not sit behind a desk. A desk is a piece of furniture designed to separate authority from petitioner, and although you may hold pastoral authority you do not want to communicate distance in this moment. Two chairs at a slight angle, not directly facing each other, with no obstruction between, is the classical counseling configuration. A small side table for tissues, a glass of water, a lamp giving warm light rather than overhead fluorescence — these details are not decorative niceties. They tell the counselee that someone prepared this place to receive him.

Mpangilio wa samani ndani ya chumba nao hubeba ujumbe wake. Usiketi nyuma ya meza ya ofisi. Meza ya ofisi ni samani iliyoundwa kutenganisha mwenye mamlaka na mwombaji, na ingawa unaweza kuwa na mamlaka ya kichungaji, hutaki kuwasilisha umbali katika wakati huu. Viti viwili vilivyoelekezwa kwa pembe kidogo, visivyotazamana moja kwa moja, bila kizuizi chochote katikati, ndio mpangilio wa jadi wa ushauri. Meza ndogo ya pembeni kwa ajili ya karatasi za kufutia machozi, glasi ya maji, taa inayotoa mwanga wa joto badala ya mwanga mkali wa taa za juu za fluoresenti — vitu hivi vidogo si mapambo tu. Vinamwambia mshauriwa kwamba mtu fulani alipaandaa mahali hapa ili kumpokea.

For some forms of counseling — what Drakeford called marketplace counseling — the place is wherever you find the person. A grandmother weeping in a grocery aisle, a teenager waiting in your car after youth group, a businessman on a park bench during his lunch break: these encounters do not permit a controlled setting. In such cases the principle is the same in spirit if not in form. You move toward the maximum privacy your circumstance allows, you protect the counselee from being overheard or interrupted, and you give them your full attention.

Kwa aina fulani za ushauri — kile ambacho Drakeford aliita ushauri wa sokoni — mahali ni popote unapomkuta mtu. Bibi analia katika njia ya duka la vyakula, kijana anakusubiri ndani ya gari lako baada ya mkutano wa vijana, mfanyabiashara kwenye benchi la bustani wakati wa mapumziko yake ya mchana: mikutano hii hairuhusu mazingira yaliyodhibitiwa. Katika hali kama hizo kanuni ni ile ile katika roho yake ingawa si katika umbo lake. Unasogea kuelekea faragha kubwa kabisa ambayo hali yako inaruhusu, unamlinda mshauriwa asisikiwe wala asikatizwe, na unampa usikivu wako wote.
1.4 Pastoral Wisdom on the Frame
1.4 Hekima ya Kichungaji Kuhusu Mfumo

There is one further dimension of time and place that deserves explicit naming, because failure here has destroyed pastoral ministries: the pastor's relationship to his own household and his own state. A counselor who rises from arguing with his wife to receive a counselee at the door has chosen a poor time, even if the appointment was scheduled. A counselor who has not slept and is reaching for caffeine to stay alert has chosen a poor time. A counselor whose own household is in crisis must consider whether he is the right person for this particular hour. The biblical office of counselor (1 Chronicles 27:32 names Jonathan as "a counsellor, a wise man, and a scribe") implies a settled center from which counsel may flow. When the center is unsettled, the wise counselor refers, postpones, or briefly explains and asks for a different time.

Kuna upande mmoja zaidi wa muda na mahali unaostahili kutajwa waziwazi, kwa sababu kushindwa hapa kumeharibu huduma za kichungaji: uhusiano wa mchungaji na nyumba yake mwenyewe na hali yake mwenyewe. Mshauri anayeinuka kutoka kubishana na mkewe ili kumpokea mshauriwa mlangoni amechagua muda mbaya, hata kama miadi ilikuwa imepangwa. Mshauri ambaye hajalala na anatafuta kahawa ili aendelee kuwa macho amechagua muda mbaya. Mshauri ambaye nyumba yake mwenyewe iko katika msukosuko lazima afikiri kama yeye ndiye mtu sahihi kwa saa hii mahususi. Cheo cha kibiblia cha mshauri (1 Mambo ya Nyakati 27:32 inamtaja Yonathani kuwa "mshauri, mtu mwenye akili, tena mwandishi") kinaashiria kitovu kilichotulia ambacho kutoka kwake shauri linaweza kutiririka. Kitovu hicho kisipotulia, mshauri mwenye hekima humpeleka mtu kwa mwingine, huahirisha, au hueleza kwa ufupi na kuomba muda mwingine.

Equally, a counselor must guard against the temptation to receive counselees at all hours under the guise of availability. Pastors who answer the phone at midnight habitually train their congregation to call at midnight habitually. Boundaries on time are an act of love both for the counselor's family and for the counselee, who needs a counselor whose mind is whole rather than exhausted.

Vivyo hivyo, mshauri lazima ajilinde dhidi ya kishawishi cha kupokea washauriwa saa zote kwa kisingizio cha kupatikana. Wachungaji ambao kwa mazoea hujibu simu saa sita usiku huwafundisha washirika wao kwa mazoea kupiga simu saa sita usiku. Mipaka ya muda ni tendo la upendo kwa familia ya mshauri na kwa mshauriwa pia, ambaye anahitaji mshauri mwenye akili timamu badala ya akili iliyochoka.

When the time and the place have been settled, the counselor has built a vessel that can hold what is about to be poured into it. The grief, the rage, the confusion, the confession that will pour out in the next steps need a container. The container is what you build in Step One.

Muda na mahali vikishaamuliwa, mshauri amejenga chombo kinachoweza kushika kile kitakachomiminwa ndani yake. Huzuni, ghadhabu, mkanganyiko, na maungamo yatakayomiminika katika hatua zinazofuata yanahitaji chombo. Chombo hicho ndicho unachokijenga katika Hatua ya Kwanza.

Step 10 — Provide Closure
Hatua ya 10 — Hitimisha
"We have done our work. Let us close it well."
"Tumeifanya kazi yetu. Na tuihitimishe vizuri."
10.1 Why Closure Matters
10.1 Kwa Nini Kuhitimisha ni Muhimu

A counseling session that simply ends — that runs out of time, that fades into goodbye, that lets the counselee walk away without a clear marker — has done less than it could. A counseling relationship that is allowed to dissolve gradually rather than to conclude deliberately tends to produce dependency rather than growth. Step Ten exists because closure is itself a form of ministry. The counselor who knows how to begin a counseling relationship well must also know how to end one well. Drakeford taught that the final minutes of a session and the final session of a counseling relationship are pastoral moments of unique importance. Done badly, closure leaves the counselee uncertain whether he has been helped, what he is supposed to do next, whether he may return, and whether anything has actually changed. Done well, closure consolidates everything that has come before. It seals the work. It sends the counselee out with clarity, with confidence, and with the assurance that the Lord who has been present in the counseling room will be present in the days to come.

Kikao cha ushauri kinachoisha tu — kinachokwisha muda, kinachofifia hadi kuagana, kinachomwacha mshauriwa aondoke bila alama iliyo wazi ya mwisho — kimefanya kidogo kuliko kilivyoweza. Uhusiano wa ushauri unaoachwa ufifie polepole badala ya kuhitimishwa kwa makusudi huelekea kuzaa utegemezi badala ya ukuaji. Hatua ya Kumi ipo kwa sababu kuhitimisha chenyewe ni namna ya huduma. Mshauri anayejua jinsi ya kuuanza vizuri uhusiano wa ushauri lazima pia ajue jinsi ya kuumaliza vizuri. Drakeford alifundisha kwamba dakika za mwisho za kikao na kikao cha mwisho cha uhusiano wa ushauri ni nyakati za kichungaji zenye umuhimu wa pekee. Kuhitimisha kukifanywa vibaya humwacha mshauriwa bila uhakika kama amesaidiwa, anapaswa kufanya nini baadaye, kama anaweza kurudi, na kama kuna chochote kimebadilika kwa kweli. Kukifanywa vizuri, kuhitimisha huimarisha na kuunganisha kila kitu kilichotangulia. Huitia kazi muhuri. Humtuma mshauriwa akiwa na uwazi, akiwa na ujasiri, na akiwa na uhakika kwamba Bwana aliyekuwapo katika chumba cha ushauri atakuwapo katika siku zijazo.
10.2 Summarizing the Work
10.2 Kufupisha Kazi

The first task of closure is summary. The counselor briefly retraces the path the counseling has walked. "When you came in, the situation was this. We listened together. We clarified what was actually going on. You acknowledged your part in it. We considered the alternatives and explored what each one would produce. You chose this action. We have prepared you to take it." The counselee hears this summary and recognizes himself in it. The work, which during the process may have felt scattered, becomes coherent. The counselee can describe to himself, and later to others, what he and his counselor accomplished. Drakeford observed that counselees who could articulate their own counseling story were far more stable in their gains than those who had been helped but could not say how. Summary makes the help nameable. The counselor's brief retracing is not for his own satisfaction; it is for the counselee's lasting clarity.

Kazi ya kwanza ya kuhitimisha ni muhtasari. Mshauri kwa ufupi hufuatilia tena njia ambayo ushauri umeipitia. "Ulipoingia, hali ilikuwa hivi. Tulisikiliza pamoja. Tulifafanua kile kilichokuwa kikiendelea kwa kweli. Ulikiri sehemu yako ndani yake. Tulizifikiria njia mbadala na kuchunguza kila moja ingezaa nini. Ulichagua tendo hili. Tumekuandaa kulitekeleza." Mshauriwa anasikia muhtasari huu na anajitambua ndani yake. Kazi, ambayo wakati wa mchakato huenda ilionekana kutawanyika, inakuwa na mpangilio unaoeleweka. Mshauriwa anaweza kujieleza mwenyewe, na baadaye kuwaeleza wengine, kile ambacho yeye na mshauri wake walikitimiza. Drakeford aliona kwamba washauriwa walioweza kuieleza hadithi yao wenyewe ya ushauri walikuwa imara zaidi sana katika mafanikio yao kuliko wale waliosaidiwa lakini hawakuweza kusema jinsi gani. Muhtasari huufanya msaada uweze kutajwa kwa jina. Ufuatiliaji huu mfupi wa mshauri si kwa ajili ya kujiridhisha mwenyewe; ni kwa ajili ya uwazi wa kudumu wa mshauriwa.
10.3 Confirming the Action Plan
10.3 Kuthibitisha Mpango wa Utekelezaji

The second task of closure is confirmation. The counselor names again the specific action the counselee has committed to take, when he will take it, and what he will do if he encounters difficulty. "You will speak with your wife on Saturday morning. You will use the words we rehearsed. If you find yourself unable, you will pray the prayer we wrote together and try again. If after one week the conversation has not occurred, you will call me." This explicit naming binds the counselee to his commitment in a way that vague intentions never do. The counselor may also write the commitment on a card the counselee carries away. Drakeford was a strong advocate of written confirmation; he believed paper held what memory often dropped. The counselee who leaves with a card in his pocket bearing the action, the date, and the contingency plan is a counselee who is more likely to do the work he came to do.

Kazi ya pili ya kuhitimisha ni uthibitisho. Mshauri hutaja tena tendo mahususi ambalo mshauriwa amejitoa kulifanya, atalifanya lini, na atafanya nini akikutana na ugumu. "Utazungumza na mke wako Jumamosi asubuhi. Utatumia maneno tuliyoyafanyia mazoezi. Ukijikuta huwezi, utaomba ombi tuliloliandika pamoja na kujaribu tena. Ikiwa baada ya wiki moja mazungumzo hayajafanyika, utanipigia simu." Kutaja huku kwa wazi humfunga mshauriwa kwa ahadi yake kwa namna ambayo nia zisizo wazi hazifanyi kamwe. Mshauri anaweza pia kuiandika ahadi hiyo kwenye kadi ambayo mshauriwa anaibeba kwenda nayo. Drakeford alikuwa mtetezi mkubwa wa uthibitisho wa maandishi; aliamini kwamba karatasi huhifadhi kile ambacho kumbukumbu mara nyingi hukiangusha. Mshauriwa anayeondoka akiwa na kadi mfukoni mwake yenye tendo, tarehe, na mpango wa dharura ni mshauriwa ambaye ana uwezekano mkubwa zaidi wa kuifanya kazi aliyokuja kuifanya.
10.4 The Spiritual Closure: Prayer
10.4 Kuhitimisha Kiroho: Maombi

No biblical counseling session should end without prayer. This is not a ritual addendum; it is a structural element of Christian counsel. The counselor and counselee, having done together the work of human reasoning, scriptural reflection, and practical planning, now together commit the work to God. The counselor prays. He thanks the Lord for what has happened in the session. He asks God's strength for the action that lies ahead. He prays for the counselee by name. He prays for those whom the action will affect. He commits the outcome — whatever it may prove to be — into God's sovereign hands. Then, where appropriate, he invites the counselee to pray. The counselee's prayer, however halting, is itself a form of integrity therapy: it places the counselee's commitment in the hearing of God. James wrote, "Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much" (Jas 5:16). The closing prayer is the final and indispensable act of Step Ten.

Hakuna kikao cha ushauri wa kibiblia kinachopaswa kuisha bila maombi. Hii si nyongeza ya kidesturi tu; ni sehemu ya muundo wa ushauri wa Kikristo. Mshauri na mshauriwa, wakiwa wamefanya pamoja kazi ya kufikiri kibinadamu, ya kutafakari Maandiko, na ya kupanga kivitendo, sasa kwa pamoja wanaikabidhi kazi hiyo kwa Mungu. Mshauri huomba. Humshukuru Bwana kwa yale yaliyotokea katika kikao. Huomba nguvu za Mungu kwa ajili ya tendo lililo mbele. Humwombea mshauriwa kwa jina lake. Huwaombea wale ambao tendo hilo litawagusa. Hukabidhi matokeo — yoyote yatakayokuwa — mikononi mwa enzi ya Mungu. Kisha, inapofaa, humkaribisha mshauriwa aombe. Ombi la mshauriwa, hata likiwa la kusitasita, lenyewe ni namna ya tiba ya uadilifu (integrity therapy): huiweka ahadi ya mshauriwa masikioni mwa Mungu. Yakobo aliandika, "Ungameni dhambi zenu ninyi kwa ninyi, mkaombeane, mpate kuponywa. Kuomba kwake mwenye haki kwafaa sana, akiomba kwa bidii" (Yak 5:16). Ombi la kufunga ni tendo la mwisho na lisiloweza kuachwa la Hatua ya Kumi.
10.5 Releasing the Counselee
10.5 Kumwachilia Mshauriwa

Finally, closure releases. The counselor sends the counselee out — out of the office, out of the counseling relationship, back into the ordinary stream of his life. The counselee is not the counselor's possession. He has been entrusted to the counselor for a season, and that season ends. The wise counselor avoids two opposite errors. The first is releasing too soon: cutting the counselee loose before the work is done, leaving him with a half-finished plan and no support. The second is releasing too late: keeping the counselee in counsel beyond what the situation requires, fostering dependency that the counselee should already have outgrown. Drakeford taught that the goal of counseling is the counselee's restored capacity to live without the counselor. The good counselor works himself out of a job. He releases the counselee with confidence, with affection, and with a clear word: "Go. The Lord goes with you. If you need me again, you know where I am. But you do not need me in order to do what you are now equipped to do." With that, the counseling closes, and the counselee walks back into his life — different, equipped, accountable, and held by the One who never closes the door upon His own. The work of the ten steps is complete. The counselor finishes Step Ten, and he is done.

Mwishowe, kuhitimisha humwachilia mtu. Mshauri humtuma mshauriwa nje — nje ya ofisi, nje ya uhusiano wa ushauri, kurudi katika mkondo wa kawaida wa maisha yake. Mshauriwa si mali ya mshauri. Amekabidhiwa kwa mshauri kwa kipindi fulani, na kipindi hicho kinaisha. Mshauri mwenye hekima huepuka makosa mawili yanayopingana. La kwanza ni kumwachilia mapema mno: kumwacha mshauriwa kabla kazi haijakamilika, akiwa na mpango uliokamilika nusu na bila msaada wowote. La pili ni kumwachilia kwa kuchelewa mno: kumbakiza mshauriwa katika ushauri zaidi ya kile ambacho hali inahitaji, akikuza utegemezi ambao mshauriwa angepaswa tayari kuwa ameuvuka. Drakeford alifundisha kwamba lengo la ushauri ni uwezo uliorejeshwa wa mshauriwa wa kuishi bila mshauri. Mshauri mwema hujiondolea kazi yake mwenyewe. Humwachilia mshauriwa kwa ujasiri, kwa upendo, na kwa neno lililo wazi: "Nenda. Bwana anakwenda pamoja nawe. Ukinihitaji tena, unajua nilipo. Lakini hunihitaji ili ufanye kile ambacho sasa umeandaliwa kukifanya." Kwa hilo, ushauri unafungwa, na mshauriwa anarudi katika maisha yake — akiwa tofauti, ameandaliwa, mwenye kuwajibika, na akiwa ameshikwa na Yule ambaye kamwe hawafungii mlango walio wake. Kazi ya hatua kumi imekamilika. Mshauri anamaliza Hatua ya Kumi, naye amemaliza.
