Listen — "Why Don't You Tell Me About It?"
Sikiliza — "Kwa Nini Usinieleze Habari Yake?"
Two-thirds of every session belongs to the counselee's voice. The counselor's first work is silence.
Theluthi mbili za kila kikao ni za sauti ya mshauriwa. Kazi ya kwanza ya mshauri ni ukimya.
2.1 The Theology of Listening
2.1 Theolojia ya Kusikiliza

The counselee comes to you with a story. He may have rehearsed parts of it; other parts will be told for the first time. Most troubled people carry a sense of profound isolation — a settled belief that no one cares enough to attend to them. The first restoration the counselor offers is not advice, not Scripture, not solution. It is undivided attention. James 1:19 commands the believer to be "swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath." This sequence is not accidental. Hearing precedes speaking, and speaking precedes the strong feeling that, if it comes first, prevents the hearing from happening at all.

Mshauriwa anakujia na habari yake. Huenda amezirudia rudia sehemu zake moyoni; sehemu nyingine zitasimuliwa kwa mara ya kwanza. Watu wengi wenye taabu hubeba hisia ya upweke mzito — imani iliyotulia kwamba hakuna anayejali vya kutosha kuwasikiliza. Urejesho wa kwanza ambao mshauri hutoa si ushauri, si Maandiko, si suluhisho. Ni usikivu usiogawanyika. Yakobo 1:19 inamwamuru mwamini kuwa "mwepesi wa kusikia, si mwepesi wa kusema, wala si mwepesi wa hasira." Mfuatano huu si wa bahati mbaya. Kusikia hutangulia kusema, na kusema hutangulia hisia kali ambayo, ikija kwanza, huzuia kusikia kusitokee kabisa.

Drakeford's rule of thumb — and it is one of the most quoted of his rules — is that the counselor should spend two-thirds of the session listening. This is harder than it sounds. The trained pastor has answers. He carries Scripture in his bones, has heard a thousand variations on the problems before him, and feels physical pressure to begin teaching, exhorting, correcting. The discipline of Step Two is to suppress that pressure long enough for the counselee's actual story to emerge. The story you hear in the first ten minutes is rarely the story that needs counseling. The real story, the story buried under shame and confusion and protective layers, only emerges when the counselee senses that you are not in a hurry to fix him.

Kanuni ya jumla ya Drakeford — nayo ni miongoni mwa kanuni zake zinazonukuliwa sana — ni kwamba mshauri anapaswa kutumia theluthi mbili za kikao akisikiliza. Hili ni gumu kuliko linavyosikika. Mchungaji aliyefunzwa ana majibu. Huyabeba Maandiko mifupani mwake, amesikia namna elfu za matatizo yaliyo mbele yake, na huhisi shinikizo la kimwili la kuanza kufundisha, kuonya, kusahihisha. Nidhamu ya Hatua ya Pili ni kulizuia shinikizo hilo kwa muda wa kutosha ili habari halisi ya mshauriwa ijitokeze. Habari unayoisikia katika dakika kumi za kwanza mara chache ndiyo habari inayohitaji ushauri. Habari halisi, iliyozikwa chini ya aibu na mkanganyiko na matabaka ya kujilinda, hujitokeza tu pale mshauriwa anapohisi kwamba huna haraka ya kumrekebisha.
2.2 The Open Question
2.2 Swali Lililo Wazi

The session opens with an invitation: "Why don't you tell me about it?" or "Tell me what brings you here today." Note what these openings have in common: they are open-ended. They cannot be answered with yes or no. They make room for the counselee to begin where he chooses, at the pace he chooses, with the level of detail he chooses. Closed questions — "Are you having trouble at home?" — narrow the conversation prematurely and force the counselee to confirm or deny a frame the counselor has supplied.

Kikao hufunguliwa kwa mwaliko: "Kwa nini usinieleze habari yake?" au "Nieleze ni nini kimekuleta hapa leo." Angalia kile ambacho mafungua haya yanafanana: ni ya wazi. Hayawezi kujibiwa kwa ndiyo au hapana. Yanampa mshauriwa nafasi ya kuanzia anapopachagua, kwa kasi anayoichagua, kwa kiwango cha undani anachokichagua. Maswali yaliyofungwa — "Una matatizo nyumbani?" — huyabana mazungumzo mapema mno na humlazimisha mshauriwa kukubali au kukana mfumo ambao mshauri ameuleta.

As the counselee speaks, the counselor's verbal contribution should be minimal but encouraging: "Yes," "Go on," "Tell me more," "I understand you to be saying…" These short verbal cues — what one psychologist called the "Rogerian grunt" — communicate presence without redirecting the flow. Body language carries the heavier load: lean forward slightly, maintain warm eye contact without staring, nod at appropriate intervals, keep your hands open and visible rather than crossed.

Mshauriwa anapozungumza, mchango wa maneno wa mshauri unapaswa kuwa mdogo lakini wa kutia moyo: "Ndiyo," "Endelea," "Nieleze zaidi," "Nakuelewa ukisema kwamba…" Ishara hizi fupi za maneno — kile ambacho mwanasaikolojia mmoja alikiita "mguno wa Rogers" — huwasilisha uwepo bila kubadilisha mkondo wa mazungumzo. Lugha ya mwili hubeba mzigo mzito zaidi: inama mbele kidogo, dumisha kumtazama machoni kwa uchangamfu bila kumkodolea macho, tikisa kichwa kwa vipindi vinavyofaa, weka mikono yako wazi na ionekane badala ya kuikunja.
2.3 Five Attitudes Behind a Response (Porter)
2.3 Mitazamo Mitano Iliyo Nyuma ya Jibu (Porter)

Elias Porter identified five basic attitudes that lie behind almost everything a counselor says. Awareness of these attitudes prevents the most common errors of Step Two. The first is evaluative: a response that signals judgment of right or wrong, appropriate or inappropriate. Counselees who hear evaluative responses too early stop telling the truth. The second is interpretive: a response that imposes the counselor's meaning on the counselee's experience ("What you really mean is…"). Used prematurely, this short-circuits the counselee's own discovery. The third is supportive: a response intended to soothe and reduce intensity ("It will be all right"). In crisis counseling some support is appropriate, but excessive reassurance teaches the counselee that you cannot bear his actual pain. The fourth is probing: a response that seeks more information ("How long has this been going on?"). Probing is useful in moderation, but if it dominates, the session becomes an interrogation. The fifth is understanding: a response that seeks to enter the counselee's frame and check that you have heard correctly ("So as you see it, your husband's promotion has actually made you feel more invisible?"). The understanding response is the gold standard of Step Two.

Elias Porter alitambua mitazamo mitano ya msingi iliyo nyuma ya karibu kila kitu anachosema mshauri. Kuifahamu mitazamo hii huzuia makosa ya kawaida zaidi ya Hatua ya Pili. Wa kwanza ni wa kutathmini: jibu linaloashiria hukumu ya haki au kosa, linalofaa au lisilofaa. Washauriwa wanaosikia majibu ya kutathmini mapema mno huacha kusema ukweli. Wa pili ni wa kufasiri: jibu linalolazimisha maana ya mshauri juu ya uzoefu wa mshauriwa ("Unachomaanisha hasa ni…"). Likitumika mapema mno, hukatiza ugunduzi wa mshauriwa mwenyewe. Wa tatu ni wa kutegemeza: jibu linalokusudiwa kutuliza na kupunguza ukali ("Mambo yatakuwa sawa"). Katika ushauri wa dharura kiasi fulani cha kutegemeza kinafaa, lakini kutuliza kupita kiasi humfundisha mshauriwa kwamba huwezi kuyavumilia maumivu yake halisi. Wa nne ni wa kudadisi: jibu linalotafuta habari zaidi ("Jambo hili limekuwa likiendelea kwa muda gani?"). Kudadisi kunafaa kwa kiasi, lakini kukitawala, kikao hugeuka kuwa mahojiano ya kiupelelezi. Wa tano ni wa kuelewa: jibu linalotafuta kuingia katika mfumo wa mshauriwa na kuhakikisha kwamba umesikia sawasawa ("Kwa hiyo kama unavyoona wewe, kupandishwa cheo kwa mumeo kwa kweli kumekufanya ujihisi kutoonekana zaidi?"). Jibu la kuelewa ndilo kipimo bora kabisa cha Hatua ya Pili.

To these five Porter's interpreters add two more: confronting (which has its place but rarely in Step Two) and paraphrasing (a close cousin of understanding). The counselor who learns to deploy understanding and paraphrase as his primary moves, with sparing use of probing and almost no use of evaluating or interpreting, will find that counselees tell him things they have never told anyone.

Kwa mitazamo hii mitano wafafanuzi wa Porter huongeza miwili zaidi: wa kukabili (ambao una nafasi yake lakini mara chache katika Hatua ya Pili) na wa kurudia kwa maneno mengine (ndugu wa karibu wa kuelewa). Mshauri anayejifunza kutumia kuelewa na kurudia kwa maneno mengine kama hatua zake kuu, akidadisi kwa kiasi kidogo na karibu kutotathmini wala kufasiri kabisa, atakuta kwamba washauriwa wanamweleza mambo ambayo hawajawahi kumweleza mtu yeyote.
2.4 The Sound of Silence
2.4 Sauti ya Ukimya

Haddon Robinson observed that silence is part of listening, not a gap to be filled. When a counselee pauses, resist the impulse to speak. Thirty seconds of silence will feel like five minutes to the inexperienced counselor; he will be tempted to rescue the silence with a question or a comment. Do not. The counselee is often closest to a breakthrough during a long pause, gathering courage to say the thing he came to say. If you fill the silence, he loses it.

Haddon Robinson aliona kwamba ukimya ni sehemu ya kusikiliza, si pengo la kujazwa. Mshauriwa anapotulia kimya, zuia msukumo wa kusema. Sekunde thelathini za ukimya zitaonekana kama dakika tano kwa mshauri asiye na uzoefu; atajaribiwa kuuokoa ukimya kwa swali au maoni. Usifanye hivyo. Mara nyingi mshauriwa yuko karibu kabisa na mafanikio ya ghafla wakati wa kituo kirefu, akikusanya ujasiri wa kusema lile jambo alilokuja kulisema. Ukiujaza ukimya, analipoteza.

Tears in counseling are also a form of speech. When a counselee weeps, do not rush to dry the tears with reassurance. Pass the tissue, wait, and ask gently when the moment has passed: "What were the tears about?" Sometimes tears come from grief, sometimes from anger, sometimes from a relief so deep the counselee did not know he was holding it. The patient counselor learns the difference. The hurried counselor never finds out.

Machozi katika ushauri nayo ni namna ya kusema. Mshauriwa anapolia, usiharakishe kuyafuta machozi kwa maneno ya kutuliza. Mpe karatasi ya kufutia machozi, ngoja, na wakati huo ukishapita uliza kwa upole: "Machozi yale yalihusu nini?" Wakati mwingine machozi hutokana na huzuni, wakati mwingine na hasira, wakati mwingine na faraja ya kina kiasi kwamba mshauriwa hakujua alikuwa ameishikilia. Mshauri mvumilivu hujifunza tofauti. Mshauri mwenye haraka kamwe hagundui.
2.5 The Body That Listens
2.5 Mwili Unaosikiliza

Listening is not done with the ears alone. The counselee reads the counselor's body before he reads the counselor's words. A counselor who says "Go on" while glancing at his phone has not said "Go on" — he has said "I am partly here." The counselee will respond to what the body said, not what the mouth said, and will withdraw the deeper material he had been preparing to disclose.

Kusikiliza hakufanywi kwa masikio peke yake. Mshauriwa huusoma mwili wa mshauri kabla hajasoma maneno ya mshauri. Mshauri anayesema "Endelea" huku akitupia jicho simu yake hajasema "Endelea" — amesema "Niko hapa kwa sehemu tu." Mshauriwa ataitikia kile ambacho mwili ulisema, si kile ambacho kinywa kilisema, na atayarudisha mambo ya ndani zaidi aliyokuwa akijiandaa kuyafunua.

The disciplines of bodily listening are simple but unnatural for many. Sit slightly forward, not slumped back. Make steady but soft eye contact — not a stare that interrogates, but a gaze that signals you are present. Let your face respond to what the counselee says, but do not perform expressions you do not feel; honest puzzlement is better than rehearsed concern. Keep your hands quiet. Do not check the clock; if you must, do so deliberately and aloud ("Let me see how we are doing on time"). The body confesses what the mouth disguises, and the counselee always hears the body first.

Nidhamu za kusikiliza kwa mwili ni rahisi lakini si za kawaida kwa wengi. Keti ukiinama mbele kidogo, si ukiwa umejilaza nyuma. Mtazame machoni kwa uthabiti lakini kwa upole — si kukodolea macho kunakohoji, bali mtazamo unaoashiria kwamba upo. Uso wako uitikie kile anachosema mshauriwa, lakini usiigize hisia usizozihisi; mshangao wa kweli ni bora kuliko wasiwasi wa kuigiza. Weka mikono yako tulivu. Usiangalie saa; kama ni lazima, fanya hivyo kwa makusudi na kwa sauti ("Hebu nione tunaendeleaje na muda"). Mwili hukiri kile ambacho kinywa hukificha, na mshauriwa daima husikia mwili kwanza.

A useful self-test: at the end of the day, can you recall the counselee's clothing, posture, gestures, and the changes in his voice as he spoke? If you cannot, you were watching for an opening to speak rather than receiving what he gave. The counselee will have felt this even if he could not name it. Bodily listening is not a technique; it is the form love takes when one person sits with another in pain.

Kipimo cha kujipima chenye manufaa: mwisho wa siku, je, unaweza kukumbuka mavazi ya mshauriwa, mkao wake, ishara za mikono yake, na mabadiliko ya sauti yake alipokuwa akizungumza? Kama huwezi, ulikuwa ukivizia nafasi ya kusema badala ya kupokea kile alichokupa. Mshauriwa atakuwa ameliona hili hata kama hakuweza kulitaja. Kusikiliza kwa mwili si mbinu; ni umbo ambalo upendo huchukua pale mtu mmoja anapoketi na mwingine katika maumivu.
2.6 The Dangers of Listening
2.6 Hatari za Kusikiliza

Listening sounds passive but is dangerous in ways the new counselor does not anticipate. The first danger is that the counselee's story will stir material in the counselor that the counselor has not yet faced. A man counseling another man on marital betrayal may discover his own marriage tightening at home that night. A woman counseling a young mother through postpartum depression may find her own old grief over a lost child rising unbidden. The Spirit can use these resonances to deepen empathy, but only if the counselor recognizes what is happening. The counselor who does not recognize it begins, subtly, to manage the counselee's story for the sake of his own peace. He steers away from the material that touches him too closely. He gives advice that is more for himself than for the one in front of him. The counselee, sensing the shift, withdraws.

Kusikiliza kunasikika kama jambo la kutulia tu lakini ni hatari kwa njia ambazo mshauri mpya hazitarajii. Hatari ya kwanza ni kwamba habari ya mshauriwa itachochea ndani ya mshauri mambo ambayo mshauri bado hajayakabili. Mwanamume anayemshauri mwanamume mwingine kuhusu usaliti wa ndoa anaweza kugundua ndoa yake mwenyewe ikikaza nyumbani usiku ule. Mwanamke anayemshauri mama kijana katika sonona ya baada ya kujifungua anaweza kukuta huzuni yake ya zamani juu ya mtoto aliyempoteza ikiibuka bila kualikwa. Roho Mtakatifu anaweza kutumia mwangwi huu ili kuongeza huruma, lakini tu ikiwa mshauri anatambua kinachotokea. Mshauri asiyetambua huanza, kwa siri, kuisimamia habari ya mshauriwa kwa ajili ya amani yake mwenyewe. Huyakwepa mambo yanayomgusa karibu mno. Hutoa ushauri ulio zaidi kwa ajili yake mwenyewe kuliko kwa ajili ya yule aliye mbele yake. Mshauriwa, akihisi badiliko hilo, hujirudisha nyuma.

The second danger is the temptation to enjoy being needed. A counselee in pain offers the counselor a position of importance the counselor's ordinary life does not provide. To be received with such trust, to hear secrets no one else hears, to be told that this conversation matters — these are pleasures, and pleasures corrupt. The counselor begins to extend sessions, to invite further disclosure than the case requires, to feel diminished when the counselee no longer needs him. Drakeford's two-thirds rule has a hidden ascetic function here: by disciplining the counselor toward silence, it disciplines him toward the recognition that the conversation is not for him.

Hatari ya pili ni kishawishi cha kufurahia kuhitajika. Mshauriwa aliye katika maumivu humpa mshauri nafasi ya umuhimu ambayo maisha ya kawaida ya mshauri hayampi. Kupokelewa kwa imani kama hiyo, kusikia siri ambazo hakuna mwingine anayezisikia, kuambiwa kwamba mazungumzo haya ni muhimu — hizi ni anasa, na anasa huharibu. Mshauri huanza kurefusha vikao, kualika kujifunua zaidi kuliko jambo lenyewe linavyohitaji, kujihisi amepunguzwa mshauriwa asipomhitaji tena. Kanuni ya theluthi mbili ya Drakeford ina kazi iliyofichika ya kujinyima hapa: kwa kumwadibisha mshauri kuelekea ukimya, humwadibisha kuelekea kutambua kwamba mazungumzo si kwa ajili yake.

The third danger is the slow erosion of the counselor's home life. Hours spent absorbing the heaviest material of others must be balanced by hours of restoration with God, with family, with rest. A counselor who finishes the workday emptied into his counselees and arrives at the dinner table with nothing left has loved the counselee at the expense of his wife and children — and that exchange is not, in the long run, a Christian act.

Hatari ya tatu ni mmomonyoko wa polepole wa maisha ya nyumbani ya mshauri. Saa zinazotumika kupokea mizigo mizito kabisa ya wengine lazima zisawazishwe na saa za kurejeshwa pamoja na Mungu, pamoja na familia, pamoja na mapumziko. Mshauri anayemaliza siku ya kazi akiwa amejimimina kwa washauriwa wake na kufika mezani kwa chakula cha jioni bila kitu chochote kilichobaki amempenda mshauriwa kwa gharama ya mkewe na watoto wake — na mabadilishano hayo, kwa muda mrefu, si tendo la Kikristo.

3.1 Why Clarification Matters
3.1 Kwa Nini Kufafanua Ni Muhimu

After listening, the counselor faces a temptation to act on the first version of the story he has heard. Resist this. The story a counselee tells in the first ten or fifteen minutes is often a rehearsal — a version polished for public consumption, missing the elements that bring shame, fear, or confusion. The work of Step Three is to gently dig beneath the rehearsed version to the events, feelings, and meanings that actually generate the distress. Without this clarification, the counselor risks spending the entire session addressing a problem the counselee did not really come to discuss.

Baada ya kusikiliza, mshauri hukabili kishawishi cha kutenda kwa msingi wa toleo la kwanza la hadithi aliyoisikia. Kipinge kishawishi hiki. Hadithi ambayo mshauriwa husimulia katika dakika kumi au kumi na tano za kwanza mara nyingi ni mazoezi — toleo lililong'arishwa ili lisikike vizuri mbele ya watu, likikosa yale mambo yanayoleta aibu, hofu, au mkanganyiko. Kazi ya Hatua ya Tatu ni kuchimba kwa upole chini ya toleo hilo lililozoezwa hadi kufikia matukio, hisia, na maana ambazo kwa kweli ndizo zinazozaa dhiki. Bila ufafanuzi huu, mshauri yuko hatarini kutumia kikao kizima akishughulikia tatizo ambalo mshauriwa hakuja kwa kweli kulijadili.

Drakeford illustrated this with the story of a man who told his pastor he would convert to Christianity if the pastor could only explain where Cain got his wife. The pastor was tempted to launch into a careful explanation of Genesis 4. Instead, he asked clarifying questions and discovered that the man's actual struggle was not theological at all: he was in an adulterous relationship with another man's wife, and his "Cain's wife" question was a deflection from the real moral crisis he could not name. Had the pastor solved the presenting problem, he would have missed the soul.

Drakeford alilieleza jambo hili kwa hadithi ya mtu mmoja aliyemwambia mchungaji wake kwamba angekuwa Mkristo kama tu mchungaji angeweza kumweleza Kaini alimpata wapi mke wake. Mchungaji alishawishika kuanza maelezo ya makini juu ya Mwanzo 4. Badala yake, aliuliza maswali ya kufafanua, akagundua kwamba mapambano halisi ya mtu huyo hayakuwa ya kitheolojia hata kidogo: alikuwa katika uhusiano wa uzinzi na mke wa mtu mwingine, na swali lake la "mke wa Kaini" lilikuwa njia ya kukwepa mgogoro halisi wa kimaadili ambao hakuweza kuutaja. Kama mchungaji angelitatua tatizo lililowasilishwa, angeikosa nafsi ya mtu huyo.
3.2 Three Things That Need Clarifying
3.2 Mambo Matatu Yanayohitaji Kufafanuliwa

There are three layers at which clarification typically operates. The first is words and phrases. A counselee may use language that makes perfect sense to him but is opaque to you. "Things just aren't right between us." Things meaning what? Communication? Sexual intimacy? Financial decisions? In-laws? You will not know unless you ask: "Just what do you mean by 'things aren't right'?" Or: "I'm not sure I follow. Tell me more about that." Counselees often use vague language because the precise language is too painful or too shameful to speak aloud. The patient request for clarity gives them permission to find more honest words.

Kuna matabaka matatu ambamo ufafanuzi kwa kawaida hufanya kazi. La kwanza ni maneno na misemo. Mshauriwa anaweza kutumia lugha inayoeleweka kabisa kwake lakini isiyoeleweka kwako. "Mambo hayako sawa kati yetu." Mambo kwa maana gani? Mawasiliano? Ukaribu wa kimapenzi? Maamuzi ya fedha? Wakwe? Hutajua usipouliza: "Unamaanisha nini hasa unaposema 'mambo hayako sawa'?" Au: "Sina uhakika kama nimekuelewa. Niambie zaidi kuhusu jambo hilo." Mara nyingi washauriwa hutumia lugha isiyo wazi kwa sababu lugha iliyo sahihi inaumiza mno au ni ya aibu mno kuitamka kwa sauti. Ombi la subira la kutaka uwazi huwapa ruhusa ya kutafuta maneno ya kweli zaidi.

The second layer is order of events. People in distress narrate poorly. They jump from yesterday to a memory from childhood to a phone call last week. This jumbled chronology often contains the key to the problem — the counselee has unconsciously linked events that the counselor must learn to see linked too. But you cannot work with the chronology until you can see it. "Could we go back? When did this start? What happened first?" These questions help both of you assemble a coherent timeline.

Tabaka la pili ni mpangilio wa matukio. Watu walio katika dhiki husimulia vibaya. Wanaruka kutoka jana hadi kumbukumbu ya utotoni, kisha hadi simu ya wiki iliyopita. Mfuatano huu uliochanganyika mara nyingi una ufunguo wa tatizo — mshauriwa ameyaunganisha matukio bila kujitambua, na mshauri lazima ajifunze kuyaona yakiwa yameunganishwa vivyo hivyo. Lakini huwezi kuufanyia kazi mfuatano wa matukio mpaka uweze kuuona. "Je, tunaweza kurudi nyuma? Jambo hili lilianza lini? Nini kilitokea kwanza?" Maswali haya huwasaidia ninyi wawili kuunda mfuatano wa matukio unaoeleweka.

The third layer, and the most important, is the real problem. The presenting problem is the one the counselee names when he sits down. The real problem is often a layer or two beneath. A wife may present "marital communication" when the real problem is that she discovered her husband's pornography use six months ago and has not told him she knows. A teenager may present "stress at school" when the real problem is sexual abuse by an uncle. A pastor may present "burnout" when the real problem is loss of faith. The counselor learns to ask, after the presenting problem has been described: "I was wondering — could there be something else troubling you that hasn't come up yet?" This invitation, offered without pressure, often opens the door to what the counselee actually came to say.

Tabaka la tatu, na lililo muhimu zaidi, ni tatizo halisi. Tatizo linalowasilishwa ni lile ambalo mshauriwa hulitaja anapoketi. Tatizo halisi mara nyingi liko tabaka moja au mawili chini yake. Mke anaweza kuwasilisha "mawasiliano katika ndoa" ilhali tatizo halisi ni kwamba miezi sita iliyopita aligundua kwamba mumewe anatazama ponografia, na hajamwambia kwamba anajua. Kijana anaweza kuwasilisha "msongo wa mawazo shuleni" ilhali tatizo halisi ni kunyanyaswa kingono na mjomba wake. Mchungaji anaweza kuwasilisha "uchovu wa kupindukia" ilhali tatizo halisi ni kupoteza imani. Mshauri hujifunza kuuliza, baada ya tatizo linalowasilishwa kuelezwa: "Nilikuwa najiuliza — je, huenda kuna jambo jingine linalokusumbua ambalo bado halijajitokeza?" Mwaliko huu, ukitolewa bila shinikizo, mara nyingi hufungua mlango wa kile ambacho mshauriwa kwa kweli alikuja kusema.
3.3 When to Be Direct
3.3 Wakati wa Kusema Moja kwa Moja

Most of Step Three is gentle and non-directive. There are moments, however, when the counselee is hedging so substantially that gentleness has become evasion. In such cases the counselor may need to be direct: "Will you please explain just what your relationship has to do with your brother's sister-in-law?" or "I notice that every time we approach the subject of your father, you change the topic. Could we stay there a moment?" Directness in Step Three should be specific, non-accusatory, and always offered with the option for the counselee to decline.

Sehemu kubwa ya Hatua ya Tatu ni ya upole na isiyo ya kuelekeza. Hata hivyo, kuna nyakati ambapo mshauriwa anazunguka-zunguka kiasi kikubwa hivi kwamba upole umegeuka kuwa ukwepaji. Katika hali kama hizo mshauri anaweza kuhitaji kusema moja kwa moja: "Tafadhali, unaweza kueleza hasa uhusiano wako una nini cha kufanya na shemeji wa kaka yako?" au "Ninaona kwamba kila mara tunapokaribia habari ya baba yako, unabadilisha mada. Je, tunaweza kukaa hapo kwa muda kidogo?" Kusema moja kwa moja katika Hatua ya Tatu kunapaswa kuwe mahususi, kusiko kwa kushtaki, na daima kutolewe pamoja na nafasi ya mshauriwa kukataa.

A particular form of clarification involves what counselees call themselves. A counselee who repeatedly says "I'm just a wreck" or "I'm hopeless" is using language that needs examination. Where did this self-description come from? Whose voice is it really? Often the counselee is repeating language from a parent, a spouse, or a critical inner voice that has nothing to do with how God sees him. The counselor's clarification of self-naming language is one of the most healing moves in the whole ten-step process.

Aina moja maalum ya ufafanuzi inahusu jinsi washauriwa wanavyojiita. Mshauriwa anayesema mara kwa mara "Mimi nimeharibika kabisa" au "Mimi sina tumaini" anatumia lugha inayohitaji kuchunguzwa. Maelezo haya juu yake mwenyewe yalitoka wapi? Kwa kweli ni sauti ya nani? Mara nyingi mshauriwa anarudia maneno ya mzazi, ya mwenzi wa ndoa, au ya sauti ya ndani yenye kukosoa ambayo haihusiani kamwe na jinsi Mungu anavyomwona. Mshauri anapofafanua lugha hii ambayo mtu hujiita nayo, anafanya mojawapo ya mambo yenye kuponya zaidi katika mchakato mzima wa hatua kumi.
3.4 Suspending Judgment
3.4 Kusimamisha Hukumu

The discipline that holds Step Three together is the suspension of judgment. Until you have clarified the situation, you do not know enough to evaluate it. A counselor who jumps to conclusions in Step Three almost always lands on the wrong conclusion, and once landed, finds it hard to revise. Wait. Ask one more question. Listen to one more layer. The wisdom literature counsels exactly this: "He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him" (Proverbs 18:13).

Nidhamu inayoishikilia Hatua ya Tatu pamoja ni kusimamisha hukumu. Mpaka uwe umeifafanua hali, hujui vya kutosha kuweza kuitathmini. Mshauri anayekimbilia hitimisho katika Hatua ya Tatu karibu kila mara hufikia hitimisho lisilo sahihi, na akishalifikia, huona vigumu kulirekebisha. Ngoja. Uliza swali moja zaidi. Sikiliza tabaka moja zaidi. Maandiko ya hekima yanashauri jambo hili hasa: "Yeye ajibuye kabla hajasikia, Ni upumbavu na aibu kwake" (Mithali 18:13).

When the situation has been clarified — when you understand the words, the order of events, and the real problem rather than the presenting one — Step Three is complete. Sometimes this clarification takes ten minutes; sometimes it takes three sessions. Do not be in a hurry to leave it. Every step that follows depends on the accuracy of the picture you build here.

Hali ikishafafanuliwa — unapoelewa maneno, mpangilio wa matukio, na tatizo halisi badala ya lile linalowasilishwa — Hatua ya Tatu imekamilika. Wakati mwingine ufafanuzi huu huchukua dakika kumi; wakati mwingine huchukua vikao vitatu. Usiwe na haraka ya kuiacha. Kila hatua inayofuata inategemea usahihi wa picha unayoijenga hapa.
3.5 The Three Layers in Practice
3.5 Matabaka Matatu Katika Utendaji

Step Three clarifies three layers: the facts (what actually happened), the feelings (what the counselee felt about what happened), and the meaning (what the counselee made of it). Vague counselees collapse all three into a single statement. The phrase "My boss humiliated me at the meeting" is doing three jobs at once: asserting a fact (something happened at the meeting), naming an emotion (humiliation), and assigning a meaning (the boss intended harm). The counselor's task is to separate the layers gently.

Hatua ya Tatu hufafanua matabaka matatu: ukweli wa mambo (kilichotokea hasa), hisia (kile mshauriwa alichohisi kuhusu kilichotokea), na maana (kile mshauriwa alichohitimisha kutokana nacho). Washauriwa wasioeleza mambo wazi huyabana yote matatu katika kauli moja. Kauli "Bosi wangu alinidhalilisha kwenye mkutano" inafanya kazi tatu kwa wakati mmoja: inathibitisha ukweli (jambo fulani lilitokea kwenye mkutano), inataja hisia (kudhalilishwa), na inatoa maana (bosi alikusudia kumdhuru). Kazi ya mshauri ni kuyatenganisha matabaka haya kwa upole.

Begin with facts. "Walk me through the meeting — who was there, what was being discussed, and what specifically did your boss say?" Often the recounted facts will already shift the picture. The boss did not call him a fool; the boss asked a sharp question in front of others. Sharp questions in front of others can humiliate, but they can also clarify, and the counselee's certainty about intent may not survive the actual words.

Anza na ukweli wa mambo. "Nieleze mkutano ulivyokwenda hatua kwa hatua — nani walikuwepo, nini kilikuwa kikijadiliwa, na bosi wako alisema nini hasa?" Mara nyingi ukweli unaosimuliwa utaanza tayari kubadilisha picha. Bosi hakumwita mpumbavu; bosi aliuliza swali kali mbele ya wengine. Maswali makali mbele ya wengine yanaweza kudhalilisha, lakini yanaweza pia kufafanua, na uhakika wa mshauriwa kuhusu nia ya bosi huenda usisimame mbele ya maneno yaliyosemwa hasa.

Then move to feelings — not "How did that make you feel?" which sounds clinical, but "When he said that, what was happening inside you?" The counselee may name humiliation first, but careful listening often reveals layers beneath: shame at being seen as incompetent, fear of being fired, anger at a long pattern, grief over a once-good working relationship. Each of these requires different counsel.

Kisha nenda kwenye hisia — si kwa kuuliza "Jambo hilo lilikufanya ujisikieje?" ambalo linasikika la kitabibu, bali "Aliposema hivyo, nini kilikuwa kikiendelea ndani yako?" Mshauriwa anaweza kutaja kudhalilishwa kwanza, lakini kusikiliza kwa makini mara nyingi hufunua matabaka yaliyo chini yake: aibu ya kuonekana kuwa hana uwezo, hofu ya kufukuzwa kazi, hasira juu ya mtindo wa muda mrefu, huzuni juu ya uhusiano wa kikazi uliokuwa mzuri zamani. Kila mojawapo ya haya linahitaji shauri tofauti.

Finally, the meaning: "What did you conclude from that moment?" Now the counselee tells you what the experience meant — that his boss is against him, that his job is in danger, that he is a failure. Meanings can be true or false. The counselor cannot evaluate the meaning until he has separated it from the facts and the feelings. Clarification is what makes that separation possible.

Mwishowe, maana: "Ulihitimisha nini kutokana na wakati ule?" Sasa mshauriwa anakueleza uzoefu ule ulimaanisha nini — kwamba bosi wake yuko kinyume naye, kwamba kazi yake iko hatarini, kwamba yeye ni mtu aliyeshindwa. Maana zinaweza kuwa za kweli au za uongo. Mshauri hawezi kuitathmini maana mpaka aitenganishe na ukweli wa mambo na hisia. Ufafanuzi ndio unaowezesha utenganisho huo.
3.6 The Counselor's Own Clarity
3.6 Uwazi wa Mshauri Mwenyewe

Clarification is two-sided. While the counselor works to clarify the counselee's situation, he must also remain clear about his own. A tired counselor distorts what he hears. A counselor who has fought with his wife that morning will project marital tension into a story that did not contain it. A counselor with a strong theological prejudgment will hear the data that confirms his prejudgment and miss the data that disconfirms it. The clarification of the counselee's situation is only as good as the counselor's clarity about his own state.

Ufafanuzi una pande mbili. Wakati mshauri anafanya kazi ya kufafanua hali ya mshauriwa, lazima pia abaki na uwazi kuhusu hali yake mwenyewe. Mshauri aliyechoka hupotosha anachosikia. Mshauri aliyegombana na mke wake asubuhi ile ataingiza mvutano wa ndoa katika hadithi ambayo haikuwa nao. Mshauri mwenye hukumu ya awali yenye nguvu ya kitheolojia atasikia habari zinazothibitisha hukumu yake ya awali na kukosa zile zinazoikanusha. Ufafanuzi wa hali ya mshauriwa ni mzuri tu kadiri ya uwazi wa mshauri kuhusu hali yake mwenyewe.

Drakeford recommended a brief discipline before each session: a moment of stillness, a short prayer, an honest acknowledgment of one's own preoccupations, and a deliberate setting of them aside for the duration of the conversation. If something is too heavy to set aside, the counselor must consider whether he is the right person for this particular hour, or whether the appointment should be rescheduled. The pastor who refuses to face his own state will inevitably project it onto every counselee he sees.

Drakeford alipendekeza nidhamu fupi kabla ya kila kikao: muda mfupi wa utulivu, sala fupi, kukiri kwa uaminifu mambo yanayoushughulisha moyo wake mwenyewe, na kuyaweka kando kwa makusudi kwa muda wote wa mazungumzo. Ikiwa jambo fulani ni zito mno kuweza kuwekwa kando, mshauri lazima afikirie kama yeye ndiye mtu sahihi kwa saa hii mahususi, au kama miadi inapaswa kupangwa upya. Mchungaji anayekataa kuikabili hali yake mwenyewe bila shaka ataihamishia kwa kila mshauriwa anayemwona.

There is also a longer-term clarity the counselor owes himself. The pastor whose own marriage is in unaddressed conflict cannot do marital counseling well. The pastor whose own children are estranged from him cannot easily counsel a parent in similar grief. The pastor's continuing self-examination — with his wife, with a fellow pastor, with the Lord — is part of pastoral preparation, not separate from it. A counselor who has clarified his own situation is far less likely to confuse it with his counselee's.

Pia kuna uwazi wa muda mrefu ambao mshauri anawajibika kujipatia. Mchungaji ambaye ndoa yake mwenyewe iko katika mgogoro usioshughulikiwa hawezi kufanya ushauri wa ndoa vizuri. Mchungaji ambaye watoto wake mwenyewe wamejitenga naye hawezi kwa urahisi kumshauri mzazi aliye katika huzuni kama hiyo. Kujichunguza kwa mchungaji kunakoendelea — pamoja na mke wake, pamoja na mchungaji mwenzake, pamoja na Bwana — ni sehemu ya maandalizi ya kichungaji, si jambo lililotengwa nayo. Mshauri aliyeifafanua hali yake mwenyewe ana uwezekano mdogo sana wa kuichanganya na ile ya mshauriwa wake.

Hatua ya Nne · Awamu ya 1: Tambua Tatizo
Investigate Previous Counseling
Chunguza Ushauri wa Awali
"What other people have you talked to about this?" — what sounds like a simple question protects both counselor and counselee.
"Ni watu gani wengine uliozungumza nao kuhusu jambo hili?" — kinachosikika kama swali rahisi humlinda mshauri na mshauriwa pia.
4.1 Why This Step Exists
4.1 Kwa Nini Hatua Hii Ipo

At first glance, the question "What other people have you talked to about this?" appears almost rude — as if you are checking the counselee's loyalty or accusing him of shopping for help. It is neither. It is one of the most pastorally protective steps in the entire ten-step model, and the counselor who skips it does so at the peril of both himself and the counselee.

Kwa mtazamo wa kwanza, swali "Ni watu gani wengine uliozungumza nao kuhusu jambo hili?" linaonekana karibu kuwa la kukosa adabu — kana kwamba unapima uaminifu wa mshauriwa au unamshtaki kwamba anazunguka akitafuta msaada kama mtu anayezunguka sokoni. Si mojawapo ya hayo. Ni mojawapo ya hatua zenye ulinzi mkubwa zaidi wa kichungaji katika mfumo mzima wa hatua kumi, na mshauri anayeiruka anafanya hivyo kwa hatari yake mwenyewe na ya mshauriwa.

There are three distinct reasons to ask this question, and each justifies the awkwardness of asking it. The first is to determine the seriousness of the situation. A person who has spoken about a problem to no one, sought help from no one, and is now sitting in your office for the first time, is presenting a fresh wound. A person who has consulted three pastors, two professional counselors, his wife's sister, and a radio host before sitting in your office is presenting something different. The pattern of help-seeking tells you about the severity, the duration, and the counselee's relationship to authority.

Kuna sababu tatu tofauti za kuuliza swali hili, na kila moja inahalalisha usumbufu wa kuliuliza. Ya kwanza ni kubaini uzito wa hali. Mtu ambaye hajazungumza na yeyote kuhusu tatizo, hajatafuta msaada kwa yeyote, na sasa ameketi ofisini mwako kwa mara ya kwanza, anawasilisha jeraha jipya. Mtu ambaye ameshauriana na wachungaji watatu, washauri wawili wa kitaaluma, dada wa mke wake, na mtangazaji wa redio kabla ya kuketi ofisini mwako anawasilisha kitu tofauti. Mtindo wa kutafuta msaada unakueleza kuhusu ukali wa tatizo, muda ambao limedumu, na uhusiano wa mshauriwa na mamlaka.

The second reason is to identify what Drakeford called the "therapy gypsy" — the counselee who moves from helper to helper, never accepting any one perspective long enough for it to do its work. Therapy gypsies are not bad people; they are usually deeply wounded people whose pattern of shopping itself reflects an inability to trust. But the counselor who does not recognize the pattern will be drawn into it, will offer his best wisdom, and will watch the counselee leave to take that wisdom to the next pastor and complain that none of the helpers really understand. Recognizing the pattern allows you to address it directly: "I notice that you've spoken with quite a few people about this. I wonder what makes it hard to settle on one helper. Could we talk about that?"

Sababu ya pili ni kumtambua yule ambaye Drakeford alimwita "mhamaji wa tiba" — mshauriwa anayehama kutoka kwa msaidizi mmoja hadi mwingine, bila kamwe kukubali mtazamo wowote mmoja kwa muda wa kutosha ili ufanye kazi yake. Wahamaji wa tiba si watu wabaya; kwa kawaida ni watu waliojeruhiwa sana ambao mtindo wao wa kuzunguka-zunguka wenyewe unaonyesha kushindwa kuamini. Lakini mshauri asiyeutambua mtindo huu atavutwa ndani yake, atatoa hekima yake bora, na kumtazama mshauriwa akiondoka kuipeleka hekima hiyo kwa mchungaji anayefuata na kulalamika kwamba hakuna msaidizi hata mmoja anayemwelewa kwa kweli. Kuutambua mtindo huu kunakuwezesha kuushughulikia moja kwa moja: "Ninaona kwamba umezungumza na watu wengi kabisa kuhusu jambo hili. Ninajiuliza ni nini kinachofanya iwe vigumu kutulia kwa msaidizi mmoja. Je, tunaweza kuzungumza kuhusu hilo?"
4.2 When the Problem Is Beyond You
4.2 Wakati Tatizo Liko Nje ya Uwezo Wako

The third reason is the most important: this question reveals when the problem is beyond your competence. A counselee who has been seen by three psychiatrists, has been hospitalized twice, and is currently on multiple medications is not someone who simply needs another pastor's wisdom. He needs ongoing professional care, possibly coordinated with pastoral support, but not pastoral counseling as the primary modality. The honest counselor learns the limits of his own competence and refers when the situation calls for expertise he does not have.

Sababu ya tatu ndiyo iliyo muhimu zaidi: swali hili hufunua wakati tatizo liko nje ya uwezo wako. Mshauriwa ambaye ameonwa na madaktari bingwa wa magonjwa ya akili watatu, amelazwa hospitalini mara mbili, na kwa sasa anatumia dawa nyingi si mtu anayehitaji tu hekima ya mchungaji mwingine. Anahitaji huduma ya kitaaluma inayoendelea, labda ikiratibiwa pamoja na msaada wa kichungaji, lakini si ushauri wa kichungaji kama njia kuu ya matibabu. Mshauri mwaminifu hujifunza mipaka ya uwezo wake mwenyewe na humpa mtu rufaa pale hali inapohitaji utaalamu ambao yeye hana.

Drakeford's list of categories that warrant referral rather than continued counseling is worth memorizing: significant or repeated suicide gestures (refer immediately); chronic alcoholism or substance abuse where medical detoxification may be needed; someone who wants only a passive role in his own healing; someone with an unrealistic fantasy of an omnipotent pastor who will magically solve everything; chronic psychiatric problems including psychosis or psychopathy; and someone currently seeing another counselor without that counselor's knowledge of this consultation. Each of these situations places demands on the counselor that exceed pastoral competence in most cases. To proceed without referral is to do harm in the name of help.

Orodha ya Drakeford ya makundi yanayostahili rufaa badala ya kuendelea na ushauri inafaa kukaririwa: majaribio ya kujiua yaliyo makubwa au yanayojirudia (mpe rufaa mara moja); ulevi sugu au matumizi mabaya ya dawa za kulevya ambapo huenda ikahitajika kuondoa sumu mwilini kwa usimamizi wa kitabibu; mtu anayetaka kuwa na nafasi ya kupokea tu, bila kushiriki, katika uponyaji wake mwenyewe; mtu mwenye ndoto isiyo halisi ya mchungaji mwenye uwezo wote atakayetatua kila kitu kimiujiza; matatizo sugu ya akili yakiwemo saikosisi (kupoteza uhalisia) au saikopathia (ugonjwa wa haiba usio na dhamiri); na mtu ambaye kwa sasa anaonana na mshauri mwingine bila mshauri huyo kujua kuhusu mashauriano haya. Kila mojawapo ya hali hizi linaweka juu ya mshauri madai yanayozidi uwezo wa kichungaji katika visa vingi. Kuendelea bila rufaa ni kuleta madhara kwa jina la kusaidia.
4.3 Spiritual Versus Professional Need
4.3 Hitaji la Kiroho Dhidi ya Hitaji la Kitaaluma

There is a category Drakeford handled with particular wisdom: the counselee who has been to many secular counselors but whose problem is fundamentally spiritual. A man who has been treated for depression for two years and shows no improvement may be wrestling with unconfessed sin, unforgiveness toward a parent, or a crisis of meaning that no medication can address. The pastor who recognizes this is offering something the secular counselor genuinely cannot: an understanding that the human being is not merely a psychological organism but a spiritual being created in the image of God, capable of guilt that requires absolution, capable of grief that requires hope.

Kuna kundi moja ambalo Drakeford alilishughulikia kwa hekima ya pekee: mshauriwa ambaye amewaona washauri wengi wasio wa kidini lakini ambaye tatizo lake kimsingi ni la kiroho. Mtu ambaye ametibiwa sonona kwa miaka miwili bila kuonyesha nafuu yoyote huenda anapambana na dhambi isiyoungamwa, kutosamehe kwa mzazi, au mgogoro wa maana ya maisha ambao hakuna dawa inayoweza kuushughulikia. Mchungaji anayelitambua hili anatoa kitu ambacho mshauri asiye wa kidini kwa kweli hawezi kutoa: uelewa kwamba mwanadamu si kiumbe cha kisaikolojia tu bali ni kiumbe cha kiroho kilichoumbwa kwa sura ya Mungu, mwenye uwezo wa kuwa na hatia inayohitaji ondoleo, mwenye uwezo wa kuwa na huzuni inayohitaji tumaini.

Conversely, a counselee whose problem appears spiritual on the surface — "I can't pray anymore," "God feels distant" — may actually be suffering from clinical depression, hormonal imbalance, untreated grief, or chronic exhaustion. The wise counselor does not assume that every problem brought to a pastor is a pastoral problem. Sometimes the most pastoral act is to refer to a physician, a Christian therapist, or a specialist in trauma.

Kinyume chake, mshauriwa ambaye tatizo lake linaonekana kwa juu juu kuwa la kiroho — "Siwezi kuomba tena," "Mungu anaonekana yuko mbali" — huenda kwa kweli anateseka na sonona ya kitabibu, kutokuwa na uwiano wa homoni, huzuni ya msiba isiyoshughulikiwa, au uchovu sugu. Mshauri mwenye hekima hadhani kwamba kila tatizo linaloletwa kwa mchungaji ni tatizo la kichungaji. Wakati mwingine tendo la kichungaji zaidi ni kumpa mtu rufaa kwa daktari, kwa mtaalamu wa tiba ya nafsi Mkristo, au kwa mtaalamu wa kiwewe.
4.4 The Posture of Referral
4.4 Msimamo wa Kutoa Rufaa

When you must refer, refer well. A bad referral feels to the counselee like rejection — "Even the pastor won't help me." A good referral feels like care — "My pastor took my problem seriously enough to send me to someone who can really help." The difference lies almost entirely in your manner. Name the referral with confidence, not apology: "I think the help you need is more than I can give in this office, and I want you to have the best help available. I would like to refer you to Dr. Martinez, who is excellent with this kind of situation. I will continue to walk with you spiritually, and you and I can keep meeting if that helps. The professional help and the pastoral help work together."

Unapolazimika kutoa rufaa, itoe vizuri. Rufaa mbaya humhisisha mshauriwa kama kukataliwa — "Hata mchungaji hataki kunisaidia." Rufaa nzuri huhisiwa kama kujali — "Mchungaji wangu alilichukulia tatizo langu kwa uzito kiasi cha kunipeleka kwa mtu anayeweza kunisaidia kwa kweli." Tofauti iko karibu yote katika namna yako. Itaje rufaa kwa uhakika, si kwa kuomba radhi: "Nadhani msaada unaouhitaji ni zaidi ya ninaoweza kuutoa katika ofisi hii, na ninataka upate msaada bora unaopatikana. Ningependa kukupeleka kwa Dkt. Martinez, ambaye ni hodari sana katika hali za aina hii. Nitaendelea kutembea nawe kiroho, na mimi na wewe tunaweza kuendelea kukutana ikiwa hilo linasaidia. Msaada wa kitaaluma na msaada wa kichungaji hufanya kazi pamoja."

A referral is not the end of pastoral care. It is the beginning of coordinated care. Stay in the counselee's life. Pray for him. Ask how the other appointments are going. Many a counselee has been saved as much by the pastor who walked alongside him through professional treatment as by the treatment itself.

Rufaa si mwisho wa huduma ya kichungaji. Ni mwanzo wa huduma iliyoratibiwa. Baki katika maisha ya mshauriwa. Mwombee. Muulize jinsi miadi mingine inavyoendelea. Washauriwa wengi wameokolewa kwa kiasi kikubwa na mchungaji aliyetembea pamoja nao katika matibabu ya kitaaluma kama walivyookolewa na matibabu yenyewe.
4.5 When Not to Refer
4.5 Wakati wa Kutotoa Rufaa

If referral is sometimes pastoral wisdom, premature referral is sometimes pastoral cowardice. A pastor who refers every counselee with a hard problem has confused his office with a switchboard. The ordinary work of pastoral counseling — marital conflict, grief, financial worry, vocational decision, conviction over sin, family rupture, anxiety, ordinary discouragement — is competent pastoral territory. These are the matters Drakeford's ten steps were built for. Sending such counselees away because they are "too complex" is failure of nerve disguised as humility.

Ikiwa rufaa wakati mwingine ni hekima ya kichungaji, rufaa ya mapema mno wakati mwingine ni woga wa kichungaji. Mchungaji anayempa rufaa kila mshauriwa mwenye tatizo gumu amechanganya wadhifa wake na swichibodi (kituo cha kuunganisha simu). Kazi ya kawaida ya ushauri wa kichungaji — mgogoro wa ndoa, huzuni ya msiba, wasiwasi wa fedha, uamuzi wa kazi au wito, kuhukumiwa moyoni kwa sababu ya dhambi, kuvunjika kwa familia, wasiwasi, kuvunjika moyo kwa kawaida — ni eneo la uwezo wa kichungaji. Haya ndiyo mambo ambayo hatua kumi za Drakeford zilijengwa kwa ajili yake. Kuwafukuza washauriwa kama hao kwa sababu mambo yao ni "magumu mno" ni kukosa ujasiri kunakojificha kama unyenyekevu.

There are also categories where premature referral does specific harm. The counselee who comes seeking spiritual counsel about a moral failure does not need to be sent to a psychologist; he needs the pastor to walk him through repentance. The wife who comes to talk about a difficult marriage does not need a marital therapist before she has had even one pastoral conversation about her own contribution. The young man considering his calling needs the wisdom of an older believer, not a vocational counselor. To refer such counselees out of the room is to refuse the office to which the Lord called the pastor.

Pia kuna makundi ambamo rufaa ya mapema mno huleta madhara mahususi. Mshauriwa anayekuja kutafuta shauri la kiroho kuhusu anguko la kimaadili hahitaji kupelekwa kwa mwanasaikolojia; anahitaji mchungaji amwongoze katika toba. Mke anayekuja kuzungumza kuhusu ndoa ngumu hahitaji mtaalamu wa tiba ya ndoa kabla hajapata hata mazungumzo moja ya kichungaji kuhusu mchango wake mwenyewe. Kijana anayefikiria wito wake anahitaji hekima ya mwamini aliye mzee kuliko yeye, si mshauri wa masuala ya kazi. Kuwapeleka washauriwa kama hao nje ya chumba ni kuukataa wadhifa ambao Bwana alimwitia mchungaji.

The right test is not "Is this hard?" but "Is this outside my competence, or am I outside my courage?" Some difficulties require referral; many require only that the pastor stay in the room and do the slow work that the office actually demands. The pastor who knows the difference is rare and valuable. The pastor who refers in fear is more common, and his congregation slowly learns not to bring him their real problems.

Kipimo sahihi si "Je, hili ni gumu?" bali "Je, hili liko nje ya uwezo wangu, au mimi niko nje ya ujasiri wangu?" Baadhi ya magumu yanahitaji rufaa; mengi yanahitaji tu kwamba mchungaji abaki chumbani na kufanya kazi ya polepole ambayo wadhifa wake unadai kwa kweli. Mchungaji anayejua tofauti hii ni nadra na wa thamani. Mchungaji anayetoa rufaa kwa hofu ni wa kawaida zaidi, na kusanyiko lake hujifunza polepole kutomletea matatizo yao halisi.
4.6 The Politics of Previous Counselors
4.6 Siasa za Washauri wa Awali

Step Four often surfaces complicated material about counselors the counselee has seen before. He may speak well of some, badly of others, and ambivalently of most. He is watching to see what you will do with what he says. If you join him in disparaging his last counselor, you have taught him that pastors speak ill of one another behind their backs — and you have begun the relationship by demonstrating that you will eventually do the same of him. He may laugh with you in the moment, but he will be less open afterward.

Hatua ya Nne mara nyingi huibua mambo tata kuhusu washauri ambao mshauriwa amewaona hapo awali. Anaweza kuwasema baadhi vizuri, wengine vibaya, na wengi wao kwa hisia mchanganyiko. Anakutazama kuona utafanya nini na anachokisema. Ukiungana naye kumdharau mshauri wake wa mwisho, umemfundisha kwamba wachungaji husemana vibaya nyuma ya migongo yao — na umeuanza uhusiano kwa kuonyesha kwamba mwishowe utamfanyia yeye vivyo hivyo. Anaweza kucheka pamoja nawe wakati huo, lakini baadaye atakuwa mwazi kidogo zaidi.

The discipline is honor for absent helpers, even when their work was imperfect. "It sounds like Pastor Lopez tried hard. I wonder what you wish had been different." This redirects the conversation from blame onto useful material — what the counselee was looking for, what he did not receive — without joining in criticism. If the previous counselor genuinely did something harmful, the counselee will need that named, but you can name harm without contempt: "What you describe was a real failure on his part. I am sorry. That should not have happened."

Nidhamu hapa ni kuwaheshimu wasaidizi wasiokuwepo, hata kazi yao ilipokuwa na kasoro. "Inaonekana Mchungaji Lopez alijitahidi sana. Ninajiuliza ungetamani nini kingekuwa tofauti." Hili huyaelekeza mazungumzo kutoka kwenye lawama kwenda kwenye mambo yenye manufaa — kile mshauriwa alichokuwa akitafuta, kile ambacho hakukipokea — bila kujiunga katika ukosoaji. Ikiwa mshauri wa awali kwa kweli alifanya jambo lenye madhara, mshauriwa atahitaji jambo hilo litajwe, lakini unaweza kutaja madhara bila dharau: "Unachokieleza kilikuwa kushindwa halisi kwa upande wake. Samahani sana. Jambo hilo halikupaswa kutokea."

Sometimes Step Four will reveal a deeper pattern: the counselee has consulted seven pastors, four therapists, and his uncle, and has left each one as soon as the conversation turned toward his own responsibility. This pattern, recognized gently, is itself a piece of pastoral material. "I notice that each of these helpers eventually said something similar to you, and you eventually left each one. I'm wondering whether the same thing will happen between you and me when I say what they said. Could we name that possibility now, so we are not surprised when it comes?" This is brave Step Four work that earlier steps rarely permit.

Wakati mwingine Hatua ya Nne itafunua mtindo ulio ndani zaidi: mshauriwa ameshauriana na wachungaji saba, wataalamu wa tiba wanne, na mjomba wake, na amemwacha kila mmoja mara tu mazungumzo yalipogeukia uwajibikaji wake mwenyewe. Mtindo huu, ukitambuliwa kwa upole, wenyewe ni sehemu ya malighafi ya kichungaji. "Ninaona kwamba kila mmoja wa wasaidizi hawa mwishowe alikuambia jambo linalofanana, na wewe mwishowe ulimwacha kila mmoja. Ninajiuliza kama jambo lile lile litatokea kati yako na mimi nitakaposema kile walichosema. Je, tunaweza kulitaja uwezekano huo sasa, ili tusishangae utakapokuja?" Hii ni kazi ya ujasiri ya Hatua ya Nne ambayo hatua za awali mara chache huiruhusu.

Uwajibikaji — "Ni Wapi Ulipokosea?"
The shift from listening to action begins here. Drakeford called this the heart of Integrity Therapy.
Mabadiliko kutoka kusikiliza kwenda kutenda yanaanzia hapa. Drakeford aliita hatua hii kiini cha Tiba ya Uadilifu (Integrity Therapy).
5.1 The Pivot of the Model
5.1 Bawaba ya Mbinu Hii

Step Five is the hinge of the entire ten-step model. Steps One through Four belong to Stage One: identifying the problem. Step Five opens Stage Two: determining what to do about it. It is here that the counseling shifts from listening to acting, from receiving the story to working within it. And the door through which that shift happens is the question of responsibility.

Hatua ya Tano ni bawaba ya mbinu nzima ya hatua kumi. Hatua ya Kwanza hadi ya Nne ni za Awamu ya Kwanza: kulitambua tatizo. Hatua ya Tano inafungua Awamu ya Pili: kuamua la kufanya kuhusu tatizo hilo. Ni hapa ambapo ushauri unahama kutoka kusikiliza kwenda kutenda, kutoka kuipokea simulizi kwenda kufanya kazi ndani yake. Na mlango ambao mabadiliko hayo hupitia ni swali la uwajibikaji.

Drakeford was clear that this question must come at the right moment. Asked too early, before the counselee has been heard and the problem clarified, "Where have you failed?" sounds like accusation and the counselee will close. Asked at the right moment — after Steps One through Four have been completed — the same question comes as an invitation to ownership and freedom. The counselee has been heard. The problem has been clarified. Previous helps have been investigated. The counselee now knows that you understand the situation. Now, and only now, is the question of responsibility ready to be asked.

Drakeford alisisitiza kwamba swali hili lazima liulizwe wakati unaofaa. Likiulizwa mapema mno, kabla mshauriwa hajasikilizwa na tatizo halijafafanuliwa, swali "Ni wapi ulipokosea?" husikika kama shtaka, na mshauriwa atajifunga. Likiulizwa wakati unaofaa — baada ya Hatua ya Kwanza hadi ya Nne kukamilika — swali lilo hilo huja kama mwaliko wa kukubali jukumu lake na kupata uhuru. Mshauriwa amesikilizwa. Tatizo limefafanuliwa. Misaada ya awali imechunguzwa. Sasa mshauriwa anajua kwamba unaielewa hali yake. Sasa, na sasa tu, swali la uwajibikaji liko tayari kuulizwa.
5.2 The Theology of Personal Responsibility
5.2 Teolojia ya Uwajibikaji wa Mtu Binafsi

Behind this step stands a particular theological conviction: that human beings are made in the image of God and are therefore responsible agents, not merely victims of circumstance. Modern therapeutic culture has trained an entire generation to locate the source of every problem outside the self — in parents, in society, in trauma, in brain chemistry. Each of these factors is real, and the wise counselor does not dismiss them. But none of them removes the moral agency of the person sitting in your office. To treat a counselee as if his problem were entirely the fault of others is to deny him the dignity of being a moral being. It is also to lock him in his suffering, because what others did to him cannot be changed, but what he himself does going forward is the only territory in which change is possible.

Nyuma ya hatua hii kuna imani mahususi ya kitheolojia: kwamba wanadamu wameumbwa kwa sura ya Mungu, na kwa hiyo ni watendaji wenye kuwajibika, si wahanga tu wa mazingira. Utamaduni wa kisasa wa tiba umefundisha kizazi kizima kutafuta chanzo cha kila tatizo nje ya nafsi — kwa wazazi, katika jamii, katika majeraha ya kiakili (trauma), katika kemikali za ubongo. Kila mojawapo ya mambo haya ni halisi, na mshauri mwenye hekima hayapuuzi. Lakini hakuna hata moja linaloondoa uwajibikaji wa kimaadili wa mtu aliyeketi ofisini mwako. Kumtendea mshauriwa kana kwamba tatizo lake ni kosa la wengine kabisa ni kumnyima heshima ya kuwa kiumbe wa kimaadili. Pia ni kumfungia ndani ya mateso yake, kwa sababu yale ambayo wengine walimtendea hayawezi kubadilishwa, bali yale ambayo yeye mwenyewe atatenda kuanzia sasa ndiyo eneo pekee ambamo mabadiliko yanawezekana.

Mowrer and Drakeford developed Integrity Therapy in part as a corrective to this drift. Their conviction was that mental health and moral integrity are connected — that confession of one's own failure, where failure is genuine, is itself therapeutic. A counselee who has been treating his marriage as 100% his wife's fault is in psychological bondage as well as moral evasion. The day he says, "I have been part of this. I have failed in these specific ways," he begins to be free.

Mowrer na Drakeford waliunda Tiba ya Uadilifu kwa sehemu ili kurekebisha mwelekeo huu. Imani yao ilikuwa kwamba afya ya akili na uadilifu wa kimaadili vinahusiana — kwamba kuungama kushindwa kwa mtu mwenyewe, pale ambapo kushindwa huko ni kwa kweli, ni tiba yenyewe. Mshauriwa ambaye amekuwa akiichukulia ndoa yake kuwa kosa la mke wake kwa asilimia 100 yuko katika kifungo cha kisaikolojia pamoja na ukwepaji wa kimaadili. Siku atakaposema, "Mimi nimekuwa sehemu ya jambo hili. Nimeshindwa kwa njia hizi mahususi," anaanza kuwa huru.
5.3 The 80/20 Principle
5.3 Kanuni ya 80/20

Most counselees come to your office convinced they are 100% in the right and the other party is 100% in the wrong. This is rarely true. Even in the most one-sided conflict — and yes, there are situations in which one party genuinely is innocent — there is almost always something the counselee himself has done, or failed to do, that contributed to the situation as it now stands. Drakeford taught his students to use what he called the 80/20 model with resistant counselees. "I understand that you feel your husband is mostly to blame. Suppose for a moment that he is 80% responsible. What would the remaining 20% — your part — look like?" This question is gentler than asking the counselee to admit equal blame, but it accomplishes the same opening. Once the 20% has been named, the counselee has crossed a line; he is no longer entirely innocent in his own account.

Washauriwa wengi huja ofisini mwako wakiwa na hakika kwamba wao wako sahihi kwa asilimia 100 na upande mwingine umekosea kwa asilimia 100. Mara chache hili huwa kweli. Hata katika mgogoro ulioegemea upande mmoja zaidi — na ndiyo, kuna hali ambazo upande mmoja kweli hauna hatia — karibu kila mara kuna jambo ambalo mshauriwa mwenyewe amelitenda, au ameshindwa kulitenda, lililochangia hali ilivyo sasa. Drakeford aliwafundisha wanafunzi wake kutumia kile alichokiita mbinu ya 80/20 kwa washauriwa wakaidi. "Naelewa kwamba unaona mume wako ndiye mwenye lawama kubwa. Tuseme kwa muda kwamba yeye anawajibika kwa asilimia 80. Asilimia 20 iliyobaki — sehemu yako — ingekuwaje?" Swali hili ni la upole zaidi kuliko kumtaka mshauriwa akiri lawama sawa, lakini linafungua mlango uleule. Mara asilimia 20 inapotajwa, mshauriwa amevuka mstari; hayuko tena bila hatia kabisa katika simulizi yake mwenyewe.

A genuinely powerful follow-up question is: "What would it be like to be married to you?" or "What would it be like to be your child?" These questions invite the counselee to imagine his own behavior from the other person's perspective. Many counselees have never done this. The exercise is itself a form of repentance — a turning of the head to see oneself as one's neighbor sees one.

Swali la kufuatia lenye nguvu kweli ni: "Ingekuwaje kuolewa nawe?" (au "kukuoa wewe?") au "Ingekuwaje kuwa mtoto wako?" Maswali haya humwalika mshauriwa kuiwazia tabia yake mwenyewe kwa mtazamo wa mtu mwingine. Washauriwa wengi hawajawahi kufanya hivi. Zoezi hili lenyewe ni aina ya toba — kugeuza kichwa ili kujiona mwenyewe jinsi jirani yako anavyokuona.
5.4 The Exception of Genuine Innocence
5.4 Hali ya Kipekee: Kutokuwa na Hatia kwa Kweli

A pastoral warning belongs here. There are situations in which the counselee is genuinely innocent. A child who was sexually abused did nothing to invite the abuse. A wife whose husband secretly siphoned the family savings is not 20% responsible for being deceived. A worker fired for refusing to participate in fraud is not partly to blame for the firing. The counselor who applies the 80/20 question rigidly to such cases will retraumatize the very people he is trying to help. Discernment is required.

Onyo la kichungaji linafaa hapa. Kuna hali ambazo mshauriwa kweli hana hatia. Mtoto aliyenyanyaswa kingono hakufanya lolote la kuualika unyanyasaji huo. Mke ambaye mume wake kwa siri alichota akiba ya familia hawajibiki kwa asilimia 20 kwa kudanganywa. Mfanyakazi aliyefukuzwa kazi kwa kukataa kushiriki katika udanganyifu hana sehemu ya lawama kwa kufukuzwa. Mshauri anayelitumia swali la 80/20 kwa ukakamavu katika hali kama hizi atawajeruhi upya kiakili (retraumatize) watu wale wale anaojaribu kuwasaidia. Busara (utambuzi) inahitajika.

In cases of genuine innocence, the counselor's task is different. Such counselees often carry false guilt — a feeling that they should have done something to prevent what happened. The counselor's work is not to find their 20%, but to release them from the false 100% they have placed on themselves. "What part do you think you played?" can still be asked, but the answer the counselor expects is not a confession of contribution but an exposure of the irrational guilt the counselee has been carrying. Then comes the assurance: "Nothing you could have done would have prevented this. You are not responsible for what was done to you."

Katika hali za kutokuwa na hatia kwa kweli, kazi ya mshauri ni tofauti. Washauriwa wa namna hii mara nyingi hubeba hatia ya uongo — hisia kwamba walipaswa kufanya jambo fulani kuzuia kilichotokea. Kazi ya mshauri si kutafuta asilimia 20 yao, bali kuwafungua kutoka asilimia 100 ya uongo waliyojitwika wenyewe. "Unadhani wewe ulikuwa na sehemu gani?" bado linaweza kuulizwa, lakini jibu analolitarajia mshauri si kukiri mchango wao, bali kufichuliwa kwa hatia isiyo na msingi ambayo mshauriwa amekuwa akiibeba. Kisha huja uhakikisho: "Hakuna lolote ambalo ungeweza kufanya lingezuia jambo hili. Wewe huwajibiki kwa kile ulichotendewa."

The challenge of Step Five is the discernment to know which kind of counselee is in your office: the resistant one who needs to own his 20%, or the innocent one who needs release from a false 100%. Both need ministry. They need different ministries.

Changamoto ya Hatua ya Tano ni busara ya kujua ni mshauriwa wa aina gani yuko ofisini mwako: yule mkaidi anayehitaji kukubali asilimia 20 yake, au yule asiye na hatia anayehitaji kufunguliwa kutoka asilimia 100 ya uongo. Wote wawili wanahitaji huduma. Wanahitaji huduma tofauti.
5.5 Behavior Before Feeling
5.5 Tabia Kabla ya Hisia

Integrity Therapy carries one further conviction that flows from Step Five: behavior change precedes feeling change, not the other way around. Most counselees arrive believing that if they could just stop feeling angry, lonely, depressed, or afraid, then they could begin acting differently. Drakeford taught the reverse. Begin acting responsibly, and the feelings will follow. "If it is to be, it is up to me to do it." This is not a denial of feelings; it is a recognition that feelings are downstream of action far more often than action is downstream of feeling. Step Five names what the counselee has failed to do and prepares the ground for Step Six, where the counselor will model the kind of action that produces the kind of feeling the counselee is seeking.

Tiba ya Uadilifu ina imani moja zaidi inayotokana na Hatua ya Tano: mabadiliko ya tabia hutangulia mabadiliko ya hisia, si kinyume chake. Washauriwa wengi huja wakiamini kwamba kama wangeweza tu kuacha kuhisi hasira, upweke, sonona, au hofu, basi wangeweza kuanza kutenda tofauti. Drakeford alifundisha kinyume chake. Anza kutenda kwa uwajibikaji, na hisia zitafuata. "Ikiwa jambo hili litatokea, ni juu yangu kulitenda." Huku si kukana hisia; ni kutambua kwamba mara nyingi zaidi hisia hufuata matendo kuliko matendo kufuata hisia. Hatua ya Tano inataja kile ambacho mshauriwa ameshindwa kutenda na kuandaa msingi wa Hatua ya Sita, ambapo mshauri ataonyesha mfano wa aina ya tendo linaloleta aina ya hisia ambayo mshauriwa anaitafuta.

Hatua ya 6 — Onyesha Mfano wa Jukumu
