6.1 The Pivot Into Action
6.1 Kugeuka Kuingia Katika Utendaji

In Step Five the counselee has acknowledged what he has failed to do. He has named his contribution to the problem. The natural and immediate question that follows is, "What now? What does responsible behavior actually look like in my situation?" Step Six answers that question. The counselor stops talking about responsibility in the abstract and begins to embody it. He models the role. He shows, by example and by speech, what the next step looks like in the flesh. Drakeford insisted that talking about new behavior was rarely sufficient; the counselee needed to see it lived. The counselor who has been trained in Integrity Therapy does not stand outside the counselee's struggle as a clinician. He steps into it as a fellow human who has had to do the same kind of difficult thing himself.

Katika Hatua ya Tano mshauriwa amekiri kile ambacho ameshindwa kutenda. Ametaja mchango wake katika tatizo. Swali la kawaida na la papo hapo linalofuata ni, "Sasa nifanye nini? Tabia ya kuwajibika inaonekanaje hasa katika hali yangu?" Hatua ya Sita inajibu swali hilo. Mshauri anaacha kuzungumza kuhusu uwajibikaji kinadharia na kuanza kuuishi. Anaonyesha mfano wa jukumu. Anaonyesha, kwa mfano wake na kwa maneno yake, jinsi hatua inayofuata inavyoonekana katika maisha halisi. Drakeford alisisitiza kwamba kuzungumza kuhusu tabia mpya mara chache kulitosha; mshauriwa alihitaji kuiona ikiishiwa. Mshauri aliyefundishwa katika Tiba ya Uadilifu (Integrity Therapy) hasimami nje ya mapambano ya mshauriwa kama mtaalamu wa kliniki. Anaingia ndani yake kama mwanadamu mwenzake ambaye yeye mwenyewe amelazimika kufanya jambo gumu la aina hiyo hiyo.
6.2 Two Kinds of Modeling
6.2 Aina Mbili za Kuonyesha Mfano

Modeling happens in two ways during a counseling session. The first is self-disclosure: the counselor selectively shares his own struggle with the same kind of issue, and the steps he took toward responsible action. This is not a confessional, and it is not the counselor's session. It is a brief, deliberate window. "When my marriage went through this kind of cold place, I had to swallow my pride and go to my wife and say, 'I have been wrong.' It was the hardest sentence I ever spoke. But the door opened." The counselor models that admitting failure is survivable. Pride lies; it tells the counselee that admission is annihilation. The counselor's lived testimony refutes the lie. Drakeford and Mowrer were emphatic that the counselor must himself walk the integrity path before he asks the counselee to walk it.

Kuonyesha mfano hufanyika kwa njia mbili wakati wa kikao cha ushauri. Ya kwanza ni kujifunua: mshauri kwa kuchagua anashiriki mapambano yake mwenyewe na suala la aina hiyo hiyo, na hatua alizochukua kuelekea tendo la kuwajibika. Huku si kuungama kwake, na si kikao cha mshauri. Ni dirisha fupi, la makusudi. "Ndoa yangu ilipopitia kipindi cha ubaridi kama hiki, ilinibidi nimeze kiburi changu, niende kwa mke wangu na kusema, 'Nimekosea.' Ilikuwa sentensi ngumu kuliko zote nilizowahi kusema. Lakini mlango ulifunguka." Mshauri anaonyesha kwamba kukiri kushindwa kunavumilika. Kiburi husema uongo; humwambia mshauriwa kwamba kukiri ni maangamizi. Ushuhuda wa maisha ya mshauri unakanusha uongo huo. Drakeford na Mowrer walisisitiza kwa nguvu kwamba mshauri lazima yeye mwenyewe aitembee njia ya uadilifu kabla ya kumwomba mshauriwa aitembee.

The second kind of modeling is role-play. The counselor invites the counselee to act out the difficult conversation in the office before he attempts it in real life. "Pretend I am your son. Say to me what you intend to say tomorrow." The counselee speaks. The counselor responds as the son might. The counselee tries again. This rehearsal is not artificial; it is preparation. The man who must apologize to his employer, the wife who must speak honestly to her husband, the parent who must confront a child — each does better when the words have been formed once already in the safety of the counselor's office. Role-play surfaces the counselee's hidden fears, the words that catch in the throat, the postures that betray defensiveness. The counselor coaches.

Aina ya pili ya kuonyesha mfano ni kuigiza nafasi (role-play). Mshauri anamwalika mshauriwa kuigiza mazungumzo magumu humo ofisini kabla ya kuyajaribu katika maisha halisi. "Jifanye mimi ni mwanao. Niambie kile unachokusudia kusema kesho." Mshauriwa anasema. Mshauri anajibu kama mwana angeweza kujibu. Mshauriwa anajaribu tena. Mazoezi haya si ya bandia; ni maandalizi. Mtu anayepaswa kumwomba mwajiri wake msamaha, mke anayepaswa kuzungumza kwa uaminifu na mume wake, mzazi anayepaswa kumkabili mtoto — kila mmoja hufanya vizuri zaidi wakati maneno yamekwisha kuundwa mara moja katika usalama wa ofisi ya mshauri. Kuigiza nafasi huibua hofu zilizofichika za mshauriwa, maneno yanayokwama kooni, na mikao inayofichua kujitetea. Mshauri anafundisha na kuelekeza.
6.3 Modeling Without Pretending Perfection
6.3 Kuonyesha Mfano Bila Kujifanya Mkamilifu

A common pastoral failure is the counselor who models from a pedestal. He speaks of responsible behavior as though he himself had never struggled with it. The counselee, sensing the distance, concludes that responsible behavior is for spiritual professionals and not for ordinary failing humans like himself. The Integrity Therapy counselor models from beside, not from above. He does not parade his sins; he does not turn the session into his own therapy. But he does, when wisdom dictates, acknowledge that he too is a fellow-struggler. Paul wrote, "Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, I press toward the mark" (Phil 3:13–14). That is the apostolic posture. The counselor who can adopt it gives his counselee permission to be human and progressing rather than perfect and arrived.

Kushindwa kwa kawaida kwa kichungaji ni mshauri anayeonyesha mfano akiwa juu ya jukwaa. Anazungumza juu ya tabia ya kuwajibika kana kwamba yeye mwenyewe hajawahi kupambana nayo. Mshauriwa, akihisi umbali huo, anahitimisha kwamba tabia ya kuwajibika ni ya wataalamu wa kiroho na si ya wanadamu wa kawaida wanaoshindwa kama yeye. Mshauri wa Tiba ya Uadilifu huonyesha mfano akiwa kando, si kutoka juu. Haonyeshi dhambi zake kwa kujigamba; hakigeuzi kikao kuwa tiba yake mwenyewe. Lakini, hekima inapoelekeza, anakiri kwamba yeye pia ni mpambanaji mwenzake. Paulo aliandika, "Ndugu zangu, mimi sijihesabu kuwa nimekwisha kushika; ila natenda neno moja tu; nikiyasahau yaliyo nyuma, nikiyachuchumilia yaliyo mbele; nakaza mwendo, niifikilie mede" (Wafilipi 3:13–14). Huo ndio mwenendo wa kitume. Mshauri anayeweza kuuchukua humpa mshauriwa wake ruhusa ya kuwa mwanadamu anayeendelea badala ya kuwa mkamilifu aliyekwisha kufika.
6.4 Pinpointing Desired Behavior
6.4 Kubainisha Tabia Inayotakiwa

Modeling requires precision. The behavior to be modeled cannot be vague. "Be a better husband" cannot be modeled. "Tomorrow morning, before you leave for work, ask your wife what she has on her mind today, and listen for sixty seconds without interrupting" — that can be modeled. The counselor helps the counselee pinpoint the specific, observable, repeatable behavior. The behavior modification literature calls this targeting. Drakeford absorbed it without becoming behaviorist; he insisted that pinpointing was simply biblical specificity. "Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might" (Eccl 9:10). A hand cannot do "betterness." A hand can do a specific named act. The counselor and counselee together name it, the counselor models it, the counselee rehearses it, and the counselee leaves the office equipped not with a vague intention but with a concrete first step.

Kuonyesha mfano kunahitaji usahihi. Tabia inayoonyeshwa haiwezi kuwa ya jumla jumla. "Kuwa mume bora" haiwezi kuonyeshwa kwa mfano. "Kesho asubuhi, kabla hujaondoka kwenda kazini, muulize mke wako ana jambo gani akilini leo, na usikilize kwa sekunde sitini bila kumkatiza" — hilo linaweza kuonyeshwa kwa mfano. Mshauri anamsaidia mshauriwa kubainisha tabia mahususi, inayoonekana, na inayoweza kurudiwa. Maandiko ya urekebishaji wa tabia (behavior modification) huita jambo hili kulenga (targeting). Drakeford aliipokea dhana hii bila kuwa mfuasi wa tabia-pekee (behaviorist); alisisitiza kwamba kubainisha ni umahususi wa kibiblia tu. "Lo lote mkono wako utakaloliona kufanya, ulifanye kwa nguvu zako" (Mhubiri 9:10). Mkono hauwezi kufanya "ubora." Mkono unaweza kufanya tendo mahususi lililotajwa. Mshauri na mshauriwa kwa pamoja wanalitaja, mshauri analionyesha kwa mfano, mshauriwa analifanyia mazoezi, na mshauriwa anaondoka ofisini akiwa ameandaliwa si kwa nia isiyo wazi bali kwa hatua ya kwanza iliyo halisi.
6.5 Christ as the Master Model
6.5 Kristo kama Kielelezo Kikuu

The Christian counselor who models the role is operating under the higher pattern of Christ Himself, who told His disciples, "I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you" (John 13:15). Jesus did not merely instruct the disciples to wash one another's feet; He took the basin and the towel and modeled the role. He did not lecture about love; He laid down His life. The counselor who points his counselee toward Christ-shaped behavior must be willing, in some measure, to walk that pattern in front of the counselee. "Be ye followers of me, even as I also am of Christ" (1 Cor 11:1). Modeling is a Christ-pattern, not merely a technique. When the counselor models humility, forgiveness, patience, or honest speech, he is reproducing in miniature what Christ has done at full scale. The counselee, watching the counselor, is being trained to look past the counselor toward Christ.

Mshauri Mkristo anayeonyesha mfano wa jukumu anafanya kazi chini ya kielelezo cha juu zaidi cha Kristo Mwenyewe, aliyewaambia wanafunzi wake, "Kwa kuwa nimewapa kielelezo, ili kama mimi nilivyowatendea ninyi, nanyi mtende vivyo" (Yohana 13:15). Yesu hakuwaagiza tu wanafunzi kutawadhana miguu; alichukua bakuli na kitambaa na kuonyesha mfano wa jukumu hilo. Hakutoa hotuba kuhusu upendo; aliutoa uhai wake. Mshauri anayemwelekeza mshauriwa wake kwenye tabia yenye umbo la Kristo lazima awe tayari, kwa kiasi fulani, kuitembea njia hiyo mbele ya mshauriwa. "Mnifuate mimi, kama mimi ninavyomfuata Kristo" (1 Wakorintho 11:1). Kuonyesha mfano ni kielelezo cha Kristo, si mbinu tu. Mshauri anapoonyesha mfano wa unyenyekevu, msamaha, uvumilivu, au maneno ya uaminifu, anazalisha kwa udogo kile ambacho Kristo amekifanya kwa ukamilifu wake wote. Mshauriwa, akimtazama mshauri, anafundishwa kutazama ng'ambo ya mshauri kuelekea Kristo.
6.6 When Modeling Fails
6.6 Kuonyesha Mfano Kunaposhindwa

Modeling can go wrong in two equal and opposite ways. The first is modeling from a pedestal — the counselor presenting himself as one who has already mastered what he asks the counselee to do. "When I had this struggle, I prayed about it and the Lord delivered me immediately." Even when something like that is true, it lands on the counselee as a comparison he cannot match. The counselor's strength becomes the counselee's accusation. He concludes, silently, "This is for spiritual professionals, not for me." Pedestal modeling produces admirers, not disciples.

Kuonyesha mfano kunaweza kwenda kombo kwa njia mbili zilizo sawa na zinazopingana. Ya kwanza ni kuonyesha mfano kutoka juu ya jukwaa — mshauri akijionyesha kama mtu ambaye tayari amekimudu kile anachomwomba mshauriwa kufanya. "Nilipokuwa na mapambano haya, niliomba kuhusu jambo hilo na Bwana akaniokoa mara moja." Hata pale jambo kama hilo linapokuwa kweli, linamfikia mshauriwa kama ulinganisho asioweza kuufikia. Nguvu ya mshauri inakuwa shtaka kwa mshauriwa. Anahitimisha, kimya kimya, "Hili ni la wataalamu wa kiroho, si langu." Kuonyesha mfano kutoka juu ya jukwaa huzaa watu wanaostaajabia, si wanafunzi.

The second failure is the inverse: modeling that overshares one's own ongoing struggle. The counselor in his anxiety to seem accessible discloses too much, too soon, in too much detail. The counselee, who came carrying his own weight, ends up carrying the counselor's too. He may even shift into the helper role — "Pastor, I'll be praying for you." Subtle, but disastrous. The session has been inverted; the counselor is now being ministered to. Self-disclosure should be brief, deliberate, and pointed toward the counselee's need, not toward the counselor's catharsis.

Kushindwa kwa pili ni kinyume chake: kuonyesha mfano kunakozidisha kushiriki mapambano yanayoendelea ya mshauri mwenyewe. Mshauri, kwa wasiwasi wake wa kutaka kuonekana anafikika, anajifunua kupita kiasi, mapema mno, kwa undani mwingi mno. Mshauriwa, aliyekuja akibeba mzigo wake mwenyewe, anaishia kubeba wa mshauri pia. Anaweza hata kuhamia nafasi ya msaidizi — "Mchungaji, nitakuombea." Ni jambo dogo kuonekana, lakini ni maafa. Kikao kimegeuzwa juu chini; sasa mshauri ndiye anayehudumiwa. Kujifunua kunapaswa kuwa kufupi, kwa makusudi, na kuelekezwa kwenye hitaji la mshauriwa, si kwenye kujipunguzia mzigo wa moyo (catharsis) kwa mshauri.

The discipline between these two failures is one of proportion. Disclose enough that the counselee knows you have walked similar ground; do not disclose so much that he must walk yours alongside his own. The apostle Paul provides the calibration: "I have not yet attained" — he is still pressing on — "but this one thing I do" — he is going somewhere — "forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before" (Phil 3:13). The counselor models a pilgrim, neither arrived nor lost. The counselee can imitate a pilgrim. He cannot imitate a master.

Nidhamu iliyo kati ya kushindwa huku kuwili ni ya uwiano. Jifunue kiasi cha kutosha ili mshauriwa ajue kwamba umepita katika ardhi inayofanana; usijifunue kiasi kwamba yeye alazimike kutembea njia yako pamoja na yake mwenyewe. Mtume Paulo anatoa kipimo: "sijihesabu kuwa nimekwisha kushika" — bado anakaza mwendo — "ila natenda neno moja tu" — anaelekea mahali fulani — "nikiyasahau yaliyo nyuma, nikiyachuchumilia yaliyo mbele" (Wafilipi 3:13). Mshauri anaonyesha mfano wa msafiri wa kiroho (hujaji), si aliyekwisha kufika wala aliyepotea. Mshauriwa anaweza kumwiga msafiri. Hawezi kumwiga bingwa.
6.7 Modeling for the Absent
6.7 Kuonyesha Mfano kwa Ajili ya Wasiokuwepo

Much of Step Six is rehearsal for a conversation the counselee will have with someone who is not in the room — a spouse, a parent, an estranged adult child, an employer. The counselor takes the role of the absent person, allowing the counselee to speak the words he needs to say while the words can still be revised. This is sacred work and easily abused, and it deserves careful technique.

Sehemu kubwa ya Hatua ya Sita ni mazoezi ya mazungumzo ambayo mshauriwa atakuwa nayo na mtu asiyekuwepo chumbani — mwenzi, mzazi, mtoto mtu mzima aliyetengana naye, mwajiri. Mshauri anachukua nafasi ya mtu huyo asiyekuwepo, akimruhusu mshauriwa kusema maneno anayohitaji kusema wakati maneno hayo bado yanaweza kurekebishwa. Hii ni kazi takatifu na inayoweza kutumiwa vibaya kwa urahisi, nayo inastahili mbinu ya uangalifu.

First, the counselor should make the role-play explicit. "Let me be your father for a few minutes. I am going to respond the way you have told me he typically responds. You say to me what you intend to say to him on Saturday." Naming the frame keeps both parties oriented; without that frame, role-play drifts toward performance or sentimentality. Second, the counselor should resist the temptation to play the absent person as either monster or saint. Play him as the counselee has actually described him — irritable on Tuesdays, defensive when accused, softening when asked sincere questions. The counselee will be disarmed by a portrait he recognizes.

Kwanza, mshauri anapaswa kuweka wazi kwamba ni maigizo. "Niache niwe baba yako kwa dakika chache. Nitajibu jinsi ulivyoniambia kwamba kwa kawaida yeye hujibu. Wewe niambie kile unachokusudia kumwambia Jumamosi." Kutaja mfumo huu kunawaweka wote wawili katika mwelekeo sahihi; bila mfumo huo, kuigiza nafasi huelekea kuwa maonyesho au hisia za kupita kiasi. Pili, mshauri anapaswa kupinga kishawishi cha kumwigiza mtu asiyekuwepo kama jitu ovu au mtakatifu. Mwigize kama mshauriwa alivyomweleza kwa kweli — mwenye hasira siku za Jumanne, mwenye kujitetea anaposhtakiwa, anayelainika anapoulizwa maswali ya dhati. Mshauriwa atanyang'anywa silaha zake za kujihami na picha anayoitambua.

Third — and this is the discipline most often missed — the counselor should role-play more than one possible response from the absent party. "Let's say he hears you and weeps. What do you say next?" Then: "Let's say he gets angry and leaves the room. What do you say next?" Then: "Let's say he listens and changes the subject. What do you say next?" The counselee who has rehearsed three responses arrives at the actual conversation with three exits prepared, and is therefore not derailed by whichever one comes. Step Eight will later weigh outcomes formally; Step Six rehearses for them concretely.

Tatu — na hii ndiyo nidhamu inayokosekana mara nyingi zaidi — mshauri anapaswa kuigiza zaidi ya mwitikio mmoja unaowezekana kutoka kwa mtu asiyekuwepo. "Tuseme anakusikia na kulia. Unasema nini baadaye?" Kisha: "Tuseme anakasirika na kutoka chumbani. Unasema nini baadaye?" Kisha: "Tuseme anasikiliza kisha anabadilisha mada. Unasema nini baadaye?" Mshauriwa aliyefanya mazoezi ya miitikio mitatu hufika kwenye mazungumzo halisi akiwa na njia tatu za kutokea zilizoandaliwa, na kwa hiyo haondolewi njiani na mwitikio wowote utakaokuja. Hatua ya Nane baadaye itapima matokeo kirasmi; Hatua ya Sita inayafanyia mazoezi kwa vitendo.

Finally, debrief. "What was hardest in that role-play? What words came easily? Where did you freeze?" These questions surface what the counselee did not know about himself, and they sharpen the rehearsal for the next round. The counselee leaves the office not with a script — scripts always fail in real conversation — but with a tested vocabulary, tried words that have already been spoken aloud once and can therefore be spoken aloud again.

Mwisho, fanyeni tathmini baada ya zoezi. "Ni nini kilikuwa kigumu zaidi katika maigizo yale? Maneno gani yalikuja kwa urahisi? Ulikwama wapi?" Maswali haya huibua yale ambayo mshauriwa hakujua kuhusu nafsi yake, na huiboresha mazoezi kwa ajili ya mzunguko unaofuata. Mshauriwa anaondoka ofisini si na hati ya kukariri — hati daima hushindwa katika mazungumzo halisi — bali na msamiati uliojaribiwa, maneno yaliyojaribiwa ambayo tayari yamesemwa kwa sauti mara moja na kwa hiyo yanaweza kusemwa kwa sauti tena.

Step 7 — Review the Alternatives
Hatua ya 7 — Pitia Njia Mbadala
"What are your options? Let us look at them all."
“Una chaguo gani? Tuyatazame yote.”
7.1 The Trap of the Single Option
7.1 Mtego wa Chaguo Moja Tu

A counselee in distress almost always arrives at the office with a narrowed field of vision. He sees one option, and the option he sees is usually the worst. The man whose marriage is in trouble sees only divorce. The mother whose teenage daughter has rebelled sees only the threat of cutting her off. The employee whose boss has been unjust sees only quitting. The grieving widow sees only loneliness stretching to the grave. Pain narrows the imagination. The Hebrew word tsar, "narrow," is the same root from which "trouble" and "distress" come. To be in trouble is to be in a narrow place where one cannot see the alternatives. The counselor's task in Step Seven is to broaden the field. He helps the counselee step out of the narrow place and survey the wider landscape of possible actions. Proverbs 11:14 declares, "Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety." The principle applies inwardly as well: where no alternatives are seen, the counselee falls; in the multitude of considered options there is safety.

Mshauriwa aliye katika dhiki karibu kila mara hufika ofisini akiwa na upeo mwembamba wa kuona. Anaona chaguo moja, na chaguo analoliona kwa kawaida ndilo baya kuliko yote. Mwanamume ambaye ndoa yake iko taabuni anaona talaka tu. Mama ambaye binti yake kijana ameasi anaona tu tishio la kumkatilia mbali. Mfanyakazi ambaye bosi wake amemtendea isivyo haki anaona tu kuacha kazi. Mjane aliye katika maombolezo anaona tu upweke unaoenea hadi kaburini. Maumivu hufinya mawazo. Neno la Kiebrania tsar, “mwembamba,” lina mzizi ule ule ambao kutoka kwake yanatokea maneno “taabu” na “dhiki.” Kuwa taabuni ni kuwa mahali pembamba ambapo mtu hawezi kuziona njia mbadala. Kazi ya mshauri katika Hatua ya Saba ni kupanua upeo. Humsaidia mshauriwa kutoka katika mahali pale pembamba na kuitazama nchi pana ya hatua zinazowezekana. Mithali 11:14 inatangaza, “Pasipo mashauri taifa huanguka; bali kwa wingi wa washauri huja wokovu.” Kanuni hii inatumika pia ndani ya mtu: pasipo njia mbadala zinazoonekana, mshauriwa huanguka; kwa wingi wa chaguo zilizofikiriwa vizuri huja usalama.
7.2 Generate Before You Evaluate
7.2 Zalisha Kabla ya Kupima

A discipline absorbed by Drakeford from problem-solving theory bears reproducing here: the counselor must help the counselee generate alternatives before evaluating them. The two activities, when mixed, kill each other. If every alternative offered is immediately judged ("That won't work because…"), the counselee's creative imagination shuts down. He stops generating. The wise counselor establishes a deliberate phase: "Before we decide which option is best, let us list every option we can think of, no matter how unlikely or impractical. We are not committing to any of them. We are simply mapping the territory." This is the brainstorming phase. The counselor accepts every suggestion without critique. He may add a few from his own pastoral imagination. Only after the list is reasonably full does evaluation begin. This sequence — generate, then evaluate — protects the counselee's creativity and produces alternatives that would never have surfaced if criticism had been allowed in too early.

Nidhamu moja ambayo Drakeford aliichukua kutoka katika nadharia ya utatuzi wa matatizo inafaa kurudiwa hapa: mshauri lazima amsaidie mshauriwa kuzalisha njia mbadala kabla ya kuzipima. Shughuli hizi mbili, zinapochanganywa, huuana. Ikiwa kila njia mbadala inayotolewa inahukumiwa mara moja (“Hiyo haitafaa kwa sababu…”), mawazo ya ubunifu ya mshauriwa hufungika. Anaacha kuzalisha. Mshauri mwenye hekima huweka kipindi maalum kwa makusudi: “Kabla hatujaamua ni chaguo lipi lililo bora, tuorodheshe kila chaguo tunaloweza kufikiri, hata kama haliwezekani sana au halitekelezeki. Hatujifungi kwa lolote kati yake. Tunachora tu ramani ya eneo.” Hiki ni kipindi cha kuchangia mawazo kwa uhuru (brainstorming). Mshauri hupokea kila pendekezo bila kulikosoa. Anaweza kuongeza machache kutoka katika mawazo yake mwenyewe ya kichungaji. Ni baada tu ya orodha kujaa kwa kiasi cha kutosha ndipo upimaji huanza. Mfuatano huu — zalisha, kisha pima — hulinda ubunifu wa mshauriwa na huzaa njia mbadala ambazo zisingejitokeza kamwe kama ukosoaji ungeruhusiwa kuingia mapema mno.
7.3 The Counselor Does Not Decide
7.3 Mshauri Haamui

A line must be drawn here that is foundational to all biblical counseling: the counselor does not make the decision for the counselee. The counselor lays out the alternatives, helps the counselee see each one clearly, and then steps back. The decision belongs to the counselee. He must own it. A decision made by the counselor and merely accepted by the counselee will not survive the first storm. A decision that the counselee himself has made, having considered the alternatives, having weighed them in the presence of God and his counselor, will hold. This is the difference between dependency and growth. The counselor who decides for the counselee has produced a counselee who must come back for the next decision, and the next, and the next. The counselor who reviews the alternatives but lets the counselee choose has produced a person who is becoming capable of biblical decision-making on his own. Drakeford was firm: counsel, do not control.

Mstari lazima uchorwe hapa ambao ni wa msingi kwa ushauri wote wa kibiblia: mshauri hamwamulii mshauriwa. Mshauri huziweka wazi njia mbadala, humsaidia mshauriwa kuiona kila moja waziwazi, kisha hurudi nyuma. Uamuzi ni wa mshauriwa. Lazima aumiliki. Uamuzi uliofanywa na mshauri na kukubaliwa tu na mshauriwa hautastahimili dhoruba ya kwanza. Uamuzi ambao mshauriwa mwenyewe ameufanya, baada ya kuzifikiria njia mbadala, baada ya kuzipima mbele za Mungu na mbele ya mshauri wake, utasimama imara. Hii ndiyo tofauti kati ya utegemezi na ukuaji. Mshauri anayemwamulia mshauriwa amezalisha mshauriwa ambaye lazima arudi kwa ajili ya uamuzi unaofuata, na unaofuata, na unaofuata. Mshauri anayezipitia njia mbadala lakini anamwacha mshauriwa achague amezalisha mtu anayezidi kuwa na uwezo wa kufanya maamuzi ya kibiblia mwenyewe. Drakeford alikuwa thabiti: shauri, usitawale.
7.4 Scriptural Filters
7.4 Vichujio vya Kimaandiko

Once alternatives have been generated, the Christian counselor helps the counselee evaluate them through a specific filter: Which of these alternatives is consistent with the will of God revealed in Scripture? Some alternatives the counselee will have generated are simply unavailable to a Christian. Adultery, theft, abandonment of duty, deception — these are not options for a follower of Christ regardless of how attractive they appear in the moment. The counselor helps the counselee see this clearly. He does not moralize; he simply applies the filter. "You mentioned that one option is to leave the marriage and begin a relationship with this other woman. Let us be honest: that option is closed to a man who follows Christ. The Lord has spoken on this clearly. Let us set it aside and look at what remains." This is not the counselor deciding; it is the counselor helping the counselee see what God has already decided.

Mara njia mbadala zinapokwisha kuzalishwa, mshauri Mkristo humsaidia mshauriwa kuzipima kupitia kichujio maalum: Ni ipi kati ya njia hizi mbadala inayopatana na mapenzi ya Mungu yaliyofunuliwa katika Maandiko? Baadhi ya njia mbadala ambazo mshauriwa atakuwa amezitaja hazipatikani kabisa kwa Mkristo. Uzinzi, wizi, kuacha wajibu, udanganyifu — haya si chaguo kwa mfuasi wa Kristo hata yaonekane ya kuvutia namna gani wakati huo. Mshauri humsaidia mshauriwa kuliona hili waziwazi. Hahubiri maadili; anatumia tu kichujio. “Ulitaja kwamba chaguo moja ni kuiacha ndoa na kuanza uhusiano na mwanamke huyu mwingine. Tuwe wakweli: chaguo hilo limefungwa kwa mwanamume anayemfuata Kristo. Bwana amesema waziwazi juu ya jambo hili. Tuliweke kando na tutazame kilichobaki.” Huku si mshauri kuamua; ni mshauri kumsaidia mshauriwa kuona kile ambacho Mungu amekwisha kukiamua.
7.5 Practical Filters
7.5 Vichujio vya Kiutendaji

After the scriptural filter, three practical filters help narrow the surviving alternatives. First, feasibility: can the counselee actually do this? An alternative that requires resources he does not possess is not really an alternative. Second, cost: what will this option require — financially, emotionally, relationally, spiritually? Every alternative has a price. The counselee must see the price before he chooses. Third, reversibility: if this alternative does not work, can the counselee return to where he was? Some choices are reversible and some are not. Alternatives that are irreversible deserve more deliberation. Drakeford taught his students to slow the counselee down at exactly this point. The counselee in pain wants to act now. The counselor, having helped him see his options, helps him also see the weight of each one. Then, having seen, the counselee chooses. The counselor moves with him into Step Eight to explore what each chosen alternative will produce.

Baada ya kichujio cha kimaandiko, vichujio vitatu vya kiutendaji husaidia kupunguza njia mbadala zilizobaki. Kwanza, uwezekano wa kutekelezeka: je, mshauriwa anaweza kweli kufanya hili? Njia mbadala inayohitaji rasilimali asizokuwa nazo si njia mbadala kweli. Pili, gharama: chaguo hili litahitaji nini — kifedha, kihisia, kimahusiano, kiroho? Kila njia mbadala ina bei yake. Mshauriwa lazima aione bei kabla hajachagua. Tatu, uwezekano wa kurudi nyuma: kama njia hii mbadala haitafaulu, je, mshauriwa anaweza kurudi pale alipokuwa? Maamuzi mengine yanaweza kubadilishwa na mengine hayawezi. Njia mbadala zisizoweza kubadilishwa zinastahili kutafakariwa zaidi. Drakeford aliwafundisha wanafunzi wake kumpunguzia mshauriwa mwendo hasa katika hatua hii. Mshauriwa aliye katika maumivu anataka kutenda sasa hivi. Mshauri, akiisha kumsaidia kuona chaguo zake, humsaidia pia kuona uzito wa kila moja. Kisha, akiisha kuona, mshauriwa huchagua. Mshauri huendelea pamoja naye katika Hatua ya Nane ili kuchunguza kile ambacho kila njia mbadala iliyochaguliwa itazaa.
7.6 The Counselee Who Refuses Alternatives
7.6 Mshauriwa Anayekataa Njia Mbadala

Sometimes Step Seven runs into a wall. The counselee has narrowed his vision to one option and refuses to entertain any other. "There is no other way." "I cannot do that." "You don't understand — none of those would work." The counselor patiently lists three, four, five alternatives, and each is dismissed the moment it is named. The conversation feels stuck.

Wakati mwingine Hatua ya Saba hugonga ukuta. Mshauriwa amepunguza upeo wake hadi chaguo moja na anakataa kufikiria jingine lolote. “Hakuna njia nyingine.” “Siwezi kufanya hivyo.” “Huelewi — hakuna hata moja kati ya hizo litakalofaa.” Mshauri kwa uvumilivu anaorodhesha njia mbadala tatu, nne, tano, na kila moja inakataliwa mara tu inapotajwa. Mazungumzo yanaonekana kukwama.

Resistance to alternatives is almost never about the alternatives themselves. It is about something else — usually one of three things. First, the counselee has already decided on a path he knows he cannot defend in Christian conversation, and he is foreclosing alternatives so the chosen path looks inevitable. The wife who has decided to leave her husband for a man at work will tell you there are no other options; admitting alternatives would force her to say "no" to them, and saying "no" to them is too close to confession. The counselor's role here is not to push harder on the alternatives but to gently name the dynamic: "I notice you are dismissing every option I name. I wonder whether you have already decided something you have not yet told me. Would it help to say what that is?"

Kukataa njia mbadala karibu kamwe hakuhusu njia mbadala zenyewe. Kunahusu jambo jingine — kwa kawaida mojawapo ya mambo matatu. Kwanza, mshauriwa amekwisha kuamua njia ambayo anajua hawezi kuitetea katika mazungumzo ya Kikristo, naye anazifunga njia mbadala ili njia aliyoichagua ionekane kuwa haiepukiki. Mke ambaye ameamua kumwacha mumewe kwa ajili ya mwanamume wa kazini atakuambia kwamba hakuna chaguo jingine; kukiri kuwa kuna njia mbadala kungemlazimisha kuzikataa, na kuzikataa kunakaribia mno kuungama. Jukumu la mshauri hapa si kusukuma zaidi njia mbadala bali kuitaja kwa upole hali inayoendelea: “Ninaona unakataa kila chaguo ninalolitaja. Najiuliza kama tayari umeamua jambo fulani ambalo bado hujaniambia. Je, ingesaidia kulisema ni nini?”

Second, the counselee is in such acute pain that exploring alternatives feels like dismissing his suffering. "If you could see other ways, why am I hurting?" When this is the case, the counselor must return briefly to Step Two — sit with the pain again, let the counselee feel heard — before resuming Step Seven. The alternatives will surface when the pain has been honored. Third, the counselee may be exhausted; the capacity to imagine alternatives is itself a function of energy he no longer has. Here the counselor proposes them rather than asks for them, and asks only that the counselee say which feels least impossible. Even the least-impossible is a foothold; the rest comes later.

Pili, mshauriwa yuko katika maumivu makali kiasi kwamba kuchunguza njia mbadala kunaonekana kama kupuuza mateso yake. “Kama ungeweza kuona njia nyingine, mbona ninaumia?” Hali ikiwa hivi, mshauri lazima arudi kwa muda mfupi kwenye Hatua ya Pili — akae tena pamoja na maumivu, amwache mshauriwa ajisikie amesikilizwa — kabla ya kuendelea na Hatua ya Saba. Njia mbadala zitajitokeza maumivu yakiisha kuheshimiwa. Tatu, huenda mshauriwa amechoka kabisa; uwezo wa kuwaza njia mbadala wenyewe hutegemea nguvu ambayo hana tena. Hapa mshauri huzipendekeza yeye mwenyewe badala ya kumwomba azitaje, naye humwomba mshauriwa aseme tu ni ipi inayoonekana kuwa isiyowezekana kwa kiasi kidogo zaidi. Hata ile isiyowezekana kwa kiasi kidogo zaidi ni mahali pa kukanyagia mguu; mengine huja baadaye.
7.7 The Wider Circle of Counsel
7.7 Mzunguko Mpana wa Washauri

Step Seven does not require that the counselor and the counselee identify every possible alternative alone. The pastor who tries to be the entire wisdom of God for his counselee has misunderstood his office. Proverbs 11:14 — "in the multitude of counsellors there is safety" — applies here as much as in Step Four. Some alternatives will only be visible to other people: a brother who knows the family situation, a wife who has watched the marriage for thirty years, an elder who has counseled in similar territory, a believer who has walked the very road the counselee is considering.

Hatua ya Saba haihitaji kwamba mshauri na mshauriwa watambue kila njia mbadala inayowezekana peke yao. Mchungaji anayejaribu kuwa hekima yote ya Mungu kwa mshauriwa wake ameielewa vibaya huduma yake. Mithali 11:14 — “kwa wingi wa washauri huja wokovu” — inatumika hapa sawasawa na katika Hatua ya Nne. Baadhi ya njia mbadala zitaonekana tu kwa watu wengine: ndugu anayeijua hali ya familia, mke ambaye ameiangalia ndoa kwa miaka thelathini, mzee wa kanisa ambaye amewahi kushauri katika hali zinazofanana, muumini ambaye amepita katika njia ile ile ambayo mshauriwa anaifikiria.

The counselor can therefore extend the alternatives-list deliberately. "Have you talked with your elder about this? What does he think? Is there an older woman in your church who has walked through a similar season? Would it help to write your brother and ask him to think with you?" These referrals to wider counsel are not abandonment; they are pastoral wisdom. The counselor remains the primary helper, but he widens the field of inputs. The counselee will sometimes return saying, "I had not thought of what my brother suggested. It changes things." Alternatives that did not exist in the counseling office have entered the room through other voices.

Kwa hiyo mshauri anaweza kuipanua orodha ya njia mbadala kwa makusudi. “Je, umezungumza na mzee wako wa kanisa kuhusu jambo hili? Yeye anafikiri nini? Je, kuna mwanamke mzee katika kanisa lako ambaye amepita katika kipindi kinachofanana? Je, ingesaidia kumwandikia kaka yako na kumwomba afikiri pamoja nawe?” Kumpeleka mshauriwa kwa washauri wengine namna hii si kumtelekeza; ni hekima ya kichungaji. Mshauri anabaki kuwa msaidizi mkuu, lakini anapanua wigo wa michango. Wakati mwingine mshauriwa atarudi akisema, “Sikuwa nimefikiria lile alilopendekeza kaka yangu. Linabadilisha mambo.” Njia mbadala ambazo hazikuwepo katika ofisi ya ushauri zimeingia chumbani kupitia sauti nyingine.

There is, however, a discipline in this widening. The counselor must know the wider circle well enough to refer wisely. Not every elder is wise; not every brother gives Christian counsel. To send a counselee to consult someone who will give him bad counsel is no kindness. The counselor's knowledge of his own congregation — who has walked what road, who counsels well, who is in season — is part of his own preparation. Step Seven trusts the body of Christ, but the counselor trusts only those parts of the body he has tested and found faithful.

Hata hivyo, kuna nidhamu katika upanuzi huu. Mshauri lazima aujue mzunguko huo mpana vizuri kiasi cha kuweza kumpeleka mtu kwa busara. Si kila mzee wa kanisa ana hekima; si kila ndugu hutoa shauri la Kikristo. Kumtuma mshauriwa kwenda kutaka shauri kwa mtu atakayempa shauri baya si wema. Ujuzi wa mshauri kuhusu kusanyiko lake mwenyewe — nani amepita njia gani, nani hushauri vizuri, nani yuko tayari kwa wakati huu — ni sehemu ya maandalizi yake mwenyewe. Hatua ya Saba inauamini mwili wa Kristo, lakini mshauri huviamini tu vile viungo vya mwili ambavyo amevijaribu na kuviona kuwa vyaaminifu.

Step 8 — Explore the Outcomes
Hatua ya 8 — Chunguza Matokeo
"What is likely to happen if you choose this path?"
“Ni nini kinachoweza kutokea ukichagua njia hii?”
8.1 The Discipline of Foresight
8.1 Nidhamu ya Kuona Mbele

Step Eight is closely linked to Step Seven and is sometimes hard to distinguish from it; the careful counselor distinguishes them deliberately. In Step Seven the counselee surveyed the alternatives. In Step Eight the counselee, having narrowed the alternatives, walks each surviving option forward in his imagination and asks, "If I do this, what is likely to follow?" The discipline is foresight. It is the discipline of which Solomon wrote, "A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished" (Prov 22:3). The simple man, in the moment of decision, sees only the action itself and not its consequences. The prudent man sees the action and the chain of events that will flow from it. The biblical counselor's task is to help his counselee become prudent rather than simple. The counselor cannot foresee for the counselee; he can ask the questions that help the counselee see for himself.

Hatua ya Nane imeunganika kwa karibu na Hatua ya Saba na wakati mwingine ni vigumu kuzitofautisha; mshauri makini huzitofautisha kwa makusudi. Katika Hatua ya Saba mshauriwa alizitazama njia mbadala. Katika Hatua ya Nane mshauriwa, akiisha kuzipunguza njia mbadala, huipeleka mbele kila njia iliyobaki katika mawazo yake na kuuliza, “Nikifanya hivi, ni nini kinachoweza kufuata?” Nidhamu hii ni kuona mbele. Ni nidhamu ile ambayo Sulemani aliiandika, “Mtu mwenye busara huona mabaya, akajificha; bali wajinga huendelea mbele, wakaumia” (Mit 22:3). Mjinga, wakati wa kuamua, huona tendo lenyewe tu na si matokeo yake. Mwenye busara huona tendo pamoja na mlolongo wa matukio yatakayotiririka kutoka kwake. Kazi ya mshauri wa kibiblia ni kumsaidia mshauriwa wake kuwa mwenye busara badala ya mjinga. Mshauri hawezi kuona mbele kwa niaba ya mshauriwa; anaweza kuuliza maswali yanayomsaidia mshauriwa kuona mwenyewe.
8.2 The Time Horizons
8.2 Vipindi vya Wakati

A useful pastoral practice is to walk each alternative through three time horizons. The first is immediate: what will happen in the next twenty-four hours if you take this action? The second is medium-range: what will be the situation in six months? The third is long-range: what will be the situation in five years, in ten years, in eternity? An alternative that looks attractive in the immediate horizon may look catastrophic in the long-range horizon. An alternative that looks costly in the immediate horizon may look gracious in the long-range horizon. The counselee must see all three. The man who is contemplating an affair sees only the immediate horizon. The counselor walks him through the medium-range horizon (your wife will know; your children will know; your testimony will be ruined) and the long-range horizon (you will stand before Christ and answer for this). Suddenly the immediate appeal looks small against the long-range cost. This is the practical work of Step Eight.

Desturi moja ya kichungaji yenye manufaa ni kuipitisha kila njia mbadala katika vipindi vitatu vya wakati. Cha kwanza ni cha papo hapo: ni nini kitakachotokea katika saa ishirini na nne zijazo ukichukua hatua hii? Cha pili ni cha muda wa kati: hali itakuwaje baada ya miezi sita? Cha tatu ni cha muda mrefu: hali itakuwaje baada ya miaka mitano, baada ya miaka kumi, katika umilele? Njia mbadala inayoonekana kuvutia katika kipindi cha papo hapo inaweza kuonekana kuwa maafa katika kipindi cha muda mrefu. Njia mbadala inayoonekana kuwa ghali katika kipindi cha papo hapo inaweza kuonekana kuwa ya neema katika kipindi cha muda mrefu. Mshauriwa lazima avione vipindi vyote vitatu. Mwanamume anayefikiria kuzini huona kipindi cha papo hapo tu. Mshauri humpitisha katika kipindi cha muda wa kati (mke wako atajua; watoto wako watajua; ushuhuda wako utaharibika) na kipindi cha muda mrefu (utasimama mbele za Kristo na kutoa hesabu ya jambo hili). Ghafla mvuto wa papo hapo unaonekana mdogo mbele ya gharama ya muda mrefu. Hii ndiyo kazi ya kiutendaji ya Hatua ya Nane.
8.3 Outcomes for Self and for Others
8.3 Matokeo kwa Nafsi Yake na kwa Wengine

Sin is rarely contained within the sinner. The counselor must help the counselee explore not only what an alternative will produce in his own life, but what it will produce in the lives of those around him. The teenage girl considering an abortion needs to consider, alongside the impact on her own future, the loss of a human life made in the image of God. The man considering bankruptcy needs to consider his creditors, who trusted him with goods and money. The wife considering separation needs to consider her children, who will live with the consequences of her decision for decades. Drakeford's casework constantly returned to this widening of vision. The counselee in distress is often locked in upon himself; the counselor draws his eyes outward to the human field his action will affect. "None of us liveth to himself, and no man dieth to himself" (Rom 14:7). Outcomes ripple. The counselor helps the counselee see the ripples before he drops the stone.

Dhambi mara chache hubaki ndani ya mtenda dhambi. Mshauri lazima amsaidie mshauriwa kuchunguza si tu kile ambacho njia mbadala itazaa katika maisha yake mwenyewe, bali pia kile itakachozaa katika maisha ya wale walio karibu naye. Msichana kijana anayefikiria kutoa mimba anahitaji kufikiria, pamoja na athari kwa wakati wake ujao, kupotea kwa uhai wa mwanadamu aliyeumbwa kwa sura ya Mungu. Mwanamume anayefikiria kujitangaza kufilisika anahitaji kuwafikiria wadai wake, waliomwamini kwa bidhaa na fedha. Mke anayefikiria kutengana na mumewe anahitaji kuwafikiria watoto wake, watakaoishi na matokeo ya uamuzi wake kwa miongo kadhaa. Kazi za ushauri za Drakeford zilirudi mara kwa mara kwenye upanuzi huu wa kuona. Mshauriwa aliye katika dhiki mara nyingi amejifungia ndani ya nafsi yake; mshauri huyavuta macho yake nje kuelekea uwanja wa watu ambao tendo lake litawagusa. “Kwa maana hakuna hata mmoja wetu aishiye kwa nafsi yake, wala hakuna afaye kwa nafsi yake” (Rum 14:7). Matokeo huenea kama mawimbi. Mshauri humsaidia mshauriwa kuyaona mawimbi kabla hajalitupa jiwe.
8.4 Outcomes Before God
8.4 Matokeo Mbele za Mungu

For the Christian counselor and the Christian counselee, the most important outcome is not measured in dollars, in relationships, or in social standing. It is measured in the eyes of God. "For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done" (2 Cor 5:10). This eternal horizon does not flatten the practical horizons; it crowns them. The counselor at Step Eight helps the counselee ask, of each surviving alternative: "If I do this, what will I have to say to my Lord at His judgment seat? Can I take this action and look Him in the face?" There are alternatives the counselee can defend before himself, before his spouse, even before his pastor, that he cannot defend before Christ. Step Eight surfaces this. The counselor does not threaten the counselee with judgment; he simply asks the question that the counselee himself will eventually have to answer.

Kwa mshauri Mkristo na kwa mshauriwa Mkristo, matokeo muhimu zaidi hayapimwi kwa fedha, kwa mahusiano, wala kwa hadhi katika jamii. Yanapimwa machoni pa Mungu. “Kwa maana imetupasa sisi sote kudhihirishwa mbele ya kiti cha hukumu cha Kristo, ili kila mtu apokee ijara ya mambo aliyotenda kwa mwili, kadiri alivyotenda” (2 Kor 5:10). Kipindi hiki cha milele hakivibatilishi vipindi vya kiutendaji; kinavivika taji. Mshauri katika Hatua ya Nane humsaidia mshauriwa kuuliza, kuhusu kila njia mbadala iliyobaki: “Nikifanya hivi, nitakuwa na la kumwambia Bwana wangu nini mbele ya kiti chake cha hukumu? Je, ninaweza kuchukua hatua hii na kumtazama usoni?” Kuna njia mbadala ambazo mshauriwa anaweza kuzitetea mbele ya nafsi yake, mbele ya mwenzi wake, hata mbele ya mchungaji wake, lakini hawezi kuzitetea mbele ya Kristo. Hatua ya Nane hulileta jambo hili juu. Mshauri hamtishi mshauriwa kwa hukumu; anauliza tu swali ambalo mshauriwa mwenyewe hatimaye atalazimika kulijibu.
8.5 The Counselee Chooses
8.5 Mshauriwa Anachagua

When the alternatives have been generated, evaluated, and explored as to their probable outcomes, the moment of choice arrives. The counselor does not extend the deliberation indefinitely; deliberation that becomes endless is paralysis. At some point the counselee must say, "I have considered. I will do this." Drakeford taught that the counselee's choice should be spoken aloud and, where possible, written down. Spoken commitment binds. Written commitment binds further. The man who has named his chosen action in the presence of his counselor and has put his hand to a written summary of it is far more likely to follow through than the man who has merely thought about it. The counselor closes Step Eight by confirming the choice: "So you have decided that this week you will go to your wife and tell her plainly that you have been wrong about the money, and that you will lay out the budget you and I have drafted. Is that your decision?" The counselee says yes. Step Nine begins.

Njia mbadala zikiisha kuzalishwa, kupimwa, na kuchunguzwa kuhusu matokeo yake yanayotarajiwa, wakati wa kuchagua hufika. Mshauri harefushi utafakari bila mwisho; utafakari usio na mwisho ni kupooza. Wakati fulani mshauriwa lazima aseme, “Nimefikiri. Nitafanya hivi.” Drakeford alifundisha kwamba uchaguzi wa mshauriwa unapaswa kutamkwa kwa sauti na, inapowezekana, kuandikwa. Ahadi iliyotamkwa hufunga. Ahadi iliyoandikwa hufunga zaidi. Mtu aliyeitaja hatua aliyoichagua mbele ya mshauri wake na kuweka sahihi yake kwenye muhtasari wake ulioandikwa ana uwezekano mkubwa zaidi wa kuitekeleza kuliko mtu aliyeifikiria tu. Mshauri huifunga Hatua ya Nane kwa kuuthibitisha uchaguzi: “Kwa hiyo umeamua kwamba wiki hii utakwenda kwa mke wako na kumwambia waziwazi kwamba umekosea kuhusu fedha, na kwamba utamwonyesha bajeti ambayo wewe na mimi tumeiandaa. Je, huo ndio uamuzi wako?” Mshauriwa anasema ndiyo. Hatua ya Tisa inaanza.
8.6 Outcomes the Counselee Cannot See
8.6 Matokeo Ambayo Mshauriwa Hawezi Kuyaona

The counselor often sees outcomes the counselee does not. This is one of the legitimate gifts of an outside perspective. The counselee has lived inside his situation for so long that certain consequences have become invisible to him; the counselor, viewing the same situation from outside, sees them as if for the first time. Part of Step Eight is the counselor naming, gently and without dictating, what he sees that the counselee may have missed.

Mara nyingi mshauri huona matokeo ambayo mshauriwa hayaoni. Hii ni mojawapo ya zawadi halali za mtazamo wa mtu wa nje. Mshauriwa ameishi ndani ya hali yake kwa muda mrefu kiasi kwamba baadhi ya matokeo yamekuwa yasiyoonekana kwake; mshauri, akiitazama hali ile ile kutoka nje, huyaona kana kwamba ni mara ya kwanza. Sehemu ya Hatua ya Nane ni mshauri kutaja, kwa upole na bila kuamuru, kile anachokiona ambacho huenda mshauriwa amekikosa.

A husband considering whether to take a new job an hour from home may not have weighed what an extra two hours of daily commute will do to his children's experience of their father. A young woman considering whether to marry a man she has known six months may not have weighed what marrying a man whose previous girlfriends all describe similar patterns is likely to produce. A businessman considering whether to confront a partner may not have weighed how that confrontation will affect the silent witness of his own children, who will learn from watching whether their father confronts hard things or avoids them. The counselor offers these views modestly: "I notice something that may matter. As you think about this choice, have you considered…"

Mume anayefikiria kama achukue kazi mpya iliyo umbali wa saa moja kutoka nyumbani huenda hajapima kile ambacho saa mbili za ziada za safari kila siku zitafanya kwa jinsi watoto wake wanavyomjua baba yao. Mwanamke kijana anayefikiria kama aolewe na mwanamume aliyemjua kwa miezi sita huenda hajapima kile ambacho kuolewa na mwanamume ambaye wapenzi wake wote wa zamani wanaeleza mienendo inayofanana kunaweza kuzaa. Mfanyabiashara anayefikiria kama amkabili mbia wake huenda hajapima jinsi makabiliano hayo yatakavyoathiri ushuhuda wa kimya kwa watoto wake mwenyewe, watakaojifunza kwa kutazama kama baba yao hukabili mambo magumu au huyakwepa. Mshauri hutoa mitazamo hii kwa unyenyekevu: “Ninaona jambo moja ambalo huenda lina maana. Unapofikiria uchaguzi huu, je, umefikiria…”

The discipline here is offering, not insisting. The counselor names the outcome; the counselee weighs it. If the counselee says "Yes, I had considered that, and here is why I think it is acceptable," the counselor has done his work. He has put the outcome on the scale. The choice belongs to the counselee, but it must now be a choice made with the outcome in view. Outcomes that surprise the counselee a year later — outcomes the counselor saw and did not name — are an indictment of the counseling, not of the counselee.

Nidhamu hapa ni kutoa, si kushurutisha. Mshauri hutaja matokeo; mshauriwa huyapima. Mshauriwa akisema, “Ndiyo, nilikuwa nimelifikiria hilo, na hii ndiyo sababu nadhani linakubalika,” mshauri amefanya kazi yake. Ameyaweka matokeo kwenye mizani. Uchaguzi ni wa mshauriwa, lakini sasa lazima uwe uchaguzi uliofanywa huku matokeo yakionekana. Matokeo yanayomshtua mshauriwa mwaka mmoja baadaye — matokeo ambayo mshauri aliyaona na hakuyataja — ni lawama dhidi ya ushauri, si dhidi ya mshauriwa.
8.7 The Discipline Against Catastrophizing
8.7 Nidhamu Dhidi ya Kukuza Maafa

The counselee in distress will often catastrophize one of his options. He will tell the counselor that if he confronts his father, his father will disown him forever; that if he takes the new job, his marriage will end; that if he tells his church about his sin, he will be excommunicated and his family will starve. These predictions may contain a kernel of truth, but they have been inflated by fear into certainties that the situation cannot support. Step Eight's discipline includes the gentle deflation of catastrophe.

Mshauriwa aliye katika dhiki mara nyingi atakuza maafa kuhusu mojawapo ya chaguo zake. Atamwambia mshauri kwamba akimkabili baba yake, baba yake atamkana milele; kwamba akichukua kazi mpya, ndoa yake itavunjika; kwamba akiliambia kanisa lake kuhusu dhambi yake, atatengwa na kanisa na familia yake itakufa njaa. Utabiri huu unaweza kuwa na chembe ya ukweli, lakini umepanuliwa na hofu kuwa uhakika ambao hali halisi haiwezi kuuthibitisha. Nidhamu ya Hatua ya Nane inajumuisha kuyapunguza maafa hayo kwa upole.

"You say your father will disown you forever. Tell me, has he ever done that? When he has been most angry with you in the past, what has he actually done?" The counselee may pause and say, "He has gotten quiet and stopped calling for a few weeks. He has never disowned me." Now the predicted outcome has been restored to realistic scale. The counselor has not minimized the cost; the silence and the few weeks are real. But "disowned forever" is no longer the picture in the counselee's mind. He can weigh the actual probable outcome rather than the inflated one.

“Unasema baba yako atakukana milele. Niambie, amewahi kufanya hivyo? Alipokuwa amekukasirikia zaidi siku za nyuma, alifanya nini hasa?” Mshauriwa anaweza kunyamaza kidogo na kusema, “Amenyamaza na kuacha kunipigia simu kwa wiki chache. Hajawahi kunikana.” Sasa matokeo yaliyotabiriwa yamerudishwa kwenye ukubwa wake halisi. Mshauri hajaipunguza gharama; ukimya na zile wiki chache ni halisi. Lakini “kukanwa milele” si picha tena iliyo akilini mwa mshauriwa. Anaweza kupima matokeo halisi yanayowezekana badala ya yale yaliyopanuliwa.

The opposite distortion is also worth naming: counselees sometimes minimize the costs of an option they want to choose. A woman who has decided in her heart to leave her marriage will tell the counselor that the children "will be fine; children are resilient." Step Eight must speak to this too: "Children are resilient, and this is true. They are also durably affected by their parents' divorce, often in ways that do not surface for ten years. May we weigh the actual research on this together?" Catastrophizing and minimizing both distort the picture; Step Eight restores the picture to honest proportions in both directions.

Upotoshaji wa upande wa pili pia unafaa kutajwa: wakati mwingine washauriwa hupunguza gharama za chaguo wanalotaka kulichagua. Mwanamke ambaye ameamua moyoni mwake kuiacha ndoa yake atamwambia mshauri kwamba watoto “watakuwa salama; watoto huvumilia na kurudia hali yao.” Hatua ya Nane lazima izungumzie hili pia: “Watoto huvumilia, na hilo ni kweli. Pia huathiriwa kwa kudumu na talaka ya wazazi wao, mara nyingi kwa njia zisizojitokeza kwa miaka kumi. Je, tunaweza kupima pamoja tafiti halisi kuhusu jambo hili?” Kukuza maafa na kupunguza gharama vyote viwili hupotosha picha; Hatua ya Nane huirudisha picha kwenye uwiano wa kweli pande zote mbili.

The counselor's tone in this discipline matters. He is not arguing with the counselee or correcting him. He is restoring scale. "Let's check what we actually know" is the spirit. The counselee in distress has lost his sense of proportion, and the counselor's calmer view returns it. After this restoration, the choice the counselee makes will be a choice made under accurate conditions rather than under the magnifications of fear or desire.

Sauti ya mshauri katika nidhamu hii ni muhimu. Habishani na mshauriwa wala hamsahihishi. Anarudisha ukubwa halisi wa mambo. “Tuangalie kile tunachokijua kweli” ndiyo roho yake. Mshauriwa aliye katika dhiki amepoteza hisia yake ya uwiano, na mtazamo wa mshauri ulio tulivu zaidi huirudisha. Baada ya urejesho huu, uchaguzi atakaoufanya mshauriwa utakuwa uchaguzi uliofanywa katika hali sahihi badala ya chini ya ukuzaji wa hofu au wa tamaa.

Step 9 — Supply Information
Hatua ya 9 — Toa Taarifa
"What do you need to know to do this well?"
"Unahitaji kujua nini ili ufanye jambo hili vizuri?"
9.1 Information Belongs Late, Not Early
9.1 Taarifa Hufaa Mwishoni, Si Mwanzoni

A common error among inexperienced counselors is to supply information too early in the process. The counselee describes his problem, and the counselor — eager to help — immediately begins to teach. He explains the dynamics of marriage, the stages of grief, the principles of forgiveness, the doctrine of sanctification. The counselee, who came for relief, leaves having received a sermon. He has been instructed but not helped. Drakeford placed information at Step Nine, near the end, for a reason. Until the counselee has been heard, until the situation has been clarified, until responsibility has been acknowledged, until alternatives have been reviewed and outcomes explored, information is premature. It bounces off. But once the counselee has done all this preceding work, he is ready — for the first time, often — to receive information. He knows what he is looking for. He has questions, not just complaints. Now the counselor's information lands.

Kosa la kawaida miongoni mwa washauri wasio na uzoefu ni kutoa taarifa mapema mno katika mchakato. Mshauriwa anaeleza tatizo lake, na mshauri — akiwa na hamu ya kusaidia — mara moja anaanza kufundisha. Anaeleza mienendo ya ndoa, hatua za huzuni, kanuni za msamaha, fundisho la utakaso. Mshauriwa, aliyekuja kutafuta nafuu, anaondoka akiwa amepokea mahubiri. Amefundishwa lakini hajasaidiwa. Drakeford aliiweka taarifa katika Hatua ya Tisa, karibu na mwisho, kwa sababu maalum. Mpaka mshauriwa amesikilizwa, mpaka hali imefafanuliwa, mpaka uwajibikaji umekubaliwa, mpaka njia mbadala zimepitiwa na matokeo yamechunguzwa, taarifa ni ya mapema mno. Inadunda tu bila kuingia. Lakini mshauriwa akishafanya kazi hii yote iliyotangulia, yuko tayari — mara nyingi kwa mara ya kwanza — kupokea taarifa. Anajua anachokitafuta. Ana maswali, si malalamiko tu. Sasa taarifa ya mshauri inatua mahali pake.
9.2 What Information to Supply
9.2 Taarifa Gani ya Kutoa

The information the counselor supplies must be the information the counselee actually needs to execute the action plan, no more and no less. The temptation is to flood: to give the counselee every relevant scripture, every helpful book, every related principle. This buries the counselee. He cannot apply twenty things at once. The counselor selects. He gives the counselee one or two key scriptures that bear directly on the chosen action. He recommends one book, not five. He supplies the practical information the counselee genuinely lacks — how to find a good Christian attorney, how to access the church benevolence fund, how to reach the addiction recovery group that meets on Tuesday evenings, what a healthy budget framework looks like for a family of four. The counselor's question is always, "What does this person, with this chosen action, need to know that he does not now know?" That is the information he supplies. Everything else, however true and however valuable, is withheld for another session or another counselee.

Taarifa ambayo mshauri anaitoa lazima iwe taarifa ambayo mshauriwa kwa kweli anaihitaji ili kutekeleza mpango wa utekelezaji, si zaidi wala si pungufu. Kishawishi ni kufurika: kumpa mshauriwa kila andiko linalohusika, kila kitabu chenye msaada, kila kanuni inayohusiana. Hilo humzika mshauriwa. Hawezi kutumia mambo ishirini kwa wakati mmoja. Mshauri huchagua. Humpa mshauriwa andiko moja au mawili muhimu yanayogusa moja kwa moja tendo lililochaguliwa. Hupendekeza kitabu kimoja, si vitano. Hutoa taarifa ya kivitendo ambayo mshauriwa kwa kweli hana — jinsi ya kumpata mwanasheria Mkristo mzuri, jinsi ya kupata msaada kutoka mfuko wa huruma wa kanisa, jinsi ya kukifikia kikundi cha kupona kutoka kwa uraibu kinachokutana Jumanne jioni, jinsi mpangilio mzuri wa bajeti unavyoonekana kwa familia ya watu wanne. Swali la mshauri daima ni, "Mtu huyu, akiwa na tendo hili alilolichagua, anahitaji kujua nini ambacho sasa hakijui?" Hiyo ndiyo taarifa anayoitoa. Kila kitu kingine, hata kiwe kweli kiasi gani na cha thamani kiasi gani, huhifadhiwa kwa ajili ya kikao kingine au mshauriwa mwingine.
9.3 Scripture as Primary Information
9.3 Maandiko kama Taarifa ya Msingi

For the Christian counselor, the most important information is always scriptural. The Word of God is given for "doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: that the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works" (2 Tim 3:16–17). When the counselee is ready, the counselor opens the Bible with him and lets the counselee read for himself. He does not paraphrase from memory; he opens the text. Eyes on the page produce a different effect than ears hearing a quotation. The counselee sees that the Word he is being asked to obey is not the counselor's preference but the Lord's command. The counselor selects scriptures with care. He does not pile up passages. He chooses one or two that go straight to the counselee's situation. The husband considering reconciliation reads Ephesians 5. The grieving widow reads 2 Corinthians 1:3–5. The angry brother reads Matthew 5:23–24. The counselor reads with him, then asks, "What does this passage say to you in your situation?" Now Scripture is not abstract doctrine; it is information for the counselee's chosen path.

Kwa mshauri Mkristo, taarifa iliyo muhimu kuliko zote daima ni ya kimaandiko. Neno la Mungu limetolewa "kwa mafundisho, na kwa kuwaonya watu makosa yao, na kwa kuwaongoza, na kwa kuwaadibu katika haki; ili mtu wa Mungu awe kamili, amekamilishwa apate kutenda kila tendo jema" (2 Tim 3:16–17). Mshauriwa anapokuwa tayari, mshauri hufungua Biblia pamoja naye na kumwacha mshauriwa asome mwenyewe. Hafafanui kwa maneno yake kutoka kumbukumbu; hufungua andiko. Macho yakiwa juu ya ukurasa huleta matokeo tofauti na masikio yakisikia nukuu. Mshauriwa anaona kwamba Neno analoombwa kulitii si upendeleo wa mshauri bali ni amri ya Bwana. Mshauri huchagua maandiko kwa uangalifu. Halundiki vifungu. Huchagua kimoja au viwili vinavyokwenda moja kwa moja kwenye hali ya mshauriwa. Mume anayefikiria kupatana tena na mkewe anasoma Waefeso 5. Mjane mwenye huzuni anasoma 2 Wakorintho 1:3–5. Ndugu mwenye hasira anasoma Mathayo 5:23–24. Mshauri husoma pamoja naye, kisha anauliza, "Kifungu hiki kinakuambia nini katika hali yako?" Sasa Maandiko si fundisho la kinadharia; ni taarifa kwa ajili ya njia aliyoichagua mshauriwa.
9.4 Information Through Referral
9.4 Taarifa Kupitia Kumpeleka Mtu kwa Msaada Mwingine (Rufaa)

Sometimes the information the counselee needs is information the counselor does not have. The medical, legal, financial, or psychiatric specialist exists for exactly this reason. The pastoral counselor who recognizes the limit of his competence does not pretend; he refers. He gives the counselee the name of the Christian physician, the name of the lawyer who handles such cases with integrity, the address of the inpatient program for the substance abuser, the phone number of the marriage counselor whose specialty matches the need. Drakeford was emphatic that the willingness to refer is one of the marks of a mature counselor. The counselor who tries to be all things to all counselees ends up failing his counselees. The counselor who, in his own words, says, "This question is beyond my training, but I know who can help, and I will walk with you to that help" — that counselor has done his counselee a service. Step Nine includes referral as a legitimate and sometimes essential form of supplied information.

Wakati mwingine taarifa anayoihitaji mshauriwa ni taarifa ambayo mshauri hana. Mtaalamu wa tiba, wa sheria, wa fedha, au wa magonjwa ya akili yupo kwa sababu hiyo hasa. Mshauri wa kichungaji anayetambua kikomo cha uwezo wake hajifanyi; humpeleka mtu kwa msaada mwingine. Humpa mshauriwa jina la daktari Mkristo, jina la mwanasheria anayeshughulikia kesi za namna hiyo kwa uadilifu, anwani ya programu ya matibabu ya kulazwa kwa ajili ya mtu mwenye uraibu wa dawa za kulevya, namba ya simu ya mshauri wa ndoa ambaye utaalamu wake unalingana na hitaji. Drakeford alisisitiza kwa nguvu kwamba utayari wa kumpeleka mtu kwa msaada mwingine ni mojawapo ya alama za mshauri aliyekomaa. Mshauri anayejaribu kuwa kila kitu kwa washauriwa wote huishia kuwaangusha washauriwa wake. Mshauri ambaye, kwa maneno yake mwenyewe, anasema, "Swali hili liko nje ya mafunzo yangu, lakini namjua mtu anayeweza kusaidia, nami nitatembea pamoja nawe hadi kwenye msaada huo" — mshauri huyo amemtendea mshauriwa wake huduma. Hatua ya Tisa inajumuisha kumpeleka mtu kwa msaada mwingine kama namna halali, na wakati mwingine ya lazima kabisa, ya kutoa taarifa.
9.5 Information for Memory
9.5 Taarifa kwa Ajili ya Kukumbuka

Information given orally and not retained is information not given. The counselor at Step Nine should make written provision wherever possible. The key scriptures should be on a card or page the counselee carries home. The chosen action plan should be written. The contact information for the referral should be in writing in the counselee's hand before he leaves the office. The counselee, in the weeks ahead, will face moments of weakness, doubt, and forgetfulness; written information at those moments will steady him. Pastoral counseling that ends with the counselee leaving empty-handed has done less than it could. Pastoral counseling that ends with the counselee walking out the door carrying a small page on which the next step, the relevant scripture, and the next contact are clearly written has done a complete work. Step Nine, properly done, equips the counselee to continue without the counselor present.

Taarifa iliyotolewa kwa mdomo na isiyokumbukwa ni taarifa ambayo haikutolewa. Mshauri katika Hatua ya Tisa anapaswa kuandaa maandishi kila inapowezekana. Maandiko muhimu yanapaswa kuwa kwenye kadi au karatasi ambayo mshauriwa anaibeba kwenda nayo nyumbani. Mpango wa utekelezaji uliochaguliwa unapaswa kuandikwa. Taarifa za mawasiliano kwa ajili ya rufaa zinapaswa kuwa kwa maandishi mkononi mwa mshauriwa kabla hajaondoka ofisini. Mshauriwa, katika wiki zijazo, atakutana na nyakati za udhaifu, shaka, na kusahau; taarifa iliyoandikwa katika nyakati hizo itamtuliza na kumsimamisha imara. Ushauri wa kichungaji unaoishia mshauriwa akiondoka mikono mitupu umefanya kidogo kuliko ulivyoweza. Ushauri wa kichungaji unaoishia mshauriwa akitoka mlangoni akibeba karatasi ndogo ambayo juu yake hatua inayofuata, andiko linalohusika, na mtu wa kuwasiliana naye kwa hatua inayofuata vimeandikwa waziwazi, umefanya kazi kamili. Hatua ya Tisa, ikifanywa ipasavyo, humwandaa mshauriwa kuendelea bila mshauri kuwapo.
9.6 Encouragement That Bears Weight
9.6 Kutia Moyo Kunakoweza Kubeba Uzito

Step Nine's second task is encouragement, and most counselors do this badly. The default mode is generic affirmation — "You can do this." "I believe in you." "God is with you." These statements are not wrong, but they are weightless. Generic encouragement, repeated, becomes background noise. It cannot bear the weight of the actual difficulty the counselee faces in the actual hour of his temptation. Real encouragement is specific.

Kazi ya pili ya Hatua ya Tisa ni kutia moyo, na washauri wengi hufanya hivi vibaya. Njia ya kawaida ni maneno ya jumla ya kuthibitisha — "Unaweza kufanya hili." "Ninakuamini." "Mungu yuko pamoja nawe." Kauli hizi si mbaya, lakini hazina uzito. Kutia moyo kwa jumla, kukirudiwarudiwa, hugeuka kuwa kelele za nyuma. Hakuwezi kubeba uzito wa ugumu halisi anaokabiliana nao mshauriwa katika saa halisi ya kishawishi chake. Kutia moyo kwa kweli ni mahususi.

Specific encouragement names what the counselee has already shown himself capable of, and ties that capacity to the action ahead. "I have watched you, over these last three weeks, name things about your own failure that few men ever speak aloud. The man who can do that is not the man you were a year ago. When you go to your father on Saturday, you go as that man. You have already done the harder work." Now the counselee has been encouraged not in the abstract but on the basis of evidence he himself has produced. He knows it is true; he has heard himself say those things in this office. Encouragement of that kind sustains.

Kutia moyo kwa mahususi hutaja kile ambacho mshauriwa tayari amejionyesha kuwa anaweza kukifanya, na huunganisha uwezo huo na tendo lililo mbele yake. "Nimekutazama, katika wiki hizi tatu zilizopita, ukitaja mambo kuhusu kushindwa kwako mwenyewe ambayo wanaume wachache sana huwahi kuyasema kwa sauti. Mtu anayeweza kufanya hivyo si yule mtu uliyekuwa mwaka mmoja uliopita. Utakapokwenda kwa baba yako Jumamosi, unakwenda ukiwa mtu huyo. Tayari umefanya kazi iliyo ngumu zaidi." Sasa mshauriwa ametiwa moyo si kwa jumla bali kwa msingi wa ushahidi ambao yeye mwenyewe ameutoa. Anajua ni kweli; amejisikia mwenyewe akisema mambo hayo katika ofisi hii. Kutia moyo kwa namna hiyo humtegemeza.

Specific encouragement also anticipates the moment of difficulty. "When you stand at his door, your hand will hesitate. That is normal. When it hesitates, I want you to remember Psalm 27:1 — 'The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?' — and knock anyway. The hesitation is not a sign that you should turn back. It is the moment when the strength of the Lord comes in." This is encouragement that has imagined the actual circumstance and given the counselee specific scriptural and behavioral provision for it. Generic encouragement is a wish. Specific encouragement is a tool. The counselor's gift to the counselee in Step Nine is tools, not wishes.

Kutia moyo kwa mahususi pia hutarajia mapema wakati wa ugumu. "Utakaposimama mlangoni pake, mkono wako utasita. Hilo ni la kawaida. Unaposita, nataka ukumbuke Zaburi 27:1 — 'BWANA ni nuru yangu na wokovu wangu, nimwogope nani?' — na ubishe hodi hata hivyo. Kusita si ishara kwamba unapaswa kurudi nyuma. Ni wakati ambao nguvu za Bwana zinaingia." Huku ni kutia moyo ambako kumeiwazia hali halisi na kumpa mshauriwa maandalizi mahususi ya kimaandiko na ya kimatendo kwa ajili yake. Kutia moyo kwa jumla ni tamanio. Kutia moyo kwa mahususi ni chombo cha kazi. Zawadi ya mshauri kwa mshauriwa katika Hatua ya Tisa ni vyombo vya kazi, si matamanio.
9.7 The Spirit Alongside the Counselor
9.7 Roho Kando ya Mshauri

No Step Nine succeeds without the Holy Spirit. The counselor's information, however well prepared, and the counselor's encouragement, however specifically aimed, are means that the Spirit uses or sets aside according to His sovereign work. The counselor who has not prayed before the session, who has not asked the Spirit to make the right text come to mind at the right moment, who has not committed the counselee to the Spirit's keeping — that counselor has been carrying a weight he was never meant to carry alone. Step Nine is the moment in the model where this dependence becomes most visible.

Hakuna Hatua ya Tisa inayofanikiwa bila Roho Mtakatifu. Taarifa ya mshauri, hata iandaliwe vizuri kiasi gani, na kutia moyo kwa mshauri, hata kulengwe kwa umahususi kiasi gani, ni njia ambazo Roho huzitumia au huziweka kando kulingana na kazi yake ya enzi. Mshauri ambaye hakuomba kabla ya kikao, ambaye hakumwomba Roho alilete andiko sahihi akilini kwa wakati sahihi, ambaye hakumkabidhi mshauriwa katika ulinzi wa Roho — mshauri huyo amekuwa akibeba mzigo ambao hakukusudiwa kamwe kuubeba peke yake. Hatua ya Tisa ndiyo wakati katika mbinu hii ambapo utegemezi huu unaonekana waziwazi kuliko wakati mwingine wowote.

The Greek word for the Spirit Christ promised His disciples is paraklētos — Counselor, Comforter, the One called alongside. The pastoral counselor in Step Nine stands as a fellow-paraklete, a junior helper called alongside the senior Helper who is doing the actual work. This shapes the counselor's prayer life. He prays before the session that the Spirit would prepare the counselee. He prays during the session that the Spirit would supply the right word. He prays after the session that the Spirit would apply what was said, fill what was missing, correct what was wrong, and bring to remembrance what will be needed.

Neno la Kigiriki kwa ajili ya Roho ambaye Kristo aliwaahidi wanafunzi wake ni paraklētos — Mshauri, Mfariji, Yule aliyeitwa kuwa kando. Mshauri wa kichungaji katika Hatua ya Tisa anasimama kama paraklete mwenzake, msaidizi mdogo aliyeitwa kuwa kando ya Msaidizi mkuu ambaye ndiye anayefanya kazi halisi. Jambo hili hutengeneza maisha ya maombi ya mshauri. Huomba kabla ya kikao kwamba Roho amwandae mshauriwa. Huomba wakati wa kikao kwamba Roho alete neno sahihi. Huomba baada ya kikao kwamba Roho ayatumie yaliyosemwa, ajaze yaliyopungua, asahihishe yaliyokosewa, na alete kumbukumbu ya yale yatakayohitajika.

This dependence is also a discipline against pastoral grandiosity. The counselor whose counsel succeeds has not himself succeeded; the Spirit has worked. The counselor whose counsel seems to fail has not himself failed in any final sense; the Spirit may still complete what was begun, long after the counseling has closed. Pastoral counseling that succeeds against the Spirit's work is impossible; pastoral counseling that fails despite the Spirit's work is also impossible. The work belongs, in the end, to God. The counselor's faithfulness in Step Nine is to do his small part well, and to trust the larger Work to the One whose work it actually is.

Utegemezi huu pia ni nidhamu dhidi ya majivuno ya kichungaji. Mshauri ambaye ushauri wake unafanikiwa si yeye mwenyewe aliyefanikiwa; Roho amefanya kazi. Mshauri ambaye ushauri wake unaonekana kushindwa hajashindwa yeye mwenyewe kwa maana yoyote ya mwisho; Roho bado anaweza kukamilisha kile kilichoanzishwa, muda mrefu baada ya ushauri kufungwa. Ushauri wa kichungaji unaofanikiwa kinyume na kazi ya Roho hauwezekani; ushauri wa kichungaji unaoshindwa licha ya kazi ya Roho pia hauwezekani. Kazi ni ya Mungu, hatimaye. Uaminifu wa mshauri katika Hatua ya Tisa ni kufanya sehemu yake ndogo vizuri, na kuikabidhi Kazi iliyo kubwa zaidi kwa Yule ambaye kwa kweli kazi hiyo ni yake.
